title: Trump Onsite Power Push Meets AI Data Center Reality
content:
With data centers dominating industry and policy discussions, it was only a matter of time before President Donald Trump weighed in.
In an Oct. 21
Truth Social
post, Trump said new, large-scale data centers should generate their own electricity and return excess power to the local community or grid. He also suggested that developers make financial arrangements with host communities, including payments to residents:
“As the President of the United States, I have been watching Data Centers very closely, and have come to a very strong conclusion. New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data Centers are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid, and therefore there is electric price increase. In fact, there could be a substantial decrease. Other elements likewise! If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend.’ I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck. MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A. President DJT”
Related:
Could the Societal Value of Workloads Shape Data Center Policy?
The comments are likely to intensify debate across the sector. Many projects already under construction have secured grid connections, signed power purchase agreements (PPAs), or otherwise locked in their energy strategy. If Trump’s position were translated into formal policy, developers would face difficult questions about whether those plans would need to change.
Equipment availability would be another major challenge. Many of the components required for gas-fired, nuclear, and battery-backed onsite power systems are already in tight supply, with some turbine models effectively sold out through 2031.
That would present a serious challenge for data center designers, engineers, developers, and operators, said Patrick Hughes, senior vice president of strategy, technical, and industry affairs at the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA). Hughes was involved in developing the
AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework
,co-developed by NEMA,
the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE),
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL).
“It’s possible for a standalone AI data center to provide sufficient onsite power to fuel its own operations – whether it’s a combined-cycle plant or solar plus storage, we have the technology,” Hughes said. “But that doesn’t mean it’s feasible for a single AI data center – let alone the whole fleet of AI data centers – to supply 100% of their own power and operate reliably 24/7; that requires significant operational management and maintenance.”
Related:
Reliability Standards for AI Data Centers, Crypto Miners Move Closer to Adoption
Permitting timelines, fuel and equipment supply chains, interconnection rules, and community considerations vary widely by location, Hughes added. Those factors will shape what is practical at any given site. For many facilities, the most likely outcome may be a hybrid approach that combines onsite generation and storage with a grid connection.
Why AI Data Centers Can’t Easily Go Off-Grid
There are substantial technical and logistical barriers to any broad requirement that AI data centers supply all of their own power. AI training and inference facilities have power densities and load profiles that differ sharply from those of traditional data centers and from facilities that have historically relied on co-located generation and storage.
At the same time, the AI infrastructure buildout is grappling with enormous demand for electrical equipment and
skilled labor
across utilities, buildings, transportation, and industrial manufacturing. Whether or not developers are pushed toward a bring-your-own-power model, they are already competing with other sectors for turbines, switchgear, transformers, batteries, and specialized labor.
Related:
Permits, Not Power, Halt Google’s Finland Data Centers
Regardless of the onsite resource selected, the AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework offers technical standards and guiding principles for safety, resilience, and grid interaction. Data center designers, engineers, developers, and operators can use it to improve energy and water efficiency while supporting grid reliability and resilience through load flexibility and other grid-interactive operations.
Existing Power Deals and Renewable Commitments Complicate the Shift
A blanket onsite power requirement would also have to contend with existing clean-energy mandates, corporate sustainability goals, and regional differences in the availability of renewable resources. Many AI data centers already have agreements in place to draw power from solar and wind projects.
Stargate site in Abilene, Texas
, offers one example. The project is already using natural gas, fuel cells, and gas engines during the construction phase and to power the first data centers now operating there. Developers are also planning to incorporate solar and wind, and the area’s solar generation potential was one of the reasons the location was selected. Abilene offers strong irradiance, abundant undeveloped land, and no major urban loads nearby. With developers scrambling to find 1.2 GW once all phases are complete, wind and solar are expected to supplement other power sources.
Applied Digital’s AI data center project in North Dakota provides another example. The company has arranged for 400 MW of stranded wind power to serve its Ellendale campus and continues to emphasize renewables in its energy strategy. It also recently signed a deal with data center developer
to use output from Soluna’s 150 MW Briscoe wind farm for a new data center in Texas.
"We have said for a long time that the constraint in AI is energy access, not chips," Soluna CEO John Belizaire said in a
press release
. "We built Soluna to bring load to the generation, so the power would be ready when the demand arrived."
A Hybrid Power Model May Be the Most Practical Path
If policymakers decide to pursue Trump’s idea, they will likely need to translate it into a more flexible and workable policy. The AI Data Center Energy Performance Framework accounts for that kind of flexibility, avoiding a rigid preference for either bring-your-own-power or grid power. Its guidance on
grid-interactive design
onsite energy, and thermal efficiency
addresses the role of onsite and offsite renewables, as well as intelligent energy storage, in reducing strain on the grid.
“There’s no single answer, as the right onsite generation strategy will inevitably depend on each facility’s load, site, and regulatory landscape,” Hughes said.

title: AGL seeks approval for 2 GWh battery in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Energy generating and retailing major AGL Energy is seeking approvals under the Australian federal government’s Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (EPBC) Act for a 500 MW/2,000 MWh battery to be built in central Queensland. The proposed Mount Britton battery project comprises a standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) with 500 MW of power capacity and four hours of total usable storage. The BESS, planned for a 27-hectare site near the town of Nebo about 75 km southwest of Mackay, would connect to Powerlink’s 275 kV transmission network at the existing Nebo substation. In referral documents, AGL said the project could be delivered in multiple construction phases of up to 250 MW each, or as a single 500 MW phase. The Sydney-based energy utility said it expects the BESS to become a significant addition to central Queensland’s energy infrastructure. “When constructed, the project will provide local electricity network resilience through stabilisation services such as frequency and voltage control, and manage energy peak demand periods as the grid transitions to renewable energy,” it said. The Mount Britton BESS project forms part of AGL’s ongoing transition away from coal-fired power generation to a majority of backed-up renewables. “With the changing nature of electricity demand across Australia, there’s an increasing need for more flexible generation and generation from a diverse range of sources and in a range of locations,” the energy utility said, adding that “battery storage can start at short notice and ramp up and down quickly, making them an excellent complement to higher levels of variable renewable generation such as wind and solar.” AGL has more than 2 GW of renewable projects in its pipeline and said it is on track to meet its ambition to add 12 GW of new renewable and firming capacity by the end of 2035 with more than 1.2 GW of grid-scale batteries in operation or under construction. The energy major already owns and operates the 500 MW/1,000 MWh Liddell and the 50 MW/50 MWh Broken Hill batteries in New South Wales, and the 250 MW/250 MWh Torrens Island BESS in South Australia. It is also constructing the 500 MW/2,000 MWh Tomago battery on the New South Wales Central Coast. Its Queensland battery projects include the 125 MW/500 MWh Abermain BESS in the state’s southeast, the 200 MW Aramara battery project, and the 500 MW/2,000 MWh Tuckeroo BESS in the Western Downs region. Of AGL’s current 23 projects under development, 14 are standalone batteries. AGL closed its Liddell coal power station in NSW in 2023 and is due to close Bayswater nearby at the end of 2033, and Loy Yang A in Victoria in 2035. title: Econergy buys up 106 MW of operational UK battery storage capacity - Energy Storage
content: Independent power producer Econergy has acquired a portfolio of four operational battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in the UK, totaling 106 MW. Under the agreement, disclosed in a filing to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE), Econergy said it has acquired 100% of the shares in the holding company that owns the four assets, giving it full ownership and control of the portfolio. The company said the projects are expected to generate around £4.7 million in EBITDA in 2027 before planned augmentation works. The four standalone BESS facilities, located in England, currently have a one-hour duration (106 MWh total), with Econergy evaluating plans to augment the systems to three-hour duration (~318 MWh). Econergy didn’t name the seller, and public registry transfer filings have not been made to Companies House yet. Econergy said the longer duration would allow the assets to capture additional value by storing more energy and dispatching it over a longer period, thus providing greater flexibility to respond to changing market conditions by shifting electricity to times of stronger demand. The acquisition increases Econergy’s operational UK BESS capacity from 90 MW to 196 MW, as the company expands from two to six assets that are connected to the grid. Econergy’s existing UK operational assets include the 50 MW / 100 MWh Swangate BESS in West Melton , Yorkshire, England, which entered operation in 2024, and the 40 MW / 120 MWh Dalmarnock project in Glasgow, Scotland, which connected to the grid in October 2026. “We’re pleased to be purchasing these four projects, which represent a business opportunity with clear upside,” said Eyal Podhorzer, CEO and director of Econergy. “The addition of 106 MW of operational storage capacity and the potential to augment the assets to three-hour duration gives us a pathway to build on the portfolio and develop its longer-term value. Alongside our existing assets, and those in development, these projects strengthen our foothold in the UK and a growing platform for further expansion.” The company said it has a 1.6 GW UK energy storage development pipeline. Across Europe, its BESS portfolio totals 5.9 GW, with 3.3 GW expected to be connected to the grid, under construction or pre-construction by 2028. title: Italy authorizes another 480 MW of battery storage - Energy Storage
content: Italy’s Ministry of Environment and Energy Security (MASE) issued two further single authorizations for battery energy storage system (BESS) projects totaling 480 MW on Nov. 2, following nearly 7 GW of approvals over the previous two months. The projects are a 280 MW facility planned by Miura Storage Srl in Tuscany, in the province of Viterbo, and the 200 MW Bess Castegnero project, developed by BESS Pieve Srl in Castegnero Nanto, in the province of Vicenza. Benny Energia, the Rome-based owner of BESS Pieve, plans to build the 200 MW project with 160 battery containers and 160 power conversion systems. Construction is expected to take around 30 months. The energy storage developer told pv magazine Italia that it has a BESS project pipeline of around 2.3 GW. This includes 1.5 GW of projects preparing for construction and intended to participate in Italy’s capacity market and MACSE storage procurement scheme, around 700 MW awaiting authorization, and a 200 MW project in Udine that has been operating for nearly three years. The other project authorized by MASE is Miura Storage’s 280 MW facility in Tuscania. It will comprise 327 battery containers, with construction expected to take five months. title: Malaysia’s data center industry gets 500 MW solar, 1 GWh battery storage boost - Energy Storage
content: A 500 MWac solar photovoltaic project coupled with a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) is set to be developed on approximately 1,300 acres of land in Bahau, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. The massive solar-plus-storage project will be developed by IOI Corporation Berhad (IOI), one of Malaysia’s leading integrated palm oil producers, in partnership with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), the country’s largest electricity utility, and a consortium of unspecified small and medium-sized enterprises. “The project will be supported by TNB’s long-term renewable energy offtake agreement with DayOne Data Centres Limited, a leading global digital infrastructure platform headquartered in Singapore,” IOI said in a statement. “Under the agreement, DayOne is expected to procure up to 500MWac of renewable energy over a 21-year period to support its data centre operations in Malaysia, as announced by the parties on 11 June 2025.” The project marks IOI’s first large-scale renewable energy investment under Malaysia’s Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), which allows corporate electricity consumers to procure renewable power directly from independent developers through the national grid. The scheme aims to encourage private investment in renewable energy infrastructure while supporting the decarbonization of energy-intensive industries. Malaysia is expanding its utility-scale solar and energy storage capacity to meet rising electricity demand from data centers. In August 2025, clean energy company Gentari and engineering group Gamuda unveiled plans to jointly develop 1.5 GW of solar capacity , alongside battery storage, to supply hyperscale data centers under CRESS. The rapid growth of Malaysia’s data center industry has also raised concerns about electricity supply, grid capacity and water availability. A March 2026 analysis highlighted the challenges of meeting rising electricity demand while maintaining grid stability and ensuring sufficient dispatchable generation. Uncertainty over grid access charges has also been identified as a key factor affecting the commercial viability of corporate renewable energy projects. In September 2026, Malaysia revised the CRESS framework to improve project bankability and stimulate investment. The changes introduced a fixed system access charge of MYR 0.14 ($0.03)/kWh for qualifying firm renewable electricity supply projects and a minimum 10-year contract term between developers and corporate consumers. Projects must begin commercial operations by the end of 2028 to qualify for the reduced charge. At the time, 11 renewable energy developers and eight corporate consumers had registered projects totaling approximately 3.15 GW under the scheme. title: Slovak utility tenders battery for largest pumped hydro plant - Energy Storage
content: Slovenské elektrárne has launched a tender to build a battery energy storage system at Čierny Váh, Slovakia’s largest pumped storage hydropower plant. The utility published the tender last week, with bids due by Nov. 27. It covers battery supply, engineering, substation work, construction, testing and training. The Slovak power producer, which is controlled by Czech energy group EPH, has not disclosed a contract value or award criteria. The company’s project page describes a battery of up to 120 MW/480 MWh, but Slovak media reports indicate that the final parameters could still change. That is larger than the up to 80 MW/160 MWh that the company and the European Union have previously described. Slovak daily Denník SME has reported that the batteries will be housed in containers and that the project includes a substation expansion and a new transformer. The battery is part of a wider upgrade of the 735 MW plant. Slovenské elektrárne has signed contracts with Voith Hydro and GE Vernova to convert two of its turbine-generators to variable-speed operation. It has reportedly said that that the investment exceeds €200 million ($223.9 million) and is due for completion in 2031. The company said the upgrade will widen the plant’s balancing range to between -712 MW and +790 MW. It said the hybrid site will be able to provide primary, secondary and tertiary balancing, with combined efficiency of up to 77%. The European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) awarded a €62.63 million grant under the Connecting Europe Facility for the variable-speed works, which began in July. CINEA said the battery is not part of the grant-funded phase, but both are part of the same EU Project of Common Interest. Slovenské elektrárne commissioned a 36 MW/72 MWh battery at the site of its former Nováky coal plant in July, which provides frequency containment reserve. The Bratislava-based company is 66% owned by Slovak Power Holding, a unit of Czech energy group EPH, and 34% by the Slovak state. Other European utilities are also pairing batteries with pumped hydro. Enel, for example, has announced plans to retrofit battery storage at a century-old pumped hydro plant in Italy. Iberdrola, meanwhile, has switched on a pumped hydro-battery project in Spain , and a hybrid pumped hydro-BESS project in Finland has doubled its planned battery capacity. title: Kia EV7 revealed as an upcoming midsize electric SUV
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 4 2026 - 7:15 am PT
Kia is crushing it with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from entry-level SUVs to the three-row EV9 and PV5 van. A leaked document revealed that
plans to add the EV7, a new midsize electric SUV, to fill the gap between the EV6 and the three-row EV9.
Kia EV7 is coming as a new midsize electric SUV
With 291,219 vehicles
sold last month
, up 10.3% from October 2025, Kia posted its eighth consecutive month of year-over-year sales growth.
Kia said it plans to build on the momentum by focusing on electrified vehicles in key markets, including hybrids in the US and fully electric vehicles in Europe.
After launching the EV2 earlier this year, Kia now offers one of the most complete EV lineups, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van.
According to a recently leaked document, a new midsize electric SUV will join the lineup.
KoreanCarBlog
uncovered an internal document from Kia’s Employment Stability Committee that reveals the company’s upcoming production plans.
The report claims “production of mid-range electric SUV ‘EV7’ to proceed” at Kia’s Gwangju factory in South Korea.
Although no other details were revealed, the EV7 will be a midsize electric SUV, slotted between the EV6 and three-row EV9.
During its

title: Tesla accused of selling FSD to Korean owners who can't legally use it
content:
Tesla Autopilot
Fred Lambert
| Nov 4 2026 - 6:27 am PT
A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year.
Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD.
Most Teslas in Korea can’t run FSD
It all comes down to where the car was built. The Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck come from US factories and enter Korea under the KORUS free trade agreement, which recognizes US safety standards. Those are the only Teslas that got “FSD (Supervised)” when Tesla switched it on in Korea late last year.
The problem is that those don’t represent the vast majority of Tesla vehicles sold in Korea.
The Model 3 and Model Y sold in Korea come from Giga Shanghai. There’s no equivalent deal with China, so those cars need Korean approval that FSD doesn’t have.
And that’s most of the fleet. Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk told lawmakers last month that FSD works on about 20% of Teslas registered in the country. Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-built vehicles in Korea since 2023, per data it handed to the National Assembly, and sales of those China-made cars grew more than fivefold between 2023 and 2025.
Seo’s figure also clears up the conflicting eligibility numbers we flagged when
Korean police booked 80 Tesla drivers for using illegal FSD unlock devices
last month. A lawmaker’s data from May put it at 2.4%, while a data firm counted 20.7% in August. Tesla’s own testimony matches the higher one.
What the complaint alleges
For years, Tesla charged Korean buyers a one-time 9.043 million won (about $6,726) for FSD. It moved to a 150,000 won ($112) monthly subscription in August.
The complaint points to Tesla’s “coming soon” promotion last year and a demo video shot on Korean roads. Neither made it clear that FSD would only work on a small slice of the cars Tesla was selling. The group says Tesla knew that and kept pitching the package to every buyer anyway.
“Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day,” said Choi Young-suk, who heads automotive issues at the group.
It wants the KFTC to temporarily order Tesla to stop marketing FSD for ineligible cars. It’s also asking for fines and for the case to be sent to state investigators.
The KFTC is already looking at this. An official told Reuters the agency opened a probe into Tesla’s FSD advertising earlier this year and has received written responses from the company. Tesla didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.
Tesla only applied for approval last month
Tesla has collected FSD money from buyers of China-made cars in Korea for more than three years. But at an October 8 parliamentary hearing, Seo testified that Tesla had never formally asked the transport ministry to test FSD. Tesla filed for certification about two weeks later.
Approval won’t be a rubber stamp either. The ministry told a lawmaker that FSD doesn’t comply with local safety rules, including the requirement that drivers keep their hands on the wheel. Current FSD versions let drivers go hands-free as long as the cabin camera sees them watching the road.
None of this slowed sales. Tesla passed BMW this year to become Korea’s top imported car brand.
So far, owners haven’t had much luck in court. Last month, a Seoul court dismissed a lawsuit from Tesla owners seeking FSD refunds, with the judge pointing to Korean regulations, not Tesla, as the reason more features never launched.

title: What does a blue Texas sweep mean for Elon Musk, Tesla & SpaceX?
content:
Elon Musk
Jameson Dow
| Nov 4 2026 - 6:00 am PT
historic election defeat
in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies.
The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.
Perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning
statewide contest. Republicans maintained some state legislative power and won the State Senate, but as of this writing Democrats are currently ahead in the count for the State House.
Despite huge spending, Democrats won almost everything
The highest profile contest was for Texas Senate, where James Talarico won by a 55-43 margin. This race set the record for the most expensive Senate race in the nation’s history, with
over half a billion dollars spent
on this one seat alone.
About half of the total money spent on the race came courtesy of republican PACs, a method by which companies and the ultra-wealthy can launder money into bribes to buy elections. And most of the PAC money in the race came from one man, Elon Musk, who
spent $212 million
to support the enormously unpopular and
scandal-ridden
outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton
That’s nearly half of the $474 million dollars that Musk put into this election cycle, suggesting that he saw this race of particular importance. And yet, his candidate lost miserably.
But the rout did not stop with Paxton. Paxton’s old job as AG is now going to be filled by Democrat Nathan Johnson. And Greg Abbott, the outgoing Governor, was defeated by Gina Hinojosa. Even the less high-profile races for court seats were swept by Democrats – three seats on the 15th Court of Appeals and four seats on the Texas Supreme Court.
And those results, even beyond the big-spending Senate race, could all matter quite a lot to Elon Musk.
Republicans rolled out the red carpet for Musk in Texas
In 2021, Musk announced that Tesla would
move its headquarters to Texas
, after Musk got in a spat with California government because he didn’t want to follow COVID restrictions for worker safety.
But the move wasn’t only about COVID restrictions – it was also about Musk’s vision of having more control over the business environment. And, by making allies with Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott, he has had quite a bit of control in Texas.
The two have rolled out the red carpet for Musk, giving him carte blanche in his adopted state.
Autonomous vehicle regulations have been changed, allowing
driverless Robotaxis to operate
where other states with more advanced regulations and transparency requirements would not. And
many other laws
benefitting Tesla and SpaceX have been passed. Paxton even
sued Sam Altman
, Musk’s chief AI rival, just weeks ago.
Perhaps more notably for Musk personally, Texas has promised to allow Musk to get away with more
financial shenanigans
than states with more established business regulations might.
With Tesla both headquartered and
incorporated
in Texas, it can now use special “
business courts
” instituted by Abbott at Musk’s own urging. If cases from these courts are appealed, they go to the 15th Court of Appeals, a court created by Abbott and filled with 3 hand-picked judges, intended to reduce the chance that a Democratic district court (say, one in Austin, whereTesla is headquartered) gets final say on any issue.
Several specific seats overseeing Musk went blue
But, the 15th Court of Appeals just had elections last night – and its three seats were flipped to Democratic control.
The 15th Court of Appeals also, just
last week
stopped an inquiry
into thousands of pages of emails between Abbott and Musk. The emails had been
released
, but are heavily redacted, with Abbott referring to the redacted portions as having “
intimate
” information in them.
And who made that request for inquiry into the emails? Gina Hinojosa, a name you might recognize, as she is the next Governor of Texas, as of last night.
As of yet, those emails have not all been released, so we don’t actually know exactly how much influence Musk was able to exercise over the state’s outgoing Governor. But given the changes we know about, the money Musk spent in Texas, and the thousands of pages of emails that have been redacted, it seems likely that there is something more to be found in them.
What does this mean for Musk’s companies?
So what does this all mean for Tesla, our main area of coverage here at
Electrek
On a Texas state level, probably not all that much. There’s no reason that Democrats in the state would interfere with Tesla’s production of electric vehicles – in fact, they’d probably encourage it more than republicans do. Talarico has stated that he supports Tesla – it is a large employer in the state, after all.
And certainly, the national wins by Democrats could be a boon for EVs, and for
climate action
, given how hostile republicans have been to them (and Musk has been the
single largest supporter
of that hostility towards EVs, which has
cost Tesla billions
The same likely goes for SpaceX – perhaps a blue Texas will be more restrictive of the company’s improper usage of
protected habitats
building of data centers
whatever the hell is going on on twitter
. But the core businesses of space launches and Starlink don’t seem likely to go anywhere.
What does it mean for Musk himself?
For Elon Musk, though, things could be different. Given his “intimate” relationship with Abbott, the extreme amounts of money he spent on Paxton, and the highly personal nature of his
truly ridiculous attacks
against Talarico, it seems unlikely that he will have a similar level of allyship with Texas government actors as he did in prior years. Talarico’s main anti-corruption message was seemingly aimed straight at Musk’s attempts to buy elections, after all.
And given his high levels of spending on a party that is outright hostile electric vehicles, it seems clear that his
personal
fortunes are far more important to him than the well-being of his companies.
This is all important to note, because Musk has been working towards a scheme to merge SpaceX and Tesla, a deal which would likely be a detriment to
both companies and all of their shareholders
. Musk wants the deal so he can
exercise more control over, and extract more personal wealth from, the combined entity.
But that scheme could rely on a favorable legal environment in Texas courts, an environment that just got less favorable.
And, given Musk’s penchant for childish lashings-out anytime he deems people insufficiently obsequious to his imagined greatness, could we see another situation where Musk encounters the tiniest amount of pushback from state government and then picks up his toys and leaves, as he already did in both California and Delaware? Time will have to tell. Keep your popcorn buckets primed and ready.

content:

keep up with emerging technologies
such as AI,
cloud computing
, and sustainable infrastructure, and learn how they can be applied in practice, the
IEEE Computer Society
Central Indiana Chapter
recently launched its Tech Talk Series.
The live webinar series connects IEEE members, undergrad and graduate students, and engineering professionals from
IEEE Region 4
with industry practitioners. The monthly sessions have covered
AI governance
and security, agentic systems, and related topics. The sessions featured speakers from
, software company
cybersecurity
Upcoming sessions and registration details are available on the
IEEE Region 4 virtual events calendar
Technical discussions grounded in engineering
Rather than presenting on
emerging technologies
only at a conceptual level, speakers discussed the design decisions behind specific tools and systems, how the systems are structured, and implementation challenges. They also shared lessons learned from using the tools in their daily work.
Sessions also include technical walkthroughs and practical examples.
The live format allows attendees to discuss and compare their approaches when evaluating and implementing new technologies with those used by other organizations.
Extending access through a virtual format
The organizers chose to make the series virtual so that chapter members and other attendees could participate in technical discussions with engineers from major technology companies and eliminate the need to travel.
For young professionals, the sessions connect what they’ve learned in a classroom with the realities of the workplace.
Technical programs such as the Tech Talk Series give professionals and students access to expertise, help create connections across career levels, and make important engineering discussions available to a broader community.
Attendees learn how practitioners approach projects such as system architecture, reliability, security, governance, and product delivery. For experienced professionals, the talks offer a forum to examine new ways of designing, securing, and operating software systems, and compare technical approaches. Gajendra Babu Thokala

The IEEE senior member explained how teams can move beyond adding isolated AI features to applications and instead build governed AI-agent systems that use real-time business data to complete multistep business workflows.

Sandeep Shivam

Those two sessions illustrate the series’ purpose: helping participants understand what a technology can do and what is required to use it responsibly.

Future sessions are being planned on areas including enterprise AI,

Upcoming sessions are expected to cover cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, and the responsible development of AI systems.

title: Internet Critics Mocked The Ferrari Luce EV—Now It’s Completely Sold Out For 2027
content:
Defying Online Backlash, The Ferrari Luce EV Is Already Sold Out Through 2027
Purists slammed the electric Ferrari’s design at launch, but its wealthy buyers just bought out the entire 2027 allocation.
- The Ferrari Luce, which costs over half a million dollars, has no dearth of buyers.
- It faced backlash for its radical design, but demand is clearly no issue.
- The company's CEO said buyers were "better understanding" the EV after seeing it in person.
Ferrari's first all-electric model is already sold out for 2027, the automaker said during its third-quarter earnings call Tuesday. The Luce starts at an eye-watering $560,800 in the U.S., but neither its price nor its controversial design appears to be putting off Ferrari's deep-pocketed clientele.
“The Luce that we plan to sell next year basically are all allocated,” Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna said in the earnings call. He added that customers placing an order now would have to wait a year to take delivery. Ferrari didn't disclose how many units it plans to sell or provide a regional breakdown of its orders.
Gallery: Ferrari Luce (2026)
Designed through a collaboration with former Apple design chief Jony Ive's LoveFrom, the first electric Prancing Horse looks nothing like the Ferraris we're used to seeing. It trades the brand's signature aggressive, low-slung proportions for a higher-riding silhouette with an industrial-design aesthetic. The Luce is also Ferrari's first-ever five-seat car. The radical departure hasn't gone down particularly well with critics, many of whom have questioned whether the design looks like a Ferrari at all.
Ferrari isn't alone in taking a more unconventional approach to EV design. Jaguar's new Type 01 and the all-electric Mercedes-AMG GT have also sparked plenty of debate. Key rival Lamborghini, meanwhile, has scrapped plans for its first-ever EV, opting to stick with hybrids and gas models for now.
Vigna, however, said buyers were better understanding the Luce after seeing it in person and getting behind the wheel. “We see when and how the perception changes when the people drive the car,” he said.
Early media reviews appear to support that argument. A handful of outlets have already had the opportunity to drive the Luce, and the initial impressions have been overwhelmingly positive. MotorTrend, for instance, described its driving dynamics as “beguilingly natural in its responses, fluid and concise in its change of direction, and beautifully balanced through all phases of a corner.”
The Luce is a beast on paper. It's equipped with quad motors—one at each wheel—for a total of 1,035 horsepower and 730 pound-feet of torque. That's enough to rocket the Luce to 62 mph in 2.5 seconds, Ferrari says. The EV also has rear-wheel steering and a suspension setup derived from the F80 supercar. Steering wheel-mounted paddles let the driver jack up torque or regenerative braking, which is supposed to make the car more engaging to drive.
The EV-specific specs are less impressive for a half-million-dollar car. The Luce's 112-kilowatt-hour battery uses SK On pouch cells and provides 530 kilometers (329 miles) of range on Europe's WLTP cycle. That should translate to somewhere under 300 miles when it gets an EPA rating. Peak charging power lands at 350 kilowatts, which is plenty strong in objective terms but falls short of some of the fastest-charging EVs. But then again, you don't buy a $560,000 Luce because you're looking for a great, practical electric car.
And if there were any doubts about how much wealthy collectors are willing to pay for Ferrari's first EV, consider what happened in August. The first production Luce, dubbed “Chassis 0,” fetched a staggering $40 million at auction, making it the most expensive new car ever sold at auction.

title: Mercedes Wants To Rethink EV Batteries With This Clever New Technology
content:
Mercedes Wants To Rethink EV Batteries With This Clever New Technology
Instead of charging the battery as a whole unit, micro-converters can charge or discharge each cell individually.
- Mercedes-Benz is working on a new technology that could change how future EV batteries work.
- The Power Converter can control individual cells or cell groups, potentially prolonging the battery pack’s life.
- It also enables the use of different cell chemistries and voltages inside the same pack.
Mercedes-Benz wants to flip the script on how electric car high-voltage batteries work. Its new Power Converter, which is still in the development stage, can control the charge and discharge of individual cells inside the battery, which is a big change from how the vast majority of EV batteries work today.
For decades, traction batteries have had thousands of individual cells, which are arranged into cell groups or modules. The car’s brain can monitor the voltage of each cell or module, but when it comes to charging or discharging, everything gets the same treatment. Does the electric motor require 100 kilowatts? The whole pack delivers 100 kW. Charging at 150 kW? All the cells get treated equally.
Mercedes-Benz Power Converter
With Mercedes’ new technology, however, each cell inside the pack can not only be monitored, but also controlled by a programmable micro-converter. In theory, the approach has a lot of advantages, including prolonging a car’s battery life, using different cell chemistries inside the same pack, and removing bulky power electronics that handle AC and DC conversion.
Let’s look at the longevity aspect first. When an EV battery fails, it’s usually because one or more cells inside the pack can no longer sustain the same voltage as their neighbors. The car throws a scary error message on the screen, and the dealer or service center will recommend replacing the entire battery, which costs a lot of money if the warranty has run out.
With Mercedes-Benz’s new approach, if a cell can no longer sustain the required voltage, it can be simply disabled by its micro-converter. Sure, the battery capacity goes down a smidge, but the car will still work as before.
No more bulky components
The technology also enables a more modular approach to battery use. For instance, if a large-capacity battery isn’t used at full potential most of the time—say the owner drives only 50 miles daily—the car’s brain can put part of the pack in standby mode, keeping the cells at the right level for preservation. Then, when a long-distance road trip is being planned, the computer can unlock the full capacity.
Bidirectional charging is baked into the Power Converter. This means that AC and DC conversion, as well as bidirectional charging, are handled directly by the micro-converters, enabling finer control over how the battery is used.
Mercedes-Benz said that the new technology has the potential to boost the driving range and efficiency of future plug-in models, though there is one big asterisk that the company conveniently left out. With thousands of micro-converters sealed inside a battery pack, it inevitably means that there are thousands of components that can fail. If done right, though, it can bring a new level of modularity and fine-tuning to EV batteries.

title: Nearly 1 In 3 Hyundais Sold In October Was A Hybrid As High Gas Prices Push Buyers To Pivot
content:
Nearly 1 In 3 Hyundais Sold In October Was A Hybrid As High Gas Prices Push Buyers To Pivot
Hyundai’s hybrid mix hit a record 29% last month, while Kia’s affordable EV3 made a strong U.S. debut.
- Hybrids made up a record 29% of Hyundai's U.S. sales in October 2026 amid stubbornly high gas prices.
- The sub-$32,000 Kia EV3 is off to a strong start, already outselling the larger EV6 crossover.
- EV and hybrid sales across both Korean automakers rebounded after a weaker fall 2025.
A whopping 29% of Hyundai’s total October sales volume in the U.S. were hybrids, the automaker said Tuesday. That’s the highest mix ever for gas-electric powertrains for the Korean automaker, thanks to buyers seeking more fuel efficient cars due to gas prices that have remained stubbornly high since the start of the U.S. war in Iran.
Hyundai doesn't break out hybrid sales in its monthly reports, instead bundling them together under individual model names. But it did say that hybrid versions of the Santa Fe and Palisade set new October sales records. Meanwhile, sales of the all-electric Ioniq 5 bounced back, climbing 21% year over year to 1,981 units.
Hyundai sold 73,452 vehicles in October, a 5% increase over the same month last year. Its year-to-date sales now stand at 770,916 units, up 3% from 2025.
Sister brand Kia also reported record overall and electrified vehicle sales. It sold 80,008 vehicles last month, bringing its year-to-date total to 747,394 units, not far behind Hyundai.
Kia's hybrid sales jumped 114% year over year, helped by strong demand for hybrid versions of the popular Sportage and Sorento SUVs and the Carnival minivan. But the more interesting news is the recovery in Kia's EV sales, which have struggled for several quarters.
Sales of the three-row EV9 surged 111% to 1,406 units, while EV6 sales climbed 58% to 803 units. Kia also sold 976 units of the more affordable EV3, whose production and deliveries are still ramping up following its recent U.S. launch.
There's a caveat to those EV growth figures, though. The Ioniq 5, EV6, and EV9 were all coming off a particularly weak October 2025, when sales cratered following the expiration of the federal EV tax credit a month earlier.
The months leading up to the September 2025 deadline saw buyers rush to claim the incentive, pulling demand forward and causing subsequent sales to decline. The broader EV market has been gradually recovering since, with the third quarter marking its strongest performance since then.
The EV3, meanwhile, could give Kia's electric lineup another shot in the arm. Starting at $31,385 including destination, it's among the cheapest EVs on sale in the U.S., alongside the Nissan Leaf and Chevrolet Bolt. We recently reviewed the small electric crossover and think it offers really good value.
Hyundai could also see another boost to its EV business in the coming months. The automaker is preparing to supply Waymo with tens of thousands of Ioniq 5-based robotaxis, Hyundai CEO José Muñoz said in September. That could be a new source of demand for its electric crossover, beyond individual consumers.

title: Renault’s Latest EV Was Designed For The Army’s Toughest Missions
content:
Renault’s Latest EV Was Designed For The Army’s Toughest Missions
The Forefront Concept is completely silent, making it an ideal choice for high-risk, hard-to-reach areas.
- France’s Renault Group has developed a remotely operated electric vehicle for military use.
- The Forefront Concept uses proven automotive components to keep costs down.
- It features dual-motor all-wheel drive, four-wheel steering, and roughly 250 miles of range.
Renault Group has developed an all-electric, all-wheel-drive modular electric vehicle for military operations. Dubbed the Forefront Concept, it uses proven automotive components to keep costs down and boost production times.
The electric field vehicle was designed for both defense and civilian applications, and can be remotely operated by a human or sent into high-risk, hard-to-reach areas on its own, using its autonomous driving capabilities.
Renault Group built the vehicle, while John Cockerill designed the EV’s remote-operation and autonomy functions. The defense company listened to input from the French armed forces, which will use the Forefront Concept in several exercises and trials in the coming weeks to put it through its paces. After the trials, Renault will further refine the concept based on operational feedback.
Powered by two electric motors, the cab-less field machine has four-wheel steering and can travel in complete silence in some of the harshest terrain. The French automaker said the projected range is roughly 250 miles (400 kilometers) on a full charge, but an add-on range extender can further extend the driving distance. That said, Renault didn’t say how much energy the on-board battery or range extender can store.
With a 2,200-pound (1-tonne) payload, the dual-motor buggy can be used for logistics support, anti-drone operations, fire support, and evacuation. In highly disputed areas, sending in a vehicle that doesn’t have a human behind a steering wheel means fewer potential casualties. At the same time, the Forefront Concept can be used by companies that need a safe way to access dangerous sites.
Gallery: Renault Group and John Cockerill Forefrunt Concept
Renault Group said the remotely-operated EV was designed to be quickly put into production at competitive costs. There’s no price yet, but if there’s enough interest, we might see the boxy R/C car for adults become a reality sooner rather than later.
As the world’s battlefields continue to transform into places where machines do the heavy lifting while being controlled from hundreds of miles away by human operators, vehicles like Renault’s Forefront will become increasingly ubiquitous.
Renault Group isn’t alone in this game
Ukrainian companies have churned out thousands of remotely controlled robots in the fight against Russia. The models range from pint-sized mini-tanks to big drones that can airlift wounded soldiers.
Over in the United States, the Army has recently awarded an 18-month contract to American Rheinmetall to develop and deliver the next generation of uncrewed ground vehicles (UGV). The cab-less prototype is based on Harbinger’s extended-range EV platform, which uses a gas engine as a generator for an all-electric powertrain.
With a full tank of gas and a full battery, the military-grade plug-in hybrid can deliver over 500 miles of range, with the big benefit being its ability to shut off the gas engine for silent operations. Compared to Renault’s new concept, the Harbinger-based UGV platform can accommodate larger and heavier payloads of up to 18,000 lbs.

title: This Startup Is Turning Used E-Bike Batteries Into Affordable Energy Storage
content:
Why throw away old e-bike and e-scooter batteries when they can be repurposed? Best of all, they don’t even need to be dismantled.
Photo by:
KBO Bike
9:15am ET
Used batteries from e-bikes and e-scooters have been integrated into an industrial energy storage system.
German startup EDENenergy used over 100 second-life e-scooter batteries for a 70 kWh ESS.
In the future, the tiny startup’s system will be able to accommodate multiple types of batteries in the same enclosure.
Millions of
e-bike and e-scooter
batteries are thrown away every year, even though they might still have life in them. Now, a German startup is trying to reduce battery waste by integrating used batteries from e-mobility vehicles into energy storage systems.
EDENenergy, which has just three part-time staff members in addition to its three founders, has shipped its first commercial product, a 70-kilowatt-hour battery system that uses no fewer than 112 second-life e-scooter batteries.
EDENenergy's first commercial energy storage system uses 112 repurposed e-scooter batteries.
Photo by: EDENenergy
All modules were thoroughly tested, and the results were better than expected. The company’s founders, who used to be researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE, said that they expected the old batteries to have roughly 80% life left in them, but the tests revealed that most retained about 90% of their original capacity.
After being abused in their previous life, the e-scooter batteries will have a much easier future in the startup’s energy storage systems, where vibrations and large temperature fluctuations are non-existent. What’s more, the long-term energy capacity of the system can be easily kept at 70 kWh by simply replacing modules that become unusable down the line.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The startup said it remotely monitors each module, and when it’s time for a replacement, it can be done without powering down the whole system. That’s a big plus, especially for energy-sensitive scenarios where cutting the power would result in massive losses.
The keen-eyed among you might have noticed that there’s a solar inverter on one side of the battery box. That’s because EDENenergy’s first product was designed for companies that have solar panels but can’t store solar energy yet. “In mid-October, we delivered the first storage system to a customer, which was an important milestone for our young company,” said Florian Bierwirth, one of the founders. “With this storage size, we initially aim to target medium-sized companies in the region that have a photovoltaic system but do not yet have a storage solution.”
For its next step, the startup wants to come up with a way of using different batteries from different manufacturers. “To do this, the connector interfaces, battery management system, and communication protocols must be adapted for each new battery. There’s a particularly wide range of options when it comes to e-bikes,” said Bierwirth. Currently, the small company relies on large suppliers that can send in large numbers of the same battery type.
A larger-capacity battery system of up to 300 kWh is also in the works, putting roughly 500 second-life e-scooter modules to good use instead of sending them to the landfill. The batteries will eventually give up, but when that happens, they’ll be sent to a
recycling facility
where they’ll be dismantled, and their contents will be reused, if possible.

title: Used EVs Are Selling Like Hotcakes. The Fastest Movers May Surprise You
content:
Used EVs Are Selling Like Hotcakes. The Fastest Movers May Surprise You
The biggest name in the business didn't even crack the top 10.
Used EVs are getting more popular. Not only are they increasing in popularity, they're selling even faster than their hybrid and even gasoline counterparts, according to iSeeCars.
You might assumed that all of the used Teslas hitting the market would be a big reason why. But in reality, no Tesla even cracked the top 10 list of best-selling used EVs in September 2026.
Compared to the same month last year, this September saw a 9.8% price increase for used EVs. That's exactly double the 4.8% increase used hybrids saw year-over-year. However, both absolutely crush used gas car values, which only jumped 0.3%. You can bet that high fuel prices over the past year or so have had an affect on gas and diesel demand. People are thinking about EVs more than ever before, especially every time the see eye-watering receipts from every fill up.
“These pricing shifts reflect significantly different year-over-year trends across drivetrains,” iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer said in a release. “Ongoing higher fuel prices are likely driving the shift, though the EV segment has also recovered from the demand turbulence caused by the loss of federal incentives a year ago.”
Price isn't the only indicator of demand, though. Speed is another. Used EVs fly off the figurative shelves faster than gas cars, spending an average of 41.9 days on the lot. Not only is that 10.1% faster than September 2025, but it's almost two weeks faster on average than gas cars, which take 54.8 days to sell. Furthermore, gas car sale time increased by 19.9%. So it's getting harder to sell used gas cars, while EVs are getting easier.
Admittedly, in defense of gas cars, customers are spoiled for choice. There are far, far more gas cars available for sale—for example, Autotrader lists 1,384,383 used gas and diesel cars nationwide, but only 44,434 used EVs. There are also fewer EV models for sale, so customers aren't cross-shopping as much. Still, there's no denying that used EV demand is increasing as supply continues to grow.
There are also more options than ever in a market that was once essentially wholly dominated by Tesla. But in September, none of the top 10 fastest-selling used EV models were Teslas. There weren't any Lucids or Rivians in there, either. The quickest-selling EVs were oddly the Audi Q4 E-tron Sportback, followed by the Toyota bZX4, and Lexus RZ 300e. So it seems that used EV customers are becoming like everyone else: they just want something small and practical, with some quirky styling and a nice interior. Also on the list were the Honda Prologue, BMW iX, and even Polestar 2.
The slowest-selling EVs aren't exactly surprising, though, as they're mostly massive and expensive SUVs and trucks. The Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-seller by a huge margin, but it's also uber-expensive. It was followed by the GMC Sierra EV, Chevy Silverado EV, and the Volvo EX90. The Hummer EV was on the list, too, proving that GM's Ultium trucks aren't exactly popular on the used market.
One of the reasons why used Teslas might not have sold as quickly as other EVs is that their prices have increased. The Tesla Model S and Model X both saw used price increases of 22% and 18%, respectively. That is good for the two highest of any used car on the market, regardless of powertrain.
It's interesting to see used EVs increasing in selling speed, showing that customers are willing to go electric when the vehicle type and price suits their needs. And now that data has come out proving that EVs don't lose as much range over time as previously thought, it seems that used EVs are becoming better and better buys.

title: 6 年后或将坠落，NASA 重启哈勃望远镜救援方案研讨
content:
IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）正在重新讨论拯救哈勃太空望远镜的可能性。尽管目前哈勃望远镜运行状况良好，但按照现有轨道变化趋势，预计其将在大约 6 年后重新进入地球大气层。
NASA 于 10 月 29 日发布了一份信息征询书（RFI），征集能够在轨为航天器提供服务的技术方案。这些方案可能包括提升哈勃望远镜的轨道高度，以抵消大气阻力造成的轨道持续衰减，甚至可能执行一项任务，以某种方式进一步增强望远镜的观测能力。
哈勃望远镜于 1990 年 4 月发射升空，由 NASA 与欧洲航天局（ESA）合作建造。此后，宇航员曾通过航天飞机任务为其执行过 5 次维修和升级，最近一次是在 2009 年。
哈勃望远镜取得了大量具有里程碑意义的科学成果，其中包括帮助科学家证实宇宙膨胀正在加速，这项发现后来获得了诺贝尔奖。此外，它还在行星、星系、恒星以及宇宙其他领域取得了大量重要发现。
哈勃望远镜还经常与其他望远镜协同开展科学观测。NASA 的数据显示，其观测成果已经促成至少 2.3 万篇科学论文发表。尽管服役时间已经很长，哈勃望远镜依然受到天文学界的高度重视。NASA 今年 9 月表示：“天文学家每年申请的观测时间，约为实际可提供时间的 7 倍。”
哈勃望远镜也深受公众喜爱。多年来，人们一直在欣赏和分享它拍摄的标志性宇宙图像，其中最著名的当属鹰状星云中的“创生之柱”。这张令人惊叹的照片在过去几十年间曾多次重新拍摄。
因此，近年来 NASA 并非首次讨论如何让这台著名的太空望远镜继续服役。
例如，2022 年，亿万富翁科技企业家贾里德 · 艾萨克曼（Jared Isaacman）曾提议利用 SpaceX 的设备执行哈勃望远镜维修任务。艾萨克曼还曾购买并指挥过两次 SpaceX 载人轨道飞行任务，分别于 2021 年 9 月和 2024 年 9 月执行。
不过，NASA 当时拒绝了这一提议，理由是相关任务可能给这台运行状况良好的望远镜带来风险。
但如今，情况似乎发生了变化。艾萨克曼于 2025 年 12 月出任 NASA 局长。他在 NASA 10 月 30 日发布的一份声明中表示，考虑到哈勃望远镜能够持续带来的科学价值，NASA 应该“寻找一切合理的机会，让它尽可能长时间地继续发挥作用”，尤其是在延长其服役时间的成本低于发射新任务的情况下。
艾萨克曼还于 10 月 30 日在 X 平台发文称，相关方案“仍然值得探索”。他指出，NASA 此前曾考虑过一种“成本低得多的解决方案”，以便让哈勃望远镜继续留在轨道上。他补充说：“那是过去的方案，但现在仍然值得付出努力。哈勃望远镜值得这样做。”
不过，此次发布的信息征询书也允许考虑其他方案，包括在哈勃望远镜任务结束时，让其安全、可控地重返地球大气层，或者将其转移至轨道进行处置。
NASA 表示，由于轨道阻力的影响，哈勃望远镜预计将在 2033 年或 2034 年自然进入地球大气层。因此，如果要执行在轨维修任务，最晚需要在 2032 年实施。
今年早些时候，NASA 还曾与 Katalyst Space Technologies 公司合作，推进一项耗资 3,000 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2.01 亿元人民币）的任务，计划提升尼尔 · 格雷尔斯 · 斯威夫特天文台（Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory）的轨道高度。这座天文台同样受到轨道阻力影响，正在逐渐向地球坠落。
这项希望渺茫的轨道救援任务是在较短时间内紧急制定的，目的是赶在太阳活动增强之前完成任务。太阳活动增强会导致地球大气层膨胀，进而增加航天器受到的阻力。
该任务最终于今年夏季成功发射。不过，由于控制系统出现问题，Katalyst 公司的 LINK 飞行器未能与 Swift 天文台完成交会对接。
预计这座天文台将在 11 月 4 日重返地球大气层，结束长达 22 年的运行任务，这远远超过了其原本仅有两年的设计使用寿命。

title: 人类改变轨道的小行星，终于被欧空局赫拉探测器拍摄到
content:
IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，欧洲行星防御探测器“赫拉”（Hera）正在接近 NASA 曾实施 DART 撞击偏转测试的双小行星系统，目前已能够分辨出这两颗岩质天体。
赫拉探测器即将结束前往“迪迪莫斯”（Didymos）小行星系统的旅程。该探测器于 2024 年 10 月搭乘 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号火箭发射升空。10 月 18 日，赫拉在距离这对小行星约 1280 公里处拍摄了迪迪莫斯及其体积较小的伴星“迪莫弗斯”（Dimorphos）。目前，这对小行星距离地球约 1.97 亿公里。
欧洲航天局（ESA）赫拉项目科学家迈克尔 · 库佩尔斯（Michael Kueppers）在一份声明中表示：“通过这张图像，我们首次看到了体积较小的迪莫弗斯小行星。在拍摄这张照片之前，探测器仍然只能将迪迪莫斯系统识别为一个单独的光点。但现在，尽管迪莫弗斯在这张初始图像中仅占据大约一个像素，却已经能够与其母体清晰地区分开来。”
据IT之家了解，2022 年 9 月，美国 NASA 的“双小行星重定向测试”（DART）任务探测器撞击了迪莫弗斯，成功改变了这颗小行星的轨道，完成了一次具有开创意义的行星防御技术演示。赫拉探测器的任务是调查撞击造成的影响，进一步完善人类对这次撞击过程以及两颗小行星本身的认识。
赫拉探测器于今年 10 月早些时候实施了减速机动，以降低接近速度，并调整飞行轨道，为与这对双小行星会合做好准备。该探测器搭载了 12 台科学载荷，计划对两颗小行星开展后续观测，为行星防御工作提供新的研究数据。
此外，此次任务还携带了两颗立方体卫星（CubeSat），用于近距离观测迪莫弗斯，并最终尝试在这颗直径约 151 米的小行星上着陆。
目前，赫拉仍在继续接近目标，并为抵达做好准备。预计本月晚些时候，这项任务将迎来一个重要节点。
欧洲航天局任务经理伊恩 · 卡内利（Ian Carnelli）表示：“随着赫拉不断接近目标，我们拍摄到的图像将变得更加清晰。11 月 25 日，我们将公布迪莫弗斯的首批详细图像。这是太阳系中首个因人类行动而被证实轨道发生可测量变化的天体。”

title: 你的下一辆车，机器人手搓的
content:
各位IT之家家友都门儿清：现在造车，既不是纯“机器造”，也不是老派“人工造”，而是人和机器深度组队。
像冲压、焊接、涂装这种大工艺，交给机器猛猛干就完了，力气大、效率高；但到了总装环节，那些复杂的手工装配，还真得靠人上手。说白了，机器负责大力出奇迹，人负责细活儿出奇迹。
但各位有没有想过：会不会有那么一天，机器把人类那双会干细活的手也替了，活儿全包圆？答案很干脆：会。
更关键的是，来替人工的不是那种傻大黑粗的大机器，而是灵活得多的机器人；真别不信，没准儿你下一次买的车，就是机器人给你手搓出来的。
关于机器人造车这事儿，小编觉得真得好好唠一唠。
IT之家小编为啥突然想和大家唠机器人造车？还不是因为今早刷到一条视频。
雷军分享了小米机器人的“实习”新进展：首次在汽车工厂挑战 8 小时作业，满足工站全天生产需求，实现产线级作业能力的初步验证。
几个月“实习”下来，小米机器人能长时间稳定作业，有些朋友提的小米汽车，背后可能就有小米机器人参与制造。
从视频来看，小米机器人干起活来还挺麻利。虽说任务只是翻来覆去地“中控台侧盖板排序”，但人家干得有条不紊，节奏稳得很。
AMR 联动这块也挺有看头：工站物料更换时，机器人会耐心等着。
哪怕中途零件掉了这种小意外，另一个机器人也能立马协同处理，突发事件处理得挺及时。
除了小米让机器人在总装车间当“长工时实习生”，还有多家国产车企也把人形机器人真投进了造车流程，不过大多还处在从“试点实习”往“规模化应用”过渡的阶段，具体干的工序也各有侧重。
比如上汽，今年 3 月就宣布，由上汽通用与智元机器人联合研发的具身智能人形机器人“能仔 1 号”，正式在别克至境 E7 电池量产线上岗。
这货本事不小：视觉感知、双臂协同、力控抓取都安排上了，能自主完成电芯来料识别和抓取路径规划，不用靠固定编程，也不用等来料精确到位。导航引导轨迹累计定位精度达到 ±0.1 毫米，作业效率大约每件 2 秒，占地面积还不到传统自动工位的 15%。
另外，奇瑞、小鹏、蔚来、长安等车企也都布局人形机器人，不过目前还没到让机器人挑大梁、干核心造车工序那一步。
长安汽车首席专家谭欢就曾透露，长安以后要用机器人造车、用机器人卖车、把机器人放上车，最终目标是实现“用机器人造机器人”，再用机器人造出世界万物。
彼时靠机械臂，此时看人形机器人。咱以后买的车，很可能真就是机器人一手一脚“手搓”出来的。
二、“黑灯工厂”的目标
不知各位IT之家家友听没听过“黑灯工厂”？这玩意儿说白了，就是靠智能机器人、自动化设备和数字化系统撑起来的全流程无人化智能工厂。核心特征就一句话：生产、存储、检测这些环节都不用人工值守，关着灯也能持续运转。
到目前为止，已经有多家车企通过大规模部署传统工业机器人，把“黑灯工厂”给整出来了。但话又说回来，至今还没有任何一家车企，是完全依靠人形机器人实现真正意义上的“黑灯工厂”。
在国外分析机构看来，到 2030 年，至少会有一家汽车制造商实现 100% 装配自动化，大概率来自美国或中国。
还有分析师笃定认为，中国有望诞生全球首座完全“熄灯运行”的汽车工厂 —— 所有工序全由机器人完成。
在业界看来，这事儿要是真成了，那就标志着人工智能、人形机器人和数字化制造技术的融合到了拐点，装配流程里的人工岗位会被大幅削减，而且影响范围可不止工厂车间 —— 汽车设计理念、劳动力培训体系，乃至整个汽车生产的经济模式，都可能被重新塑一遍。
看好美国或中国的汽车制造商率先建成全自动化装配线，这个很好理解 —— 毕竟这两个市场的多家车企“已在布局颠覆性生产流程，且对人形机器人的关注度日益提升”。
那问题来了：为啥时间线要锁定在 2030 年左右，而不是更近的明年、后年？
原因也不复杂：目前汽车装配线里，还有两个环节没实现完全自动化，人形机器人暂时还搞不定。
一个是线束安装。这活儿难就难在，线束是上百根粗细不一、软了吧唧还容易变形的导线凑一块儿，人形机器人的手很难像人手那样灵活地抓、定、穿、打结，想复刻人的柔性操作，属实有点为难它。
另一个是座舱装配。这活儿更憋屈：人形机器人得“钻进”狭小车厢里，角度有限、行程也有限，还得完成精细操作，机械手臂干这个真不太灵光。
一个软得难拿捏，一个窄得难施展。本来就还在验证早期，眼下又卡着两道不好迈的坎。
但机器人造车这事，本来就是一道工序一道工序往外交：先交刚性、固定的活儿，再交柔性、讲究“手感”的活儿，最后才交那些得钻进犄角旮旯里的活儿。
总之，真正完全由人形机器人主导的“黑灯工厂”还在演进中，仍是一个未来目标。
三、人工智能 + 人类智慧
写到这里，IT之家小编忍不住想问各位一句：假如以后的车是纯人形机器人造的，你敢买吗？
咱理性盘一盘。真到了机器人能独立造车那一步，说明它的可靠性和精度已经摸到工业级门槛，跟要求之间不存在数量级差距。
而机器最大的优势，恰恰就在于它是个机器：不喊累、不走神、不摸鱼，也不会因为早上跟对象吵架就手抖。理论上，人为失误这个变量能被直接清零。
但是，既然是机器人，就不排除出现“幻觉”的可能，一旦某个节点抽风，搞不好就是大麻烦。
传统工厂出了岔子，能一路追到某个工位、某个人、某个班次，问责对象起码是一个大活人，全自动化之后呢？假设真出了质量事故或人身伤害，责任该怎么划分？
所以现实点看，人形机器人在造车领域，不是来替代传统工业机器人的，而是来补位的 —— 专门瞄准后者几十年来啃不动的“长尾非标工序”，干那些机器干不了、人干又费劲的柔性活儿。
而且就算装配线全自动化了，工厂里其他岗位照样得有人参与。把人工智能技术和“人类智慧”捏到一块儿，才是车企未来成功的关键。
车企对人形机器人的依赖度会越来越高，这确实是趋势，但行业真正的核心趋势，绝非是简单的“换机器人”。
关于机器人造车这事儿，IT之家小编就先唠到这儿。
未来几年买车，大概率还是“有人参与”造出来的，但人参与的程度，肯定比眼下的低不少，而且只会越来越低。
哪怕真到了传统机器加人形机器人合力手搓的那天，监控、把关这种环节，还是希望人来盯着。
毕竟，车可以没人造，但买车的终究是大活人，安全感可不能打折。

title: 德国初创企业实现在轨 3D 打印刚性梁，验证太空建造能力
content:
IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，德国初创公司 Orbital Matter 研发的一颗卫星，近日在轨道上利用 3D 打印技术制造出一根长约半米的横梁。公司高管称，这是自由飞行航天器首次在轨完成此类打印，也是未来在太空建造大型结构迈出的重要一步。
据IT之家了解，这颗名为 Replicator 2 的小型卫星于今年夏季搭乘 SpaceX 的拼车发射任务进入太空，机上搭载了 Orbital Matter 的 4 台 3D 打印机。每台打印机都能够通过挤出树脂线圈制造坚固的圆柱形横梁，随后利用紫外线照射使树脂固化。该公司将这一过程比作水泥与水混合后凝固成型。
这项技术之所以重要，是因为未来的航天器需要拥有更大的尺寸，才能产生更多电力，并将更多热量散发到太空真空环境中。如果未来要建设轨道数据中心，这方面的需求将尤为突出。然而，航天器在发射时仍必须适应运载火箭顶部整流罩内部狭小的空间。如果航天器能够在轨道上自行建造所需结构，电力供应和散热方面的难题就有望更容易得到解决。
Orbital Matter 首席执行官兼联合创始人雅库布 · 斯托耶克（Jakub Stojek）表示：“Replicator 2 首次证明，我们完全可以直接在太空中建造太阳能电池阵列，并根据任务需求决定其尺寸。”
目前，Orbital Matter 正与欧洲航天局（ESA）以及欧洲领先的卫星制造商泰雷兹阿莱尼亚航天公司（Thales Alenia Space）开展合作，后者也参与了 Replicator 2 项目。
如今，太空中的大型结构主要通过类似折纸的方式展开：大型太阳能电池阵列或望远镜镜面在发射前折叠收纳，进入轨道后再展开。这类操作涉及复杂的工程设计，因此，直接在太空中制造和组装这些结构成为一种颇具吸引力的方案。
NASA 已经资助过一些相关研究。其中较为突出的是与 Redwire 公司合作开展的一项任务。该公司曾于 2023 年在真空舱内成功 3D 打印结构横梁，但这项技术始终未能真正进入太空应用。
Orbital Matter 的 4 台打印机中，有两台专门用于展开柔性太阳能电池阵列。不过，一次异常情况导致其中一台打印机发生故障。尽管如此，另一台打印机成功制造出的支撑杆仍顺利展开了太阳能电池阵列，成为这项技术的重要概念验证。
此前，微重力环境下的 3D 打印尝试仅限于国际空间站内部的加压环境，而 Orbital Matter 此次则在自由飞行的卫星上完成了相关测试。
Orbital Matter 首席技术官罗伯特 · 伊纳蒂辛（Robert Ihnatsin）告诉 TechCrunch：“这就是我们为什么要在这颗卫星上搭载这么多台打印机。与其在地面上花费数年时间测试各种可能性，我们更愿意直接在轨道上积累经验，并根据需要调整软件。”
此次打印横梁的长度受到卫星携带树脂数量的限制，但公司工程师认为，制造长度达 100 米的横梁是可行的。作为对比，SpaceX 的 Starlink V2 卫星是目前轨道上性能最强的量产卫星之一，其太阳能电池阵列长度约为 20 米。
Orbital Matter 于 2022 年由伊纳蒂辛和斯托耶克共同创立。伊纳蒂辛此前曾在 3D 打印公司 Formlabs 工作。公司成立后完成了 300 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,005.2 万元人民币）的种子轮融资。
目前，Orbital Matter 正在筹备另一项技术验证任务，计划于 2028 年发射。届时，公司将测试一款更大尺寸的打印机，并将其搭载在一颗更大的卫星上。公司希望借此展开一套能够提供 5 千瓦电力的太阳能电池阵列。
该任务将成为后续扩大部署规模的“垫脚石”。Orbital Matter 计划到 2030 年实现单侧太阳能电池阵列输出功率超过 100 千瓦的大规模部署。
此外，该公司还在与多家卫星制造商合作。这些制造商正在考虑将 Orbital Matter 的 PADS（打印机辅助展开系统）集成到自家航天器中，用于展开太阳能电池板、天线或其他组件。

title: 比尔 · 盖茨：阿尔茨海默病的检测和治疗方法已经问世，但采用的进展很缓慢
content:
IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，微软创始人比尔 · 盖茨今日发文称，阿尔茨海默病的检测和治疗方法已经问世。
比尔 · 盖茨表示，过去，诊断阿尔茨海默病的唯一方法是进行昂贵的脑部扫描或腰椎穿刺。这一障碍导致了一个恶性循环：由于检查过程过于繁琐，且当时本就没有有效的治疗方法，因此很少有人接受检测。由于缺乏大量确诊患者，研究人员难以找到符合条件、能够参与检测和治疗临床试验的患者。这阻碍了本应带来新诊断工具的研究进展，导致该领域在数十年间基本停滞不前。
正因如此，近期血液检测技术的研发才是一项重大突破。对患者而言，这一过程与抽血检测胆固醇并无二致。首批两项血液检测技术于去年问世，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）也于今年 8 月刚刚批准了另外两项新技术。
在治疗方面，FDA 已批准两种抗体疗法，这些疗法能够清除淀粉样蛋白（与阿尔茨海默病密切相关的蛋白质），并能在一定程度上延缓认知功能衰退。这两种疗法都需要前往诊所接受输液治疗，其过程类似于癌症患者接受化疗的方式。
最新的创新就在今年早些时候：7 月，FDA 批准了一种可在家中使用注射笔进行注射的版本，这种注射笔与人们用于注射 GLP-1 制剂的工具相同。这使得该药物对患者来说更加方便实用，特别是对于行动不便或居家老年人而言。
在美国，联邦医疗保险甚至会承担输液治疗的费用，使患者能够以更低廉的价格接受治疗。
然而，阿尔茨海默病专家表示，目前这些工具被采用的进展很缓慢。IT之家注意到，比尔 · 盖茨在文中提到了部分障碍：
并非所有人都知道。据我采访的专家称，许多医生和患者根本不知道有这些检查和治疗方法。
获批治疗可能需要数月时间。全科医生可以开具血液检查单，但通常只有记忆障碍专科医生才能开具治疗方案。由于预约专科医生可能需要数月时间，因此确诊患者往往需要等待很长时间才能开始服药。这段时间非常宝贵，因为治疗开始得越早，效果就越好。
存在监管和行政方面的障碍。除美国以外，大多数国家的医疗保险计划都不涵盖血液检测费用。即使在美国，联邦医疗保险是否支付检测费用也取决于你的居住地。该保险完全不涵盖认知功能正常人群的筛查。此外，与输液治疗相比，新型注射治疗患者自付的费用要高得多。
输液治疗过程繁琐且伴有副作用。其中一种药物需要患者在一年半的时间里每两周前往输液诊所一次，此后则需每月前往一次。对许多患者而言，这超出了他们的承受能力。此外，在极少数情况下，这些药物可能会引起严重的副作用，因此患者在治疗初期必须接受一系列磁共振成像检查。
临床试验在招募志愿者方面仍面临困难。要参加试验，你必须住在试验开展地点附近，并且能够前往该地点。研究人员在招募多样化的受试者群体方面尤为困难，因此无法全面了解不同种族和族裔群体的治疗获益。
为此，比尔 · 盖茨正在思考如何降低这些障碍。能够加速研究进展的一项具体举措，就是吸引更多人自愿参与临床试验。阿尔茨海默病协会提供了一款在线工具，可帮助你了解自己或亲人是否符合参与条件，如果符合，还能帮你找到合适的临床研究项目。
比尔 · 盖茨还透露，目前行业正在研发新的血液检测方法，用于检测 tau 蛋白 —— 这种蛋白质会杀死神经元并导致认知能力下降。新药也可能针对 tau 蛋白发挥作用。
在预防方面，已发表的研究表明，饮食、运动和社会交往可以降低认知能力下降的风险。目前，研究人员正在研究在患者出现症状之前进行干预，是否能够减缓疾病进展、推迟发病时间，甚至完全预防该疾病。

title: BIM, KI und die Zukunft des Bauens: Neue Vortragsreihe am IU Campus Hannover
content:
BIM, KI und die Zukunft des Bauens: Neue Vortragsreihe am IU Campus Hannover
Wie verändern Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz das Planen und Bauen? Die kostenfreie Vortragsreihe „BIM / KI / Digitalisierung – BAU“ am IU Campus Hannover geht dieser Frage im Wintersemester 2026/2027 nach. Seit dem Auftakt am 6. Oktober 2026 stellen Gäste aus Planung, Beratung, Forschung und Bauausführung ihre Projekte, Erfahrungen und Technologien vor, jeweils mit Beispielen aus der Praxis.
Bildung für alle, praxisnah
Die Reihe unterstreicht den Anspruch der IU, Bildung für alle zugänglich zu machen und praxisnah zu gestalten. Sie richtet sich nicht nur an Studierende, sondern auch an Unternehmen und Fachpublikum. Wer sich für BIM (Building Information Modeling, auf Deutsch: Bauwerkinformationsmodellierung) und KI im Bauwesen interessiert, kann mitdiskutieren, Fragen stellen und Kontakte knüpfen. Die Gäste bringen aktuelles Praxiswissen direkt in den Hörsaal, wo Studierende und Interessierte es direkt mit ihrem Studium oder Job verbinden können.
Neun Abende, ein roter Faden
Die Reihe umfasst sechs Haupttermine am ersten Dienstag des Monats und drei Zusatztermine am dritten Dienstag von Januar bis März 2027. Sie beginnen jeweils um 17 Uhr. Die Schwerpunkte:
1) BIM-Management bei der Deutschen Bahn und aktueller Stand der BIM-Implementierung in der Verkehrsanlagenplanung

Thermische und thermochemische Randschichtbehandlungen sind wichtige Verfahren in der industriellen Fertigung. Sie machen Werkzeuge und Bauteile beispielsweise härter, verschleiß- und ermüdungsfester und können ihre Korrosionsbeständigkeit verbessern, gleichzeitig sind diese Prozesse jedoch sehr energieintensiv. Wie sich der Energieverbrauch bei konstanter Bauteilqualität künftig optimieren lässt, untersucht das neue Verbundprojekt »CyPro – Cyber-physische Produktionssysteme zur Energieeffizienzsteigerung und Quali-tätssicherung von thermischen und thermochemischen Behandlungsprozessen«, das vom Fraunhofer-Institut für Schicht- und Oberflächentechnik IST koordiniert.
Energieverbrauch und Bauteilqualität gemeinsam betrachten
Eine besondere Herausforderung bei thermischen und thermochemischen Behandlungsprozessen besteht darin, dass Prozessparameter, Energieverbrauch und Bauteilqualität eng miteinander verknüpft sind. Eine Reduzierung des Energieeinsatzes darf nicht zu Lasten der geforderten Bauteileigenschaften gehen. Das Projekt »CyPro« setzt genau an dieser Schnittstelle an. Ziel ist die Entwicklung eines cyber-physischen Produktionssystems (CPPS), das Prozess-, Energie-, Sensor- und Produktionsdaten kontinuierlich erfassen und miteinander verknüpfen soll. Ergänzend ist unter anderem der Einsatz der optischen Emissionsspektroskopie vorgesehen, um den Zustand des Plasmas in Echtzeit zu überwachen.
Auf Basis der erhobenen Daten sollen erklärbare KI-Modelle entwickelt werden, die Zusammenhänge zwischen Prozessparametern, Energiebedarf und Qualitätsmerkmalen abbilden. Geplant ist, dabei beispielsweise die Nitrierhärtetiefe, die Ausbildung der Verbindungsschicht oder die Korrosionsbeständigkeit der behandelten Bauteile zu berücksichtigen. Im Unterschied zu reinen datengetriebenen »Black-Box«-Ansätzen soll damit nachvollziehbar werden, wie sich Veränderungen der Prozessführung auf Energieverbrauch und Bauteileigenschaften auswirken.
Darüber hinaus sollen die datenbasierten Modelle durch physikalisch basierte Modellierun-gen wie thermodynamische und CFD-gestützte Simulationen ergänzt werden, um so unter anderem Wärmeflüsse, Phasenübergänge und Abwärmepotenziale in der Anlage und ihrer Peripherie untersuchen zu können. Auf diese Weise sollen sich Energieverluste sowohl da-tenbasiert als auch physikalisch fundiert bewerten lassen. Zudem soll ein Planungswerkzeug auf Basis des bestärkenden Lernens perspektivisch nicht nur einzelne Prozessparameter, sondern auch Auftragsreihenfolgen, Anlagenbelegung, Durchlaufzeiten und Lastspitzen berücksichtigen. Geplant ist es, die gewonnenen Informationen in Echtzeit in einem Dashboard bereitzustellen und prädiktive Handlungsempfehlungen für den Anlagenbetrieb zu ermöglichen.
Plasmanitrieren als industrieller Demonstrator
Die Methoden werden zunächst am Beispiel des Plasmanitrierens entwickelt und erprobt. Als industrieller Demonstrator dient eine Plasmanitrieranlage des Fraunhofer IST, an der zentrale Messkampagnen mit definierten Referenzchargen durchgeführt sowie Prozess-, Energie- und Qualitätsdaten erfasst und ausgewertet werden sollen. Die behandelten Bauteile sollen hinsichtlich relevanter Randschicht- und Gebrauchseigenschaften charakterisiert werden, um auf dieser Basis die Sensorik, Datenmodelle und weiteren Komponenten des geplanten CPPS schrittweise integrieren und unter realitätsnahen Produktionsbedingungen zu validieren zu können.
Rund 24 MWh Einsparpotenzial pro Jahr
Eine erste Potenzialabschätzung für die Plasmanitrieranlage zeigt die mögliche Größenordnung: Rund 24 MWh Energie pro Jahr könnten langfristig deutschlandweit ggf. eingespart werden. Davon entfallen nach der Abschätzung rund 17 MWh auf die Rückgewinnung und Nutzung von Abwärme und weitere 7 MWh auf eine optimierte Prozessführung.
Im Projekt soll nun untersucht werden, wie sich diese Potenziale technisch erschließen und unter realitätsnahen Produktionsbedingungen nutzen lassen. Für Produktionsbetriebe und Lohnbehandler könnten sich daraus geringere Strom- und Betriebskosten, reduzierte Last-spitzen und ein geringerer CO₂-Ausstoß ergeben. Gleichzeitig soll die präzisere Überwa-chung und Steuerung der Prozesse dazu beitragen, das Risiko von Qualitätsabweichungen und kostenintensiver Nacharbeit zu reduzieren.
Im weiteren Projektverlauf ist vorgesehen, die beim Plasmanitrieren gewonnenen Erkenntnisse auf weitere thermische und thermochemische Verfahren, insbesondere PACVD-Beschichtungen und Gasnitrieren, zu übertragen. Darüber hinaus soll geprüft werden, inwieweit sich die entwickelte Methodik auf andere industrielle Ofensysteme übertragen lässt, bei denen hohe Temperaturen, lange Prozesszeiten und relevante Abwärmeströme auftreten. Perspektivisch könnte das CPPS auch eine anlagenübergreifende Produktionsplanung er-möglichen, bei der mehrere Wärmebehandlungsanlagen dann energieoptimiert, lastflexibel und möglichst netzdienlich betrieben werden könnten.
Zum Projekt
»CyPro – Cyber-physische Produktionssysteme zur Energieeffizienzsteigerung und Qualitätssicherung von thermischen und thermochemischen Behandlungsprozessen«

Wie Gebirge oder Flussläufe das Entstehen von Arten beeinflussen, untersucht der Evolutionsbiologe und Umweltwissenschaftler Prof. Oskar Hagen anhand von Computermodellen. In der jetzt erschienenen Ausgabe des Magazins „Forschung Frankfurt“ erklärt der Experte, wie seine Modelle das „Nachspielen“ der Evolution von vielen Millionen Jahren ermöglichen und erste Prognosen für die Lebensvielfalt im Klimawandel geben. Weitere Beiträge von Forschung Frankfurt berichten über die Kanaren als Biodiversitätshotspots, nehmen das Aussterben des prähistorischen Hais Megalodon in den Blick oder schildern, wie globale Standards für die Nachhaltigkeitsberichterstattung von Unternehmen entwickelt werden.
FRANKFURT. Oskar Hagen ist Herr über Zeit und Raum – zumindest in seinen Computermodellen. Hier kann er Flussdeltas entstehen und Gebirge zu Ebenen werden lassen, und Millionen von Jahren schrumpfen zu Minuten an Rechenzeit. Warum gibt es – untypischerweise – am Oberlauf des Amazonas so viel mehr Fischarten als im Flussdelta? Warum sind im üppig grünen Kongobecken viel weniger Tier- und Pflanzenarten beheimatet als in den Regenwäldern Südostasiens oder Südamerikas? In der jüngsten Ausgabe von „Forschung Frankfurt“ berichtet der Wissenschaftler, wie er und sein Team Computermodelle entwickeln, um die Mechanismen der Evolution besser zu verstehen – und wie sich damit auch Prognosen zum Beispiel für das Aussterben tropischer Fischarten bei steigenden Meerestemperaturen ableiten lassen. Das Thema Artensterben berührt ihn auch persönlich: „Jede Art wurde über viele Millionen Jahre hinweg durch die Evolution geformt. Das allein sollte uns demütig stimmen.“
Weitere Artikel von „Forschung Frankfurt“ handeln zum Beispiel von den Kanaren, auf denen sich in der Abgeschiedenheit vom Festland viele neue Pflanzenarten entwickelt haben – die besonders anfällig für einschleppte Kaninchen und Ziegen sind. In weiteren Texten erklären Forschende, wie man den Speiseplan des einstigen „Königs der Meere“, des riesigen Hais Megalodon, anhand seiner Zähne rekonstruieren kann und warum er ausgestorben ist. Weitere Forschungsgeschichten handeln davon, wie Finanz- und Biowissenschaftler der Goethe-Universität gemeinsam an der Entwicklung einer Umweltklassifikation etwa von DAX-Konzernen arbeiten und wie sie zur Schaffung globaler Standards für die Nachhaltigkeitsberichterstattung beitragen.

title: Hilti und Universität Liechtenstein verstärken Zusammenarbeit
content:
Hilti und Universität Liechtenstein verstärken Zusammenarbeit
Im Rahmen des neuen «Hilti Innovation Hub» finanziert die Hilti Foundation für vier Jahre drei Professuren an der Universität Liechtenstein in den Bereichen Innovation, Technologie, Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz. Ein zusätzlich von der Hilti Gruppe finanziertes Kompetenzzentrum für nachhaltigeres Bauen verbessert den Wissenstransfer in die Praxis.
Die langjährige Zusammenarbeit zwischen dem Unternehmen Hilti und der Universität Liechtenstein hat Forschung und Praxis besser vernetzt. Um die akademische Basis an der Universität zu festigen, finanziert die Hilti Foundation über den «Hilti Innovation Hub» drei Professuren zu den Themen «Technologie und Innovation», «Künstliche Intelligenz und Datenwissenschaft» sowie «Informationssysteme und digitale Innovation». Damit sollen bestehende Kooperationsbereiche gesichert, neue aufgebaut und Qualität, Geschwindigkeit und Praxisrelevanz des Wissenstransfers erhöht werden.
«Mit der Weiterentwicklung des Engagements seitens der Hilti Foundation und des Unternehmens wollen wir Forschung und Wissenstransfer in und aus Liechtenstein stärken. Durch eine höhere Kontinuität aufseiten Wissenschaft und Forschung können bessere Ergebnisse erzielt werden, die sich praxisnah nutzen lassen», erklärt Michèle Frey-Hilti, Verwaltungsratsmitglied der Hilti Gruppe.
«Für uns sind Forschung und Lehre zentral. Mit der Unterstützung der Hilti Foundation und der Hilti Gruppe können wir auf beiden Seiten noch mehr bewirken», sagt Christian Frommelt, Rektor der Universität Liechtenstein. «Je stärker die Studierenden in reale Fragestellungen eingebunden sind, desto grösser wird der Beitrag zur Fachkräfteentwicklung und damit zur Innovationsfähigkeit der Region.»
Kompetenzzentrum vereint Forschung und Industrie
Im Rahmen der Kooperation werden von der Hilti Gruppe unter anderem gemeinsame Projekte, Doktorarbeiten und Praktika im Unternehmen gefördert. Von besonderer Bedeutung ist das «Kompetenzzentrum für Nachhaltigkeit und digitale Innovation im Bauwesen», das seit Anfang 2026 besteht und von der Hilti Gruppe während zunächst drei Jahren finanziert wird.
Im Zentrum konzentrieren sich die Aktivitäten auf Nachhaltigkeit und Wirtschaftlichkeit von Bauprojekten über deren gesamten Lebenszyklus. Schwerpunkte sind klimafreundlicheres, effizienteres und digitales Bauen, von der Planung über die Realisierung bis hin zum Betrieb von Gebäuden. Dafür werden die Forschung und das internationale Netzwerk der Universität mit dem Praxiswissen und den Marktkenntnissen von Hilti zusammengebracht.
Um die Ergebnisse möglichst schnell in die Bauindustrie übertragen zu können, ist das Kompetenzzentrum als offene Plattform gestaltet, bei der Studierende, Forschende, Unternehmen und internationale Partner zusammenkommen, ihr Wissen austauschen und voneinander lernen.
