title: Electric cars are about to overtake petrol in the UK, data shows
content:
Battery-electric cars took 32% of the UK’s new car market in October, while petrol cars fell to just 37.2%, according to new data from the SMMT. That’s the closest the two have been.
At the current pace, electric cars will outsell petrol in the UK within a year. And it could happen as soon as this December.
October: EVs up 33%, petrol down 12%
The UK registered 152,730 new cars in October, up 5.4% year-over-year and the 11th straight month of growth for the overall market.
All of that growth came from plug-ins. BEV registrations jumped 32.7% to 48,858 units, and plug-in hybrids rose 30.1% to 22,898. Meanwhile, petrol fell 11.6% to 56,876 units, diesel dropped 15.9%, and even conventional hybrids were down 5%.
Through the first 10 months of the year, the UK has now registered 503,805 BEVs, up 30.4%, for a 26.6% market share. Petrol’s year-to-date share is down to 41.1%, from 47.2% at the same point last year.
The trend points to 2027, or sooner
We pulled SMMT’s monthly fuel-type data going back to March 2024 to see where this is heading. Note that SMMT counts mild hybrids as petrol (or diesel) in its headline categories, and that’s generally how we count them at Electrek.
In March 2024, petrol held 55.9% of the market and BEVs 15.2%. In October 2026, it was 37.2% vs 32.0%. Petrol’s share is shrinking by about half a point per month on a linear trend, while BEVs gain about 0.36 points a month. Extend both lines and they cross around August 2027 at roughly 33% each.
But that’s the slow scenario, because it ignores December.
UK BEV share spikes every December as automakers push volume to get closer to their ZEV Mandate targets. BEVs hit 31.0% in December 2024 and 32.2% in December 2025, when petrol was at 39.4%. Over the last five months, BEV share has run about 5 points higher than a year earlier, and petrol about 7 points lower. If December follows that pattern, BEVs land around 37% and petrol around 32%.
That would be the first time BEVs beat petrol in SMMT’s headline numbers, mild hybrids included.
However, SMMT’s own forecast of 27.2% BEV share for the full year implies roughly 31% for November and December combined, which would make it a much closer call. And on a stricter definition that puts mild hybrids with hybrids instead of petrol, BEVs already outsold every other powertrain in August.
Zoom out to full years and the picture is just as clear. Cars that run only on petrol or diesel, mild hybrids included, made up 72.5% of the UK market in 2021. This year, they’re at 45.5%.
Automakers still want the mandate cut
None of this is good enough for the SMMT, which is using the release to push the government, again, to cut the ZEV Mandate targets.
The mandate requires 33% of 2026 sales to be zero-emission. SMMT now forecasts 27.2%. It expects 32% next year against a 38% target, and 37.5% in 2028 against 52%, a 14.5-point gap.
The trade group says automakers have spent “billions” on discounts, 0% financing, deposit contributions, and even subsidized charging to move EVs, on top of the government’s Electric Car Grant. It also slammed last week’s Budget, which confirmed a new EV-specific road tax (eVED) starting in 2028 and kept 20% VAT on public charging.
“Higher targets may force supply, but they do not create demand,” SMMT chief executive Mike Hawes said.
We’ve heard this one before. The SMMT made the same argument after September’s record 99,199 BEV registrations, and the government already opened a review of the mandate this year.
Chinese brands are taking the growth
This might be the main reason why the trade group wants to slow things down. The brands growing fastest in the UK are mostly Chinese. BYD registered 6,065 cars in October, up 73%. Jaecoo more than doubled to 6,089 units, Chery nearly tripled to 3,707, and Leapmotor doubled to 1,773. MG was up 85%.
Tesla, on the other hand, registered just 282 cars in October, down 45% from 511 a year ago. The first month of the quarter is always slow for Tesla in the UK, and the brand is still up 31% year-to-date at 46,526 units after a big September. But it didn’t have a single model in October’s top 10 BEVs, which was led by the Skoda Enyaq (1,568), Mini Countryman (1,494), and Jaecoo 5 (1,465).
Electrek’s Take
The SMMT’s framing is that there’s a “demand gap.” The data shows the opposite. BEV registrations are up 30% this year while petrol is shrinking every single month. That’s not a market rejecting EVs.
Top comment by European Bob
The SMMT is not a neutral organisation, they have been briefing against EVs for years and continue to do so.
The ZEV mandate is NOT a measure of how many pure BEVs are sold, and the SMMT know it, it's a measure of REDUCING emission against a level set in the past.
Those emissions reductions can be met by selling BEVs, or selling more efficient PHEVs or even selling more efficient petrol or diesel cars! The manufacturers can also buy credits if they choose to.
NO manufacturer has paid any ZEV fines to date (DfT announcement March 2026)
As for the "heavy discounts" and "loss making sales", well I have two data points on that.
1. The retail price of EVs has continued to climb in the UK over the past 6 years, despite the cost of any average 50kWh battery pack dropping several thousand dollars.
2. There are hundreds of main dealerships who are buying cars from the manufacturers, driving them for the minimum 3 month period, often with just a few thousand miles on the clock and then selling them with a 30-35% retail price discount, and then repeating ad infinitum. The dealerships are still making a few thousand with each transaction, so we know where the manufacturers price really sits.
And the discounts automakers keep complaining about? That’s the mandate doing exactly what it was designed to do. It forces automakers to sell EVs, so they price them to sell, and buyers respond. Hawes says targets don’t create demand, but cheaper EVs clearly do. October proves it.
Now, is the jump to 52% in 2028 steep? It is steep, but it looks achievable to me. If anything is hurting demand, it’s the government’s own moves: a new EV-only road tax and 20% VAT on public charging. That’s what the industry should be fighting. It’s too early for that.
Either way, petrol’s days as the UK’s default car are numbered. The only question is whether the milestone comes in December or sometime in 2027. Our bet is December.

title: Toyota updates the 2027 RAV4 PHEV with an NACS port and up to 52 miles of EV range
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 5 2026 - 7:40 am PT
The 2027
RAV4 is bringing a few major updates, including an added NACS charge port on all plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models.
2027 Toyota RAV4 prices and updates
The RAV4 was Toyota’s best-selling nameplate in the US last year and consistently ranks among America’s most popular vehicles alongside the Ford F-Series and Chevrolet Silverado.
For the 2027 model year, Toyota added several notable upgrades. The 2027 Toyota RAV4 will be available with hybrid (HEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains, with available front- or all-wheel drive (AWD).
The biggest change is that all 2027 RAV4 PHEV models now have a built-in NACS charge port with Level 3 DC fast-charging capabilities.
The NACS port is on the driver’s side and lets drivers use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. All PHEV grades also include an 11 kW onboard AC charger.
Powered by Toyota’s sixth-generation PHEV system, the plug-in RAV4 has standard AWD with a combined output of 321 horsepower. The setup includes a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, two electric motors, and a high-capacity traction battery.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV Woodland (Source: Toyota)
The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV offers up to 52 miles of pure electric range on the base SE trim. It will be available in four trims: SE, XSE, Woodland, and GR Sport.
Toyota updated the suspension system in the Woodland grade for the 2027 model year with new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, giving it 9.1″ of ground clearance.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport (Source: Toyota)
The Woodland trim adds a rugged look with standard All-Terrain tires, Roof Rails with Cross Bars, and a Tow Hitch Receiver. It also features new all-weather floor and cargo mats.
Lastly, the RAV4 GR Sport trim is for those who want a more performance-oriented, sporty style, with GT-tuned suspension and steering, sports seating, and a standard PHEV powertrain with AWD.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport interior (Source: Toyota)
Inside, the 2027 RAV4 includes a standard 12.3″ digital cluster and a 10.5″ touchscreen with the Toyota Audio Multimedia system, plus wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
A 12.9″ touchscreen with a JBL Premium Audio system with 9 speakers is standard on the Limited trim and available on the XSE grade.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 HEV starts at $32,300 (LE FWD), and the PHEV version starts at $42,100, not including the $1,595 destination fee.

title: 中创新航/鹏程无限等5企储能电池项目开工、投产
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期国科能源、中创新航、中科弘泰、天顺智慧能源、鹏程无限等多家企业相继推进产能落地。
国科能源兰州30GWh电池项目一期投产
11月2日，国科能源（兰州新区）有限公司年产30GWh新能源电池生产基地项目（一期）正式投料开机。
该基地整体规划产能30GWh，分三期建设，总投资约90亿元。其中，一期投资约28亿元，建设4条生产线，具备年产10GWh磷酸铁锂储能电芯能力，产品涵盖102Ah、314Ah及588Ah方形铝壳电芯，并同步布局钠电、固态电池技术路线。
天顺智慧能源洋梓5MWh项目投产下线
近期，天顺智慧能源洋梓项目5MWh集成储能柜在湖北荆门京山工厂完成产线联调与出厂检测，投产下线。
该项目聚焦储能系统集成业务，涵盖柜体、PCS、BMS、温控、消防及配电一体化装配调试，产品主要面向工商业削峰填谷、光伏配储、电网调峰及应急备用电源等场景。
本次下线标志着该基地具备了该机型的批量交付能力，后续将按计划开展排产与交付。
中创新航枣庄基地首批588Ah储能电芯下线
10月30日，中创新航枣庄基地举行电芯下线仪式，首批588Ah长循环储能电芯正式下线。
据悉，枣庄基地总规划产能100GWh，分三期推进。本次投产的一期项目总投资55亿元，建有电极车间、电芯车间及动力站房等，达产后将具备年产25GWh储能电池规模。下线产品为“至久”系列588Ah储能电芯，循环寿命超15000次，设计运行寿命达25年，主要应用于风光电站、电网侧调频及大型储能电站等场景。
中科弘泰铜陵固态电池及系统集成项目开工
10月23日，中科弘泰（安徽）新能源科技有限公司年产1GWh锂金属、超低温固态电池及2GWh储能、动力电池系统集成项目，在铜陵郊区经济开发区大通工贸园举行开工奠基仪式。
该项目由中科弘泰投资建设，并获得北京申宏资产管理有限公司投资支持。项目规划建设年产1GWh锂金属及超低温固态电池、2GWh储能及动力电池系统集成产线。
项目建成投产后，将贯通电池研发、电芯制造至系统集成全链条，主要面向储能及新能源动力应用场景，提升企业的规模化交付与品控能力。
鹏程无限遂宁25GWh储能电池项目开工
近日，深圳鹏程无限新能源有限公司25GWh新型储能电池项目在四川遂宁船山区开工建设。
该项目总投资55亿元，占地450亩，规划建设2条锂/钠兼容电芯产线及配套设施，具备年产25GWh储能电芯产能。产线支持磷酸铁锂与钠离子电芯柔性切换生产，产品面向大型储能、工商业储能、AIDC算力供电及便携储能等场景。

title: 亿纬锂能、新能安等6企签重磅储能订单合作
content:
近期，储能市场多项合作及项目进展落地。亿纬锂能、新能安、宁德时代、远东储能、国家电网、上能电气等6家企业，陆续宣布多项储能合作及交付动态。
亿纬锂能与CleanPeak签署战略合作协议
10月29日，亿纬锂能与CleanPeak签署1GWh储能项目合作谅解备忘录。
备忘录显示，双方就澳大利亚市场合计1GWh储能项目达成长期框架合作，覆盖储能电池与系统供应、技术协同、项目交付、并网调试及资产运维全环节。
章鱼能源、宁德时代与新能安签署战略合作
11月3日，新能安宣布，已与宁德时代、英国能源公司章鱼能源签署战略合作谅解备忘录（MOU），将围绕家庭储能、智能能源管理及数字化能源服务展开合作。
三方达成战略合作意向，可实现技术服务互补，打造含电池技术、产品制造、数字平台的完整能力链。
其中，宁德时代可为家庭储能提供全球领先的电芯与系统级技术支撑；新能安具备专业的产品研发、系统集成及规模化制造能力；章鱼能源在数字能源平台、智能能源管理及能源服务方面拥有丰富经验，可推动储能设备深度融入智慧能源运营。
远东储能供货拉脱维亚储能项目
11月3日，远东储能宣布，近日，正式交付拉脱维亚5MW/10MWh电源侧储能二期项目。
据悉，这是继一期项目落地后，远东储能再度以全液冷储能系统方案供货波罗的海市场。二期项目总规模5MW/10MWh，核心采用远东储能PowerSTROM 5000液冷储能集装箱，搭配2.5MW液冷型储能变流器（PCS）。
宁德时代中标内蒙古1.2GWh储能设备项目
11月3日，中国电建湖北工程有限公司内蒙蒙宁时代沙井300MW/1200MWh独立储能EPC项目储能设备采购项目成交结果公示，成交单位为宁德时代新能源科技股份有限公司。
据悉，蒙宁时代沙井300MW/1200MWh独立储能电站项目，是落地于内蒙古鄂尔多斯市杭锦旗的电网侧大型储能工程，由宁德时代间接全资控股的内蒙古蒙宁时代储能科技有限公司投资建设。
国家电网与阿曼企业签署储能合作协议
11月2日，阿曼Nama Holding与国家电网国际发展有限公司签署框架协议，双方将合作评估和开发阿曼的两座电池储能系统，规划规模为1000MW。
据悉，这两座储能系统拟分别位于杜库姆工业站和苏贝希站（伊卜里光伏三期），单座规模均为500MW，将接入阿曼400千伏国家输电网络。根据协议，双方将围绕项目评估与开发开展合作。
上能电气供货储能项目投运
11月3日，上能电气宣布，由其供货的宁夏同心1GW/2GWh共享储能示范项目已实现全容量并网投运超半年。
项目地处西北区域，上能电气为项目提供了1250kW集中式储能PCS，该机型在各类复杂电网条件已实现规模化应用、在国内外多个标杆项目中得到充分验证。

title: 合计注资2亿，晶澳、宁德时代、央国企成立新子公司
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近段时间，光储龙头企业、央国企接连设立新能源相关子公司，加码光伏运维、新材料、数字科技、风光储能项目开发等业务。
晶澳成立能源科技子公司
10月19日，东台晶联衡能源科技有限公司成立。企查查股权穿透显示，该公司由晶澳科技间接全资持股。
新公司法定代表人为赵亚超，注册资本2000万元。经营范围包含太阳能发电技术服务、光伏设备及元器件销售、光伏发电设备租赁、节能管理服务、合同能源管理等。
宁德时代接连成立新子公司，合计注册资本1.3亿
11月3日，宁德时代（福鼎）新材料科技有限公司成立。企查查股东显示，该新公司由宁德时代全资持股。
新公司注册资本1.2亿元，法定代表人为邹佳，注册地位于福建省宁德市福鼎市。经营范围为新材料技术研发、电子专用材料制造与销售、新型膜材料销售、电池制造、电池销售、化工产品销售等。
此外，企查查显示，10月31日，宁德时代数据科技（鄂尔多斯）有限公司成立。该公司同样由宁德时代全资持股。
新公司法定代表人为刘景江，注册资本1000万，经营范围包括云计算设备制造、云计算设备销售、云计算装备技术服务等。
央国企共同成立新能源子公司
10月27日，中煤（哈密）新能源有限责任公司成立。
企查查股东显示，该公司由中国中煤旗下中煤集团新疆能源有限公司、中国电建全资子公司中国电建集团北京勘测设计研究院有限公司共同持股，持股比例分别为95%、5%。
新公司法定代表人为于建民，注册资本为5000万元，经营范围包含风力发电技术服务、储能技术服务、太阳能发电技术服务、发电业务、输电业务、供（配）电业务等。

title: 宁德时代设立阿根廷办事处，供货1025MWh储能系统
content:
据ESS NEWS报道，宁德时代已在阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯设立商务与技术办事处，配备销售、工程与项目管理团队，支持其在阿根廷储能系统的安装与运维。
上周，宁德时代美洲区总裁Ray See、拉美区总经理Harry Lau及阿根廷业务负责人Lucas Ponce在布宜诺斯艾利斯公布了公司的战略规划。
宁德时代当前为阿根廷发电企业Central Puerto的两个储能项目供应设备，规模合计205 MW/1025 MWh。
其中，包括150 MW/750 MWh的Nuevo Puerto电站和55 MW/275 MWh的Central Costanera电站，均采用宁德时代磷酸铁锂电池，储能时长5小时，由Central Puerto在AlmaGBA储能招标中获得。
据宁德时代透露，Nuevo Puerto项目的建设进度已接近80%。Central Puerto计划在2026年底前投运其中一个项目，另一个则预计于2027年1月投入使用。Central Puerto首席执行官Fernando Bonnet表示，目前储能电池已经安装完毕，但最终投运取决于从中国采购的变压器的运抵情况。
此外，宁德时代还与Edison Energía、Newsan、Rowing等本土企业建立商业合作。
宁德时代表示，其在拉美地区获得的储能项目累计超15 GWh。截至2026年6月，宁德时代全球储能电池累计出货量已超过330 GWh。

title: 晶澳、隆基等4企获光伏组件大单
content:
近期，晶澳、隆基、晶科、三一微电网等企业光伏订单捷报不断，在国内集采、海外组件供货与EPC项目上均有斩获，持续布局澳洲、南非、赞比亚等市场，相关动态整理如下。
晶澳供货南非光伏项目及中标1GW集采
11月2日，晶澳宣布于近日被选为Sediba 120MW光伏项目独家光伏组件供应商，将为项目提供高效n型组件。
据悉，该光伏项目位于南非自由省帕里斯（Parys），项目归属Teraco，这是一家为托管服务提供运营商中立、云中立及厂商中立数据中心环境的服务商。
项目投运后，预计年发电量超过35.4GWh，计划于2026年底前投入运营。
11月3日，晶澳宣布其中标2026年南水北调集团年度集采项目。据悉，南水北调集团2026-2027年度光伏组件框架集采合计1.3GW，其中1GW TOPCon组件标段晶澳科技成功入围。
隆基签2GW澳洲光伏订单
10月30日，隆基宣布，在2026澳大利亚国际能源展展会期间，与澳新地区多家合作伙伴接连达成战略合作签约，锁定2GW组件合作规模。
隆基与澳大利亚独家分销合作伙伴Raystech签署战略合作备忘录，双方合作从传统组件分销，拓展至电站开发、AIDC（人工智能数据中心）综合能源解决方案等新兴业务，合作模式由单纯贸易升级为大型能源项目联合开发。双方锁定2027至2029年合计2GW组件交付目标。
此外，面向新西兰市场，隆基分别与Corys Electrical、Rise Energy签订战略分销合作备忘录，进一步完善新西兰本地渠道网络，巩固大洋洲整体市场布局。
晶科组件中标1GW海光集采及5GW框采
10月30日，晶科能源宣布，其飞虎3光伏组件近日成功中标上海新能源2026—2027年度光伏组件框架协议采购项目。
据悉，该框架协议由申能集团下属海南申能物资有限公司发起，预估采购量1GW，采购标的为N型高效光伏组件。此次中标产品将用于申能“风光同场”海上光伏项目。
11月3日，晶科宣布，成功入围中国华电集团有限公司2026年第二批光伏组件框架招标项目。本次框架采购规模达5GW，晶科能源飞虎组件凭借成熟的N型技术平台与稳定的产品交付能力，成功入围。
三一微电网获赞比亚55MW光伏项目
10月31日，三一微电网宣布，已于近日与LPC正式签署赞比亚利文斯顿55MW光伏发电EPC总承包合同。该光伏项目是目前三一微电网在非洲落地的单体最大EPC项目。
据悉，项目位于赞比亚利文斯顿区域，采用三一标准化、集约化光伏系统设计，由三一微电网提供从方案设计、设备供货到并网交付的全流程EPC总承包服务。

title: 英发睿能印尼7.5GW TOPCon电池基地披露最新进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，11月2日，英发睿能披露其印尼海外制造基地的最新进展。该基地由英发睿能印尼子公司BCI运营，成立于2024年，占地面积357亩，年产能达7.5GW，主要生产N型TOPCon电池，是英发睿能首个海外制造基地。
10月29日，英发睿能印尼基地BCI在印尼雅加达举行技术发布会，首次面向印尼市场发布半片钝化、多分片及BC电池等技术。
随着印尼提高TKDN（本地含量指标）要求，并推动光伏产业链本土化，近地化电池供应及本地制造能力成为市场关注重点。英发睿能表示，印尼基地将依托7.5GW TOPCon电池产能，服务当地光伏制造及供应链需求，同时辐射东南亚、中东等市场。
目前，该公司的TOPCon电池量产效率已达27.3%，BC电池效率达28.4%，并已完成钙钛矿/BC叠层组件全流程制备。其中，TOPCon技术主要用于现有产能供应，BC电池则针对印尼分布式屋顶、外岛离网及微网等应用场景。
此外，发布会上，英发睿能与印尼太阳能组件制造商协会（APAMSI）签署谅解备忘录（MOU），双方将在本地供应、技术协同等方面开展合作。
公司官网显示，英发睿能成立于2016年，专注于光伏电池片的研发、生产和销售，在中国宜宾、天长、绵阳及印尼运营着四座制造基地。
其中，其总部所在地宜宾基地成立于2022年，年产能29GW的TOPCon电池、6GW的BC电池和14GW直拉单晶硅棒；天长基地成立于2016年，主要生产PERC光伏电池；绵阳基地成立于2025年，年产能为9GW的TOPCon光伏电池。

title: How a Czech Math Professor Reinvented Solar Eclipse Photography
content:
With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery
13 min read
Vertical
Advanced image-processing software developed by Miloslav Druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated. The techniques reveal fine details in the sun’s corona, which is white in this image. The tiny pink shapes seen along portions of the edge of the blacked-out solar disk are prominences, which are extensions of relatively cool plasma that can jut out hundreds of thousands of kilometers into space.
Miloslav Druckmüller, Shadia Habbal, and Václav Široký
The sun hangs low
over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain. But from a slope of the mountain
Pico Trigaza
, it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing.
A group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. That’s because the
began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse.
In the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. From an abandoned hut on the slope a few meters above, where the researchers have set up camp, one of the grad students emerges and nods toward the cloud formation. “Do you think it will dissolve?” he blurts out.
“It will.”
Miloslav Druckmüller
glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weather can turn quickly when the moon’s shadow suddenly pushes the temperature down. Plus, there’s no sense in riling up the grad students any more than they already are.
Miloslav Druckmüller led the design and construction of a unique optical instrument that incorporates eight astrocameras. Each is equipped with a spectral filter for sensing and recording specific emission spectra from the solar corona. Each of those spectra, in turn, is associated with a particular ionic species of iron atoms. Because the temperature needed to ionize iron varies depending on the ionic species, analyzing the locations and relative abundance of these ionic species offers valuable insights into the distribution of heat in the corona.
Václav Široký
During totality, the moon blocks the overwhelming glare of the solar disk, revealing delicate structures in the sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona. Using custom-built
telescope
systems and image-processing techniques that Druckmüller has spent decades developing, the researchers aim to gain insights into the processes in this enigmatic region that is otherwise
hard to study
. In addition to imaging the visible coronal light, the team will try to track the dispersal of superhot ions of iron into interplanetary space, which could give rare insights into the pattern of heat emanating from the corona.
And they’ll have 107 seconds to do all that.
A Mathematician’s Path to Solar Eclipse Photography
Druckmüller is a professor of
mathematics
image processing
Brno University of Technology
in the Czech Republic and a leading figure in the
Solar Wind Sherpas
, an international team that studies the sun’s corona during total eclipses. In the solar eclipse world, he is nothing short of a legend, albeit a reluctant one.
An image from Miloslav Druckmüller’s first solar-eclipse expedition, to Hungary, vividly shows Baily’s Beads. These elongated white lights along a piece of the left edge of the blacked-out solar disk are caused by beams of sunlight shining through gaps in the irregular lunar surface during the eclipse. The pink shapes are solar prominences, which are jets of plasma extending out into space and held in place by the sun’s intense magnetic field.
Miloslav Druckmüller
He photographed his first solar eclipse in 1999, in what he thought would be a one-off lark. During that eclipse, the moon’s deep shadow missed Druckmüller’s native Czechia by just a few tens of kilometers, so he chased it to Hungary with a 30-year-old
Soviet MTO 1,000-millimeter lens
. All he remembers from that day is the rush of adrenaline he felt while trying to find the sun in the sky with the lens’s minuscule field of view and keep it in focus for the two minutes of the eclipse.
He insists that he has never enjoyed any of the eclipses he has photographed. “In fact, I have never properly seen any of those eclipses. You are just watching the screens, making sure that it’s all doing what it’s supposed to do. There are so many things that can go wrong and you can’t redo it.”
A composite sequence of photographs shows the 12 August 2026 solar eclipse as seen from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain.
Václav Široký and Miloslav Druckmüller
Despite Druckmüller’s outward tranquility on this Spanish hillside, the stakes are high. Just 45 minutes ago, his group heard from their colleagues in Iceland, where viewing conditions had promised to be better than in Spain. But a vast low-pressure system had clouded the entire sky, leaving all three Iceland teams without a view.
What Solar Eclipses Reveal About the Corona
On the Pico Trigaza mountain in Spain, two postgraduate researchers used a laser to get a rough, initial alignment for the tracking mount of an optical instrument. The alignment was necessary to precisely compensate for the Earth’s motion.
Martin Šebek
The corona has been a
for centuries. Though dimmer—by a factor of a million—than the sun’s visible surface, the corona is nevertheless extremely
: about a million degrees Celsius compared to 5,500 degrees on the surface. Because the sun’s
nuclear fusion
engine churns at the star’s heart, it might seem that temperatures should fall farther from the core.
To observe the faint corona in visible light, researchers must block the sun’s ferocious glare. Specialized telescopes called
coronagraphs
do this with an opaque disk called an occulter. But because light bends around the occulter’s edges in an effect called diffraction, it must block an area much larger than that of the solar disk to prevent light from spilling over and ruining the images. But doing so means obstructing the inner part of the corona, which harbors the most important processes that underpin the puzzling phenomena of the sun’s upper atmosphere.
That’s why total eclipses matter so much to solar physicists. By sheer chance, the moon is exactly the right size and at just the right distance to completely cover the sun during a total solar eclipse. Because the moon is so far away from Earth, the view is not marred by diffraction, and the corona reveals itself nearly all the way down to the sun’s surface.
As astrocameras recorded spectral data about the sun’s corona, a laptop computer [on table, at left] displayed the phase of the eclipse.
Václav Široký
Space probes
can image the solar surface in other wavelengths, but those views have limitations, too. Spacecraft such as NASA’s
Solar Dynamics Observatory
do see the innermost parts of the corona in
extreme ultraviolet
light, explains
Shadia Habbal
, a solar physicist at the
University of Hawaii
and leader of the
Solar Wind Sherpas
project. “But it cuts off very quickly, so you don’t see its extension into space as well as we can see it in the visible emission lines” during an eclipse. “That’s the biggest advantage,” she says, of solar eclipse photography.
The European Proba-3 mission, launched in 2024, simulates total solar eclipses by flying two spacecraft in a formation 150 meters apart with one acting as an occulter and the other as the telescope. The instruments aboard that satellite, however, have limitations compared to the equipment used by the Solar Wind Sherpas team.
How Eclipse Images Sparked a Scientific Partnership
When Druckmüller developed the film from his 1999 eclipse expedition, the photographs didn’t do justice to the event’s eerie beauty. He spent countless evenings applying his expertise in numerical image processing in an attempt to re-create in his photographs the sights he witnessed in that Hungarian corn field.
It took two years, but eventually he succeeded. Where before there were dull views of the blackened lunar disk surrounded by the blunt wisps of the corona, Druckmüller revealed the subtlest details of the magnetic field lines stretching from the sun far into space. As his photographs circulated among solar physicists, invitations to eclipse expeditions began to arrive.
Solar researchers Miloslav Druckmüller and Shadia Habbal have been collaborating for two decades and 15 eclipses.
Miloslav Druckmüller
Habbal learned about the images from a Ph.D. student who had seen them at a conference presentation that didn’t credit Druckmüller. When Habbal’s team later published the images in a paper, they misattributed them to another researcher. Druckmüller found out through an astrophysicist friend. “I wrote her a rather disappointed email and she responded within 10 minutes,” Druckmüller recalls. “She really didn’t have a clue.”
The error was corrected, and within weeks, Habbal and Druckmüller began a collaboration that grew into a friendship. “Milos’s processing brings out details that nobody has seen before, and they tell you a lot about very tiny features in the corona that you don’t see otherwise,” says Habbal.
How Image Processing Reveals the Solar Corona
Capturing the corona’s delicate structures means finding a way to show its brightest and faintest features in the same image. “During the solar eclipse, the contrast between the darkest and brightest parts of the corona is enormous, possibly one to a million,” Druckmüller explains. “But a computer monitor only allows you to display a contrast ratio of one to about 800.” (Some modern monitors, particularly
ones, can deliver higher contrast ratios.)
The human eye can adjust to this enormous range of brightness, allowing an observer to see both the bright corona and the faint stars and planets that briefly emerge in the darkened sky. To bring those details together in a photograph, Druckmüller uses custom image-processing
algorithms
to combine exposures that capture different parts of that range.
Researchers Martin Šebek and Peter Urgoš make fine adjustments to the focus and alignment of the astrocameras on a key optical instrument before the 12 August solar eclipse.
Václav Široký
To create a single image, Druckmüller’s teams need to take 200 individual frames during the eclipse at exposure times ranging from 0.001 second to two seconds. The data must then be
calibrated
against a vast number of reference images to filter out noise and imperfections.
Flat fields
, which depict a uniform light background, help correct for defects caused by telescope
, dust spots, and variations in pixel sensitivity.
Dark frames
, taken with light blocked from the sensor, help correct for artifacts created by the camera’s image sensor itself. “It takes the computer more than two days to process one image,” Druckmüller says. Including the calibration data, a single finished image requires about 3,000 input frames.
Choosing a Location for Solar Eclipse Photography
Since 2008, teams directed by Habbal and Druckmüller have traveled to every total solar eclipse, spreading out across multiple locations to hedge against bad weather. About half of the teams return with usable data. For the others, it’s just a short and stressful voyage. For the 12 August eclipse, three groups deployed to Iceland and two to Spain.
The teams seek sites close to the center of the band of totality, where the moon blocks the sun for longest. In Spain, the 12 August
band of totality cut across the north of the country
; the center line of the shadow passed within 11 kilometers of Pico Trigaza, promising Druckmüller and his colleagues a precious 107 seconds of totality.
But duration is only part of the calculation. Totality on Pico Trigaza will commence 51 minutes before sunset, with the sun just 8 degrees above the horizon. That low, the rays must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere than when the sun is higher in the sky, increasing the light distortion that complicates photography. At the researchers’ camp on Pico Trigaza, 1,600 meters above sea level, the thinner air should help a bit.
An abandoned hut on the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain was spruced up so that it could serve as a home base for the research team recording the 12 August solar eclipse.
Martin Šebek
“Iceland would have been a much better place for us than Spain because the sun was higher up, some 25 degrees above the horizon,” Druckmüller says wistfully. But Iceland’s notoriously unpredictable weather made Spain an essential backup.
If you pack a van with thousands of dollars’ worth of cameras and optical gear and then set out on a 2,351-kilometer journey, you shouldn’t be surprised if you finish the trip with a few striking photographs [top]. The sleeping arrangements for the grad students at the Pico Trigaza hut [bottom] were spartan, but the views were first-rate.
Top: Martin Šebek; Bottom: Václav Široký
On the mountain, locals have spruced up a rustic, long-unused hut for the researchers, running power cables from a nearby telecommunication outpost and bringing in a water tank. Five Ph.D. students drove more than 2,000 kilometers from Brno and have spent nearly a week preparing the equipment. Druckmüller and his wife joined them two days before the eclipse. They cook on a small propane grill and sleep in sleeping bags on yoga mats. “We have plenty of space here to set up our telescopes, beautiful views, and a roof over our heads,” Druckmüller says with a grin. “It’s perfect.”
But even the best equipment and a carefully chosen site count for nothing if the clouds roll in. “So much work goes into the preparations and then, if you end up with nothing, you just feel terrible sadness,” says
Jana Hoderová
, an assistant professor of mathematics at Brno University of Technology and one of Druckmüller’s key collaborators.
As the moon continues to slide in front of the solar disk, the pesky cumulus cloud that kept everybody on edge begins to dissolve. It’s 10 minutes to totality. The relief is palpable.
Mapping the Solar Corona’s Temperature With Iron
The countdown on the computers that control the cameras has begun. The screens are now showing only a tiny orange sliver, and the evening is becoming perceptibly less bright.
Twenty astrophotography cameras, most of them drawing power from a car battery that was also buffering the cameras from any grid instabilities, are pointed at the sun. Alongside equipment capturing the corona’s visible light, the team has built an assembly of eight cameras to detect light emitted by various iron ions that arise in the corona.
Among the optical gear assembled at Pico Trigaza to capture the 12 August solar eclipse was a unique instrument designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona [at left].
Václav Široký
Those instruments looking for iron ions have been put together with resourcefulness and thrift. A colleague of Druckmüller’s laser-cut the aluminum plates holding the carefully aligned lenses in exchange “for two bottles of whisky.” The brackets and attachments were 3D-printed at Brno University of Technology. The lenses, produced for the defunct camera maker Contax, were bought at steep discounts on eBay. By far the most expensive elements are interference filters that isolate the wavelengths emitted by the iron ions.
Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still.
“That’s something nobody else in the world can do,” Druckmüller says with visible satisfaction. The unique technology, codeveloped with Habbal’s Hawaii team, has already enabled researchers to map the
distribution of temperatures across the entire corona
and to discover previously unseen structures, dubbed “smoke rings,” in the coronal
. The photographs also revealed the boundary region where the solar plasma becomes so thin that its ions stop colliding.
The optical assembly designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona is outfitted with astrocameras, each of which captures spectra from a different ionic species. To do that, each astrocamera is equipped with a spectral filter whose bandwidth is so narrow—one nanometer—that the filter appears as a mirror.
Martin Fornůsek
“Iron is the most abundant of the heavy elements that we see in the solar corona,” says Habbal. “And because the corona is so hot, the iron atoms lose electrons and get ionized. The larger the loss, the higher the temperature.”
For example, a temperature of around 1.6 million °C is necessary to produce an iron ion that has lost 12 electrons. But only 1.4 million °C is needed to strip an iron atom of 11 electrons. Once it’s in a particular electrical state, the ion retains its specific ionization, even as it travels outward with the
solar wind
. Each of those ions, whether +11 or +12, emits a different wavelength of light, allowing the researchers to map not just temperatures within the corona, but also how those iron ions spread into interplanetary space and distribute heat. Habbal and her colleagues had long been trying to image those iron ions during solar eclipses. But it wasn’t until Druckmüller entered the picture that they were able to develop the gear and the mathematical techniques to do it.
Three, Two, One…Totality
With just a minute to go to totality, the researchers begin removing protective filters from the lenses. It’s 50 minutes to sunset, and the waning sun has just begun to light up the clouds above the horizon with the first tinge of orange. Then, suddenly, the evening begins a rapid and premature descent into darkness. Along the edge of the fantastically thin solar crescent, the brilliant orange points known as
Baily’s Beads
flash and disappear—the last fragments of photospheric light visible through deep lunar valleys. As totality begins, observers remove their glasses. The hot air cools. The graduate students remain quietly and intently focused on their gear.
Druckmüller looks up from his camera toward the darkened plains. Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still. The sky is ablaze with fiery colors all along the horizon where the deep lunar shadow drops off.
burns brilliantly in the southwest, a sharp white pinpoint in the darkened sky. The sound of camera shutters suddenly fills the air. Then, as quickly as it fell, the darkness begins to recede, bid farewell with another handful of golden Baily’s Beads.
The crowd erupts in cheers. The Ph.D. students throw themselves at each other and hug like they mean it.
“The students did most of the work this time, so I actually allowed myself to really look at it,” Druckmüller says. “It was beautiful. Pico Trigaza may not have been the best for science photography, but from the aesthetic point of view, it was extraordinary.”
The 2026 solar-eclipse team at Pico Trigaza in Spain included [from left] Magdalena Šrotířová, Peter Urgoš, Martin Fornůsek, Miloslav Druckmüller, Václav Široký, and Martin Šebek.
Václav Široký
But for Druckmüller, this is just the beginning. While other eclipse chasers will race to release their images, he will take his time. He expects to publish the first
visible-light images of the corona
in about two weeks. Processing the iron-ion images, and uncovering whatever insights they may hold, will take months—maybe even a whole year.
“Probably until the next eclipse in 2027” in North Africa, Druckmüller says.
Who knows? Maybe he’ll even enjoy that one, too.

title: China Has An Iron Grip On EV Batteries. Here's America’s Plan To Break It
content:
China Has An Iron Grip On EV Batteries. Here's America’s Plan To Break It
The U.S. wants a domestic battery supply chain by 2030, but tens of billions of dollars in battery projects have already been canceled.
- The Trump administration is doubling down on building a domestic battery supply chain by 2030.
- This not only includes cell and pack production, but also extraction, refining, and making battery subcomponents in the U.S.
- Billions of dollars worth of battery projects were canceled last year.
The U.S. Department of Energy last week released a new three-step plan to localize the supply chain of batteries and reduce America’s reliance on China. The plan may not even mention electric vehicles, but the EV market could be among its biggest beneficiaries if successfully executed.
Citing data from research firm BloombergNEF, the DOE said demand for batteries would increase four fold between 2025 and 2035, from 179 gigawatt-hours to 707 GWh. The demand is expected to skyrocket across sectors including transportation, the power grid, AI data centers, consumer electronics, and drones.
While the report acknowledged that America’s battery cell and pack manufacturing had improved over the past few years, the core supply chain was still heavily reliant on imports. That means things like raw material mining and the production of a battery’s subcomponents such as anodes, cathodes, electrolytes, and separators were still largely happening overseas, mostly in China.
To fix this, DOE said a new three-step plan was necessary, and the following are its objectives:
- Mine-to-market: Establish a continuous domestic value chain by 2030.
- Discovery-to-deployment: Achieve technology and manufacturing leadership by 2035.
- Enable affordable, safe, and reliable storage applications for the American public.
In part one of this plan, the focus would be to invest in the battery supply chain. “DOE is prioritizing investments to shift from a discontinuous, import-reliant supply chain to an integrated domestic production system through the upstream (mining), midstream (refining and engineered materials), and downstream (cells, packs, and end products),” the DOE said. It added that it would focus on targeted investments in companies that specialize in extraction, recycling, refining, and equipment manufacturing.
Part two outlines developing and commercializing next-generation batteries that are right for their specific applications. “These batteries should be more affordable, longer lasting, higher performing, and less reliant on critical minerals in select market segments,” the DOE said. So think solid-state cells or more advanced versions of current lithium-ion technology. And the final part of the plan is to get them past the “valley of death,” meaning converting discoveries made in the lab into actual products people can buy.
To be clear, the Biden administration had shared similar objectives back in 2021 in far more detail with a focus on clean energy, social justice, and equitable jobs. The Trump administration’s blueprint is much thinner and instead leans on national security, the grid, humanoid robots, and the enormous power demands of AI data centers. It doesn't explicitly mention EVs, but instead says next-gen batteries would also help in the transportation sector.
It's also worth remembering that America's battery industry was surging long before that. After Trump swept to power in 2024, battery manufacturing in the U.S. took a severe hit. According to clean energy think tank E2, the U.S. canceled, closed or downsized battery projects worth $42 billion between 2022 and 2026, costing the nation over 85,000 jobs. Across the broader clean energy sector, the sum increases to $137 billion, costing over 240,000 jobs, according to the same report.
The new blueprint is still a step in the right direction, even if it is more of a continued effort. It also reflects how much the battery landscape has changed since the start of the decade. EV sales have been up and down, while demand for stationary energy storage has surged, driven by utility upgrades and AI data centers. The revised strategy accounts for that shift, and automakers could still benefit over the long term for their EV plans.

title: EVs Made Up Nearly A Third Of UK Sales As Europe's Electric Boom Continues
content:
EVs Made Up Nearly A Third Of UK Sales As Europe's Electric Boom Continues
Fully electric cars outsold gasoline and hybrid models in October, as UK EV registrations surged 54% from a year earlier.
- EVs continue to boom in Europe.
- In the UK, nearly one in three cars sold last month was battery-powered.
- Germany posted big gains as high gas prices drive demand for electric cars.
While EV sales are growing slowly in the U.S., despite the loss of federal tax incentives, they're exploding in the UK. According to UK's car industry lobby New Automotive, 49,155 new fully battery-electric vehicles (BEV) were sold in October. That's not only a massive 54% increase over last October, but it's 32% of the UK's new car market share, or almost a third.
That 32% market share also gave EVs the largest market share of any one fuel type, more than gas, diesel, or hybrids. "Almost one in three new cars sold in October was fully electric, more than any other fuel type, and electric car sales are up by more than half on last year," said Ben Nelmes, CEO at New AutoMotive. "Drivers are voting with their wallets. Every one of those new electric cars means a household spending less on running costs, and a country less exposed to the oil price shock."
There's more EV variety in the UK than there is in America. The UK has access to EVs from brands like Renault, Peugeot, Fiat, Volkswagen, Skoda, and even Chinese EVs like BYD and Jaecoo. Last month, Kia, BMW, Volkswagen, and BYD led the country's electric market. Tesla slumped after a big September.
2027 Kia EV3
Year-to-date, though, Tesla is number one, with 9.53% market share. That's up 25.4% from last year, too. Kia took second place, with 6.9% market share, and BYD came in third, with 6.8%. What's surprising is that no European EV brands were in the top three, despite being in their home continent. I'd sell a non-essential organ for a Renault 5 E-Tech, so I'm surprised to see cars like that not taking top spots in the UK.
It isn't just new EVs, either. The UK is also seeing a jump in used EVs, just like we are here. According to EV Powered, data shows that more and more UK customers are shopping for used EVs.
The run up in oil costs is driving record EV sales across Europe. BEVs took 37% share of the car market in Germany, the country's road traffic agency said, with over 94,000 vehicles sold. That's a nearly 80% increase year over year.

title: Tesla Sold FSD To Koreans Who Still Can't Use It. Now It's Facing A Complaint
content:
Data shows that 99% of Teslas imported into Korea last year can't activate Full Self-Driving, even if owners paid for the feature.
Photo by:
5:35pm ET
Korean owners allege that Tesla failed to deliver on its FSD promises.
About 80% of Teslas sold in South Korea since 2023 are ineligible to activate FSD today due to import restrictions.
A court rejected a lawsuit from 2024, but a new complaint to a regulatory agency relights the fire as an advertising issue.
Full Self-Driving
will turn 10 years old next month. Nearly four of those years have labeled FSD as an
official beta product
, and over two additional years have been under the new "
Full Self-Driving (Supervised)
" rebranding. Whatever the name, the car that is in your driveway today still can't technically drive itself without you being responsible for what happens behind the wheel.
Needless to say, some
drivers are getting impatient
—especially those who have purchased FSD for multiple cars, or have managed to pay off their car loan before getting unsupervised FSD. Now a consumer advocacy group in South Korea is firing back to demand answers and accountability.
Photo by: robot*irl/YouTube
The rollout of FSD in Korea is even more confusing that it is in the U.S. thanks to another layer of complexity: where the vehicle was manufactured.
According to
, only about 20% of the Teslas registered in South Korea—vehicles assembled in the United States—are actually eligible to enable the Full Self-Driving software. That's because those vehicles meet the U.S. Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, and a
trade agreement with the U.S.
designates those standards as acceptable to enter Korea without additional modification.
The majority of the remaining vehicles have been manufactured in China, where no agreement (or supplementary safety certification) for its FSD software exists today. Since 2023, Tesla has imported about 170,000 of these Shanghai-built cars with the volume of Chinese-built cars increasing five-fold last year alone. In fact, 99% of Teslas imported into China in 2025 were from China and ineligible to activate FSD.
A complaint being filed by Korean consumer advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty (reviewed by
) with the Korean Fair Trade Commission alleges that Tesla has still been collecting money from buyers for its FSD software for over three years, despite the software not being available to buyers due to this restriction. This meant buyers forked over as much as $6,800 for the feature, but haven't actually been able to switch it on. Some buyers instead resorted to enabling region-locked FSD via a "jailbreak," which is seen as a safety circumvention and led to owners
facing jail time or fines of up to $15,000
Things get a bit more complicated given the recent legal loss raised by dozens of Tesla owners who had their lawsuit thrown out of Korean courts just last week. According to the ruling from the Seoul Central District Court, Tesla didn't technically break its contractual obligations with the 88 owners who requested full refunds via a lawsuit filed in 2024.
The court acknowledged that Tesla's delivery of the features promised with FSD hinged on certain technical advances and regulatory approval that buyers were aware could "take considerable time to become available," according to reporting by the
South China Morning Post
. If those didn't happen, the court says that Tesla isn't in the wrong.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The complaint by Citizens United raises additional questions about the way that Tesla advertises its vehicles to consumers. And they're not the first. The KFTC confirmed to
that it launched a probe into Tesla's advertising earlier this year, but declined to comment further. Tesla didn't respond to the outlet's request for comment.
Whether or not this avenue will result in action after the court's ruling that buyers weren't entitled to a refund is unclear.

title: The 2027 Chevy Silverado EV Gets A Power Bump And A NACS Port
content:
The 2027 Chevy Silverado EV Gets A Power Bump And A NACS Port
All General Motors EVs are getting a Tesla-style charging port, but the most powerful Silverado EV gets some extra ponies, too.
- Chevrolet is boosting the power output of its most powerful electric pickup.
- All 2027 Silverado EV models now come from the factory with a NACS charging port.
- Pricing has also been increased.
Chevrolet is giving its most expensive electric pickup a power bump for the 2027 model, not that it needed it. The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss with the Max Range battery pack now puts down a whopping 750 horsepower and 775 pound-feet of torque, as reported by GM Authority.
That’s 25 hp more than the outgoing model, but it’s worth noting that the maximum output is only available when activating the Wide Open Watts (WOW) mode, which pushes every metric to the top for maximum acceleration, but isn’t intended for regular use. Chevrolet doesn’t say how much power the Silverado EV makes when the WOW mode is disabled.
Gallery: 2026 Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss
The power figures of all other Silverado EV trims stay the same, but as with all 2027 General Motors EVs, they now come from the factory with a native Tesla-style NACS charging port. This enables them to pull up to Tesla Superchargers and other NACS-equipped chargers and top up without needing an adapter.
For 2027, the electric pickup also gains a few new cameras. The Cabin Glance feature shows a live video feed of the car’s interior on the infotainment screen. Then, there’s Security Recording, which records video from the vehicle’s on-board cameras when the alarm is triggered. Last but not least, the Surround Vision Recorder acts as an on-board video security system that continuously records footage while the car is in use, much like Tesla’s Dashcam feature.
The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV is slightly more expensive than the outgoing model on all trims. The base Silverado EV Standard Range starts at $56,085 (including destination charges), $700 more than the previous model. Meanwhile, the LT and Trail Boss trims with the Extended Range battery are now $1,000 more than last year, while the top-spec Trail Boss with the Max Range battery now starts at $90,395, or $1,200 more than the 2026 model.
All Silverado EV trims come with a dual-motor, all-wheel-drive setup. The entry-level WT trim has 510 hp and 490 or 580 lb-ft of torque, depending on the battery capacity. The LT Standard Range gets 605 hp and 605 lb-ft of torque, followed by the LT Extended Range, with 645 hp and 765 lb-ft of torque. The Trail Boss Extended Range has 625 hp and 775 lb-ft of torque, and the Trail Boss Max Range pushes the power figure up to 750 hp.
Besides more power and torque, the Trail Boss also comes with a two-inch suspension lift, a more aggressive off-road body kit, 35-inch tires, four-wheel steering as standard, and some new driving modes. Despite the trail-oriented kit, the Trail Boss is the longest-range model in the lineup, with up to 478 miles on the Max Range battery.
The RST trim, which used to be the top option, has been discontinued. Production of the 2027 Chevy Silverado EV kicked off at GM’s Factory Zero in Michigan last month.

title: The Lincoln Aviator PHEV May Have Died In America, But It’s Coming Back In China
content:
The Lincoln Aviator PHEV May Have Died In America, But It’s Coming Back In China
China's MIIT has exposed the Lincoln Aviator EX8, a Changan-made PHEV made just for China.
- The Lincoln Aviator EX8 is a PHEV model made by Lincoln's Chinese joint venture partner, Changan.
- It shares nothing in common with the Lincoln Aviator PHEV, which was discontinued for 2024.
- Combustion power for the Aviator EX8 comes from a Changan-made 1.5-liter turbocharged engine.
While the Lincoln Aviator PHEV died in 2024 for most of the world, its nameplate will carry on in China. This week, China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) exposed homologation details of Lincoln’s all-new PHEV crossover, the Lincoln Aviator EX8. But while the old Aviator was a luxe version of the U.S.-designed Ford Explorer, this car is developed largely through a joint venture with one of China’s homegrown brands.
The Aviator EX8 is one of Ford China’s most recent attempts at competing in China’s fierce new energy vehicle (NEV) market. About a year ago, Ford released the Bronco New Energy, a Kia EV9-sized EREV and full EV crossover developed with and made by Ford’s joint venture partner, JMC. This Aviator feels similar in concept; however, it is made by Ford’s other joint venture partner, Changan. Changan Ford produces many Chinese-market versions of Ford combustion vehicles we are familiar with, like the Ford Escape. It also produces the U.S. market versions of the Lincoln Corsair and Nautilus.
Dimensionally, the Aviator EX8 is roughly the same size as the old Aviator, but its powertrain feels like it should be more competitive in China’s market. Instead of a V6 turbo engine, the car uses a Changan-made 1.5-liter turbocharged engine good for 148 horsepower. However, the MIIT filing has not revealed the Aviator’s electric motor setup or output, nor has it revealed the battery size and range the EX8 will have. It also has roof-mounted lidar, so I expect some level of advanced driver-assist features to be present when this car launches.
I find the Aviator EX8 to be handsome, even in the unflattering patent-style photos of China’s MIIT. It’s boxy, yet still adorned with a remarkable level of exterior finishing. The wheel choices suit the crossover’s style well; it looks big and expensive, just like a Lincoln should. In all, it looks like a shrunken version of the Lincoln Navigator. If it has a similar interior to what we’ve seen from Lincoln’s other models, then the Aviator EX8 could be a compelling PHEV entry.
And it needs to be compelling, because Lincoln’s Chinese presence is very limited, while competition is hot. For starters, Lincoln has no NEV in China. It used to sell the Corsair PHEV, but it was discontinued when the model was facelifted for 2026. If Lincoln wants to continue to sell cars in China, it needs products that are better marketed to Chinese buyers. In China, this car will face a large number of midsize PHEV or EREV competitors, some of which we’ve got our hands on, like the Lynk & Co 08.
There’s very little chance the Aviator EX8 will exit China and enter our market. Even though Lincoln is importing cars to the U.S., it plans to discontinue the China-made Nautilus and Corsair by 2030 and make more vehicles here. Also, given its development with Changan, it likely would not be compliant with the U.S. connected cars ban.

title: This Startup Wants To Turn Teslas Into Anything, From 11-Seat Minibuses To Pickups
content:
The Hoffman Badger made its debut at this year’s SEMA show, driving all the way from Wisconsin to Las Vegas.
Photo by:
Hoffman EV
6:10am ET
A Wisconsin startup wants to turn old or wrecked Tesla EVs into pretty much anything.
The Hoffman Badger made its debut at the SEMA show in Las Vegas as a minibus.
Sales are expected to start next year, with prices slotting between the Slate Truck and Tesla Cybertruck.
The slightly dorky vehicle you see here can use
Tesla’s Superchargers
and so-called Full-Self Driving (Supervised) driver assistance system. And no, your eyes are not deceiving you—this is not a Tesla. At least, not at first glance.
It’s called the Hoffman Badger, and it’s the creation of a small Wisconsin startup that wants to turn old
EVs into pretty much any type of vehicle. The first Badger made its debut at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas, driving on its own wheels all the way from its home base and using Superchargers along the way, just like any Tesla would.
Hoffman says it uses all of the hardware and software from the donor vehicle, which can be either the
. The seats, dashboard, steering wheel, motors, and even the door handles are lifted from Tesla. Then, they’re installed in a new chassis that puts the high-voltage battery pack one and a half inches higher than in the original vehicles. This, along with the eight-inch ground clearance, improves the boxy EV’s breakover angle, making it better suited for rough roads.
The startup says it can build around 100 units per year, but exact details haven’t been ironed out yet. In an
Out of Spec Review
video, Geoffrey Hoffman, the company’s founder, said that he doesn’t have a precise plan for the short term, but that attending SEMA will help in identifying what people actually want.
Hoffman expects the pricing to be somewhere between the
Slate Truck
Tesla Cybertruck
, so from $26,400 all the way up to $77,000, if the base dual-motor Cybertruck is the upper target.
These are the body styles that Hoffman EV claims will be possible for the Badger.
Photo by: Hoffman EV
The doors, the roof, and most of the seats are removable, and the vehicle is titled as an 11-seat bus. All of the structure and body parts are powder-coated aluminum, while the exposed fasteners are stainless steel or steel coated with 1,000-hour salt spray resistance. Inside, the fasteners are stainless or zinc-plated steel. All of the new materials are recycled, except for a few small 3D-printed parts.
If and when sales eventually kick off, the Badger will be available as a ready-made vehicle with whatever top hat the customer wants, or as a kit with a VIN. In the latter case, the customer will have to source a donor Tesla Model 3 or Model Y.
There’s no estimated range, but seeing how it’s shaped like a brick, it will most likely be less than the donor car’s original figure. That said, Hoffman said that its boxy EV may deliver more range around town compared to the Model 3 or Model Y, simply because the Badger is lighter. In the first quarter of 2027, the aerodynamics will be improved, according to the startup.
Hoffman’s main business is converting old British cars to electric. Its portfolio includes the DeLorean DMC-12, the classic Volkswagen Beetle, classic Land Rovers, and vintage Rolls-Royce and Bentley models.

title: Uber Wants Thousands Of Robotaxis By 2027. Waymo Is Already There
content:
In its quarterly earnings call, Uber said its putting $10 billion into driverless cars.
Photo by:
4:27pm ET
Uber has racked up a
ton of autonomous vehicle partnerships
, attempting to position itself as the key platform for driverless rides. And the company has no plans to slow down. On Tuesday, Uber said it wants to spend $10 billion to get 2,000 robotaxis into its global fleet by the end of 2027.
"Our autonomous strategy is entering an important new phase as more of our partners move from development and testing into driverless commercial service," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in written remarks shared alongside the company's third-quarter earnings.
Around half of those 2,000 robotaxis will be for the United States market, Uber said. The other half will be split up between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Uber says the self-driving fleet at that point will span 20 cities and include partnerships with May Mobility, Momenta, Zoox, Motional, and others. By the end of this year, Uber plans to have 700 robotaxis on its platform.
Photo by: Waymo
Here's the kicker, though: Even if Uber hits its goal by 2027, it will still be far behind Waymo, which is both a major competitor and, for now, a partner. Waymo, the most prominent robotaxi company in the world, already has a fleet of around 4,000 cars currently on the road, and it currently operates in 15 different U.S. cities.
Waymo aims to double its robotaxi count to 8,000 by the end of the year and hit 20,000 vehicles by the close of 2027,
reported recently. So Uber would still be playing catch-up, big time.
And while users in cities like Atlanta have to use the Uber app to call a Waymo robotaxi, that's changing. Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told
Bloomberg
on Wednesday that the company plans to end its exclusivity deal with Uber in Austin and Atlanta in January of 2028. It was “
a little bit of a crapshoot,
” she said, since Uber customers never knew if they were getting a robotaxi or a human driver.
Uber said its partners have committed to bringing 120,000 robotaxis onto its platform in the coming years, but hasn't put a timeframe on such a lofty goal. It says it's going to fund this fleet of robotaxis with its own earnings, but that it might have to “bring in third-party capital," once its self-driving fleet expands beyond 10,000 cars. Uber claims its gross bookings were up 20%, year-over-year, to the tune of $59.8 billion, so it's got a big book of business to fund its future projects. But with it splitting from Waymo, it's never been more important for the company to get its other partnership projects off the ground and expand them quickly.

title: VW And Skoda EV Owners Have Waited Years For Battery Preconditioning. It's Finally Coming
content:
VW And Skoda EV Owners Have Waited Years For Battery Preconditioning. It's Finally Coming
The two automakers are launching an over-the-air software update for the oldest Enyaq, ID.4, and ID.5 EVs on the road.
- Volkswagen and Skoda are adding a much-needed battery pre-heating feature to the oldest ID.4, ID.5, and Enyaq EVs on the road.
- Over 200,000 cars will get an over-the-air software update starting in the second half of November, 2027.
- The update will be rolled out in stages, and there are some prerequisites to keep in mind.
The first Volkswagen ID.4 and Skoda Enyaq electric crossovers to roll off the assembly lines back in 2020 marked a big step for the two automakers, but owners quickly faced an uncomfortable truth: their high-voltage batteries could not be preconditioned for fast charging, which resulted in longer-than-expected charging times during cold weather.
That’s no longer the case, though, as both Skoda and Volkswagen are releasing a new over-the-air software update that adds the long-awaited feature to the oldest Enyaq, ID.4, and ID.5 EVs on the road, manufactured from 2020 to 2024. From 2024 onward, all three models came with an automatic battery preconditioning feature, so they don’t need improvements in this area.
In the Skoda Enyaq’s case, software version 3.9 adds the battery pre-heating function, as well as an updated welcome screen that no longer needs user confirmation to boot up completely. Various security updates and a software fix for the Online Connectivity Unit (OCU) are also included.
Roughly 200,000 Enyaq EVs are scheduled to get the update, with the rollout happening in waves. The first cars will receive the new feature starting in the second half of November, followed by another wave two weeks later.
Owners of cars that have version 3.8 will be prompted to install the latest version, which happens automatically over the air. If an older version is running in the vehicle, the car will need to install version 3.8 first, which prepares the car for the battery pre-heating function, while version 3.8 introduces the function itself.
Skoda Enyaq battery preheating update
Meanwhile, cars running version 2.x will need a visit to an authorized service center to get the latest software updates that enable battery pre-conditioning.
The same improvements are also being offered to the Volkswagen ID.4 and ID.5, though the software version that includes them is 3.9.1. The latest ID. Software iteration also improves the reliability of the electric door handles and AC charging.
It’s worth noting that the new battery preconditioning feature that’s coming to older Enyaq, ID.4, and ID.5 EVs can only be manually activated on a new virtual screen in the infotainment system. What’s more, the button that turns on battery heating is only active when the battery temperature is below 68°F (20°C), according to Jiří Vlček, Skoda project manager for online updates. The new software also shows the battery’s current temperature, so drivers can easily monitor it.
Skoda engineers tested the new feature in freezing conditions.
After pressing the preconditioning button, the battery starts to gradually heat up until it reaches its optimum temperature of roughly 77°F (25°C). This can take about 30 to 40 minutes, and the automakers recommend that drivers take this into account when driving to a fast charger.
If the battery is at an optimal temperature, it can accept a higher power from a DC fast charger, shortening the time it takes to get back on the road.
„From the user’s perspective, battery pre-heating is a very simple and straightforward function, but from our perspective it requires intervention in the three most important control units of the vehicle: the vehicle control unit, the battery control unit and the infotainment system,” said Vlček. “This places enormous demands on implementation and on comprehensive testing to ensure the update functions correctly.”
Before this update, some owners had to resort to do-it-yourself methods to manually activate battery preconditioning, which involved a custom-made microcontroller or a dedicated diagnostics dongle and an OBD programming app. Now, owners can enjoy faster charging in freezing conditions without having to jerry-rig a feature that, by the looks of it, has always been possible.

title: Waymo And Uber's Robotaxi Partnership Is Ending
content:
Waymo And Uber's Robotaxi Partnership Is Ending
Waymo is planning to serve riders via its own app in Austin and Atlanta.
- Waymo is planning to serve riders via its own app in Austin and Atlanta from 2028 onwards.
- The company said the Uber partnership was a little bit of a "crapshoot."
- Both companies still have grand ambitions when it comes to autonomy.
If you want to ride in a driverless Waymo in Austin or Atlanta, you can currently only do that via the Uber app thanks to an exclusive partnership between the two companies. That will change in 2028 because Waymo has decided to go solo in those two cities.
Waymo Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg on Wednesday that the company will exit its partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta starting in January 2028. The reason? Mawakana said the Uber app doesn’t guarantee a driverless ride. You can enable autonomous rides via settings in the Uber app, but the chances of one showing up depend on how many Waymos are actually nearby. If there's no Waymo nearby, riders are matched with human drivers.
Uber says it offered to add a dedicated robotaxi ride option through its service so that customers would match with driverless cars more easily, but Waymo reportedly declined that.
“In the early days, we would partner because we didn’t have the scale,” Mawakana told the outlet. "...in that partnering, it was a little bit of a crapshoot," she added.
Customers were now demanding a more consistent experience, Mawakana said. That’s why, starting in January 2028, Waymos in Austin and Atlanta will operate the same way they’ve been operating in over two dozen other U.S. cities: via Waymo’s own dedicated app. With that, current partner Uber will also become a direct rival in those two cities.
The whole point of this partnership was to help Waymo scale and give riders exposure to its cutting-edge driverless technology. Uber is the go-to ride-hail app for millions of riders already. The company also has vast experience in fleet operations and logistics.
Waymo, by comparison, is far smaller but is growing quickly. It’s a fully-owned subsidiary of Google parent Alphabet, which is valued at over $3.5 trillion as of writing. Waymo currently conducts over 500,000 paid driverless trips each week. It’s already operational in 15 U.S. cities and plans to add over a dozen more in the coming months. It's in a comfortable lead in the robotaxi race in the U.S., far ahead of Tesla and others.
It now seems more confident about going solo in Austin and Atlanta. However, it’s still partnering with Lyft for driverless rides in Nashville, although that partnership isn’t exclusive. Waymo also serves Nashville through its own app.
Uber also has grand ambitions when it comes to robotaxis. The company plans to have 700 robotaxis online by the end of this year and 2,000 by the end of 2027. It has emerged as a broker of robotaxi technology, inking deals with several companies including Rivian, Lucid, Wayve, and others to offer their driverless vehicles on the Uber app.

title: Anthropic 绘制出全球首个包含 96 个蛋白质副本的 3D 细菌库：Claude 辅助加速研究，纯化时间从 3 天缩短至 90 分钟
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，Anthropic 今日宣布其生物学研究团队借助 Claude，首次解析出原核生物相关的 Vault（穹窿颗粒，一种囊泡状蛋白复合物）三维结构。
研究发现，一种来自噬菌体的蛋白质能够组装成完整的 Vault 颗粒，由 96 个相同蛋白质组成，总分子质量约为 9.5 兆道尔顿（MDa），包裹体积比人类细胞中的同类结构大约 25%。
IT之家注：Vault 穹窿颗粒是细胞内最大的核糖核蛋白颗粒之一，人类细胞中约含 1 万个，典型尺寸约 67 纳米长、40 纳米宽，于 1986 年首次被科学家发现，但在过去约 40 年里其生物学功能始终未知。
研究团队在约 150 亿个预测蛋白序列中搜索主要穹窿蛋白（MVP）的同源物，在 29 个细菌门和 4 个古菌门中找到了候选序列，并从中选取 44 个蛋白进行实验室测试。
实验显示，其中 7 个在大肠杆菌中表达的蛋白组装成了穹窿样颗粒，冷冻电镜确认了 4 个候选物的完整闭合结构，两个来自细菌，两个来自噬菌体。
研究团队重点解析了噬菌体来源的 L05 蛋白，结构分辨率达 3.2 埃。L05 穹窿由 96 条蛋白链组成，每条链有 7 个壁重复序列，而人类 MVP 有 9 个。L05 颗粒长 54.5 纳米、宽 47.5 纳米，外形更接近球形，内部体积比人类穹窿大约 25%。
团队进一步向 L05 中插入额外的壁重复序列，得到 L05+2 与 L05+4 变体。L05+2 的冷冻电镜结构显示，颗粒长度和宽度均增加，内部体积再增约 20%，总容积比人类穹窿大约 50%。这表明壁重复序列的数量可作为调控穹窿尺寸的工程手段。
结构分析还在 L05 内壁发现了一段未能归属的密度，计算搜索提示辅酶 A 或其衍生物是最可能的配体。人类穹窿内壁同样结合 NAD+ 等核苷酸类分子，提示穹窿的腔内面可能是结合小分子与伙伴蛋白的区域。
Claude 在此次研究中参与了蛋白搜索、DNA 序列设计、纯化流程优化与冷冻电镜数据处理。传统穹窿纯化方法约需 3 天，团队开发的尺寸排阻色谱方案将时间缩短至约 90 分钟。首个完整结构模型在 34 小时内生成，按常规分析预计需数周。
研究过程也暴露了 AI 的局限。一个实验方案中，Claude 建议的添加剂干扰了 DNA 递送，导致研究延误两周；在冷冻电镜数据处理中，Claude 跳过标准步骤后生成了不准确的结构图，团队通过更密切的监督修正了问题。
尽管结构已解析，穹窿颗粒在活细胞中的实际功能仍未被确定。原核穹窿的发现为研究组装机制提供了更易操作的实验体系，也为货物封装提供了尺寸可调的蛋白支架。L05 及其工程化变体的结构数据已存入蛋白质数据库。

title: NASA 公布 X-70 Fractal 实验飞机：探索极限机动能力，两年内首飞
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，NASA 昨日宣布，X 系列实验飞机家族迎来新成员 ——X-70 Fractal。该系列此前诞生过近 80 年前首次突破音障的贝尔 X-1，以及近年来备受关注的 X-59 静音超音速验证机。
NASA 表示，X-70 Fractal 是一个“高性能、高适应性的研究平台”，将作为新一代航空技术的试验平台，用于相关技术的开发与测试。
目前，NASA 仅公布了一张由人工智能生成的 X-70 效果图，飞机主体笼罩在烟雾和阴影之中。不过，该机构已经确认了这款飞机的多项性能指标。
X-70 将采用有人驾驶设计，巡航速度为 0.75 马赫，最高飞行高度可达 4.5 万英尺（IT之家注：约 13,716 米），作战任务航程超过 1,726 英里（约 2,778 公里）。
在载荷方面，X-70 最多可搭载 2,000 磅（约 907.2 千克）的实验设备，这些设备既可以安装在机身内部，也可以挂载在机身外部。
此外，X-70 还将配备先进的飞行控制技术，能够快速重新配置飞行控制系统。NASA 希望借此探索有人驾驶飞机此前从未展示过的机动能力。
NASA 局长贾里德 · 艾萨克曼（Jared Isaacman）表示：“X-70 Fractal 为 NASA 提供了一个高性能有人驾驶平台，可以在真实飞行环境中测试先进的飞行控制技术、机动能力以及其他前沿技术。”
他还表示，X-70 采用模块化设计，能够快速更换机身内部和外部的任务载荷。这种设计可以让科研团队持续开展飞行测试、积累数据，并迅速从一项实验转向下一项实验。
NASA 预计，X-70 将在未来两年内以 NASA 名义完成首次飞行。艾萨克曼表示，X-70 只是 NASA 航空研究新阶段的一部分。

title: NASA 阿尔忒弥斯二号发射“击穿”电离层，引发 GPS 定位扰动
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，一项最新研究发现，NASA 于 2026 年 4 月发射的阿尔忒弥斯 2 号（Artemis II）载人绕月任务，对地球电离层造成了显著扰动，可能引发局部地区短暂的 GPS 定位误差。
IT之家注意到，这项研究由中国台湾成功大学（National Cheng Kung University）的一组研究人员完成。研究团队分析了多个高精度地面固定式 GPS 接收站网络的数据。这些接收站被美国科研机构用于监测地震发生前地球构造板块的微小位移。通过测量 GPS 信号从太空传输至地面接收站所需的时间，研究人员得以还原阿尔忒弥斯 2 号任务中的太空发射系统（SLS）火箭飞过时，如何改变电离层中的自由电子浓度。电离层是地球大气层中带电的区域，位于海拔约 50 公里以上的高空。
测量结果显示，阿尔忒弥斯 2 号发射时产生的强大推力所引发的电离层扰动，比迄今其他火箭发射造成的扰动更加显著，强度最高可达 SpaceX 星舰（Starship）试飞后观测到的扰动的 10 倍。值得注意的是，根据起飞推力计算，星舰的动力是 SLS 火箭的两倍。
阿尔忒弥斯 2 号任务让人类时隔 50 多年再次进入月球空间。NASA 希望这项任务能够为后续载人登月铺平道路，并最终实现人类在月球建立长期驻留基地的目标。
在火箭发射过程中，地面 GPS 接收站检测到电离层电子密度发生变化，其影响相当于造成数米的定位误差。成功大学地球科学教授、论文共同作者 Charles Lin 表示，这种精度偏差足以让自动驾驶汽车偏离预定路线，甚至可能引发交通事故。
Charles Lin 向 Space.com 表示：“两米左右的定位误差，就足以导致自动驾驶汽车改变车道。这不仅可能对自动驾驶汽车产生重大影响，也会影响无人机的定位。”
GPS 接收器通过测量自身与 4 颗不同 GPS 卫星之间的距离，确定设备在地球表面任意时刻的位置。当高层大气中的自由电子浓度发生变化时，例如遭遇太阳风暴或火箭飞过之后，卫星信号抵达地面的速度就会加快或减慢，最终导致测量结果出现偏差。
美国 GPS 星座以及其他全球卫星导航系统（GNSS）的卫星，通常运行在距离地面约 2.02 万公里的轨道上，远高于电离层的顶部。因此，这些卫星发射的定位、导航和授时信号在抵达地面之前，必须穿过这一变化剧烈的大气层。
强烈的太阳风暴会将来自太阳的带电粒子能量注入地球大气层，导致 GPS 信号受到干扰，持续时间甚至可能长达数天。相比之下，火箭发射造成的影响要短暂得多。这种扰动主要由火箭箭体以超音速穿过高空大气层引发。火箭向上飞行时会产生冲击波，仿佛在电离层中直接打出一个空洞。
研究人员在阿尔忒弥斯 2 号发射后观测到了两个这样的空洞。其中一个由长约 65 米的 SLS 芯级火箭留下，另一个则由火箭上面级随后进行的两次发动机点火造成。在这两种情况下，形成的空洞都从美国东海岸延伸至西海岸，横跨整个北美大陆，长度约达 5000 公里，犹如两条巨大的飞机尾迹。
尽管 SLS 芯级火箭的动力十分强劲，但相比之下，第二级火箭在电离层内部点火造成的扰动更加明显。
这两次点火发生在火箭发射一小时多之后，地点位于海拔约 185 公里的高空。通过这两次点火，猎户座（Orion）载人飞船成功摆脱地球引力，踏上飞往月球的旅程。
Charles Lin 表示：“从地面向太空发射火箭，通常会产生这类影响，但在星际任务中进行轨道机动并造成这种扰动，此前我们还从未观测到过。未来，随着越来越多的任务前往月球和火星，这类空间天气效应将变得更加显著。”
这项研究目前已作为预印本发表于《地球物理研究快报》（Geophysical Research Letters）期刊。

title: 中国科大发布开源 RNA 序列基础模型 structRFM，成果登上 Nature
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，中国科学技术大学（中国科大）今日官宣，该校医学影像智能与机器人（MIRACLE）实验室周少华教授、熊鹏特任研究员团队发布一款开源 RNA 序列基础模型 structRFM，提高了模型在 RNA 结构预测与功能推断一系列下游任务中的性能，有望助力人工智能驱动的科学研究、生物学机制理解、药物发现等。
11 月 5 日凌晨，相关研究成果发表于国际学术期刊《自然》（Nature）。
这是 2026 年至今，中国科大以第一署名及通讯单位在 Nature、Science、Cell 三大国际顶尖刊物上发表的第 16 篇成果。
RNA（ribonucleic acid，核糖核酸）是一种重要的生物大分子，存在于生物细胞以及部分病毒、类病毒中，广泛参与蛋白质合成、基因表达调控和 RNA 剪接等生命过程，其功能与序列、折叠结构密切相关。
RNA 分子通过碱基配对形成二级结构，并进一步折叠为三维构象，这些结构影响着分子的生物学活性及其与其他分子的相互作用。因此，理解序列、结构与功能之间的联系，是揭示 RNA 生物学机制的重要基础，也是药物发现的支撑要素。
随着测序技术的发展，研究者积累了海量 RNA 序列数据。借鉴自然语言处理中的预训练方法，RNA 基础模型能够从这些数据中学习序列规律，提取可用于不同任务的通用特征，为结构预测和功能分析提供支持。
此次研究旨在将结构知识融入大规模序列学习，同时保持模型在不同结构与功能任务中的适应性和泛化能力。研究团队研发了 RNA 基础模型 structRFM，首先构建了约 2100 万条经计算注释的序列-二级结构的配对数据。在此基础上，设计算法同时预训练学习序列上下文与结构依赖。预训练后的模型仅需输入序列，即可提取序列级、核苷酸级和核苷酸对级特征，用于多种结构与功能推断任务，并在多项任务中达到国际前沿水平。
实验显示，structRFM 在零样本同源性分类中表现良好，并提高了二级结构预测性能；将其特征融入三级结构预测模型后，也改善了三维结构及其对应二级结构的预测结果。在功能推断方面，模型支持剪接位点预测、内部核糖体进入位点识别和非编码 RNA 分类。此外，模型在新发布的 RNA 家族上保持了较好的二级结构预测表现，并通过分段策略扩展至长非编码 RNA 分类。消融实验进一步验证了结构信息的引入及掩码策略对模型性能提升的作用，为算法设计提供了实验支持。
研究人员介绍，目前，实验室已开放完整配对数据、模型权重和源代码，为研究结果的复现和相关模型的开发提供了可复用资源。
中国科大生物医学工程学院朱河勤博士为论文第一作者，周少华教授和熊鹏特任研究员为该文章共同通讯作者。

title: 从“争气弹”到“争气路”中国速度独一无二，新型陆基洲际导弹东风-61 确认列装火箭军
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，今天是我国第一枚近程地地导弹“东风一号”成功发射 66 周年，而“东风”家族升级从未止步。2025 年 9 月 3 日，纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利 80 周年阅兵，战略打击群核导弹方队中，新型陆基洲际导弹东风-61 首次公开亮相。
据央视新闻今日报道，如今，东风-61 已列装火箭军。军事评论员邵永灵表示，东风-61 从阅兵公开亮相到常态参训，节奏远快于传统洲际导弹的战斗力生成周期。
首先，这说明它亮相前已经完成研制、定型、试装与可靠性验证，技术成熟度高。
其次，体现火箭军成熟的装备配套与训练体系。东风-61 与现有指挥、通信、保障链路兼容，依托火箭军长期积累的洲际导弹组训经验，部队接装后能够快速吃透新装备，压缩战斗力生成周期，反映改革之后火箭军“核常兼备、全域慑战”建设成效显著。
另外，东风-61 常态参训意味着它进入了野外机动、阵地转换、发射流程等实战化课目训练。我国陆基核反击力量实现迭代补强，机动生存、突防打击能力得到充实。
报道还提到，从 1960 年“东风一号”腾飞，到如今“东风快递，使命必达”自信宣言，中国导弹工业用六十余年，走过了从仿制到自主、从近程到洲际、从液体到固体、从单一核威慑到核常兼备的跨越式发展之路，已形成覆盖近程、中程、远程、洲际的全射程体系，为国家安全筑起了坚不可摧的钢铁长城。
IT之家查询获悉，东风-61 陆基洲际导弹是中国研发的陆基洲际导弹，是维护国家主权、捍卫民族尊严的战略“王牌”。其采用固体燃料推进发射，可以车载机动发射，具有“小快灵”的特点。值得一提的是，机动发射可以躲避卫星侦察和地面监视，也可以在山区快速发射，有更强的生存能力，可以用于二次战略打击。

title: 全球首次展示，高通在进博会公开全球首个 6G 终端原型机
content:
感谢IT之家网友 补药吖 的线索投递！
IT之家 11 月 5 日现场消息，第九届中国国际进口博览会（进博会）今日正式在上海开幕，IT之家在进博会现场看到，高通展示了全球首个 6G 终端原型机。
这是高通连续第九年参加进博会，今年展台的重头戏，就是全球首个符合 3GPP 最新定义的 6G 终端原型机首次走出实验室，公开实物亮相。
进博局也给原型机贴上了“硬科技展品”和“全球首展”标签。该原型机已用于与中国移动、中兴通讯等中国产业伙伴的联合 6G 技术测试和互操作验证。
此外，展台还将集中呈现智能体 AI 与多元智能终端创新，包括智能体设备、最新旗舰智能手机、AI PC、智能眼镜、汽车和机器人等多元智能终端，以及 AI 影像、XR 等互动体验。
据IT之家此前报道，今年 9 月 20 日，中国移动、高通共同宣布，双方在中国移动协同创新基地基于 6G 开放众创试验装置，成功完成全球首个符合 3GPP 最新定义的 U6G 频段 6G 原型基站与终端原型对接测试，标志着 6G 关键技术从研究迈入系统化验证的新阶段。

title: 实现翻番！今年前三季度我国氢能产业总投资 287 亿元，同比增长 108%
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，今年以来，我国氢能产业快速发展，前三季度氢能产业投资实现翻番。
数据显示，今年前三季度我国氢能产业总投资 287 亿元，同比增长 108%，实现翻番。可再生能源制氢新开工项目 10 余个，新增投运产能 10 万吨。
截至目前，我国可再生能源制氢项目建成投运年产能累计超过 35 万吨，占全球产能比重超过 50％，在建项目的年产能超过 120 万吨，处于全球领先水平。IT之家附不同区域情况如下：
华北地区建成的产能最高，占到全国 45%；
其次为东北地区，占全国的 36%；
第三是西北地区，占到全国的 15%。
目前，我国可再生能源制氢中，单体项目规模水平快速提高，万吨以上项目占比接近五成。

title: 欧空局探测器新发现：火星火山或处于休眠状态，并非地质死亡
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，长期以来，科学家一直认为火星在地质活动方面已经“死亡”，但最新的探测器观测结果显示，这颗红色星球上的火山可能只是进入了休眠状态。
这意味着，火星上的奥林帕斯山（Olympus Mons）或许并非真正意义上的死火山，而是一座仍在沉睡的庞然大物。奥林帕斯山高出周围火星平原约 26 公里，是太阳系中最高的山峰。
据IT之家了解，此次观测由欧洲航天局（ESA）的“火星微量气体任务轨道器”（ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter，TGO）完成。探测器对火星阿尔巴山（Alba Mons）区域的火山裂隙进行了研究。阿尔巴山位于火星塔尔西斯（Tharsis）地区，奥林帕斯山也坐落于此。奥林帕斯山虽然是太阳系最高的火山，但其直径约 600 公里，面积相当于美国亚利桑那州；如果以地表覆盖面积计算，阿尔巴山地区才是火星上规模最大的火山区域。
TGO 在阿尔巴山区域的裂隙中发现了含有氯化氢的气体正向火星地表逸出。在地球上，这种气体也经常从岩浆喷口释放出来，其来源是地下高温岩浆。此次在火星上发现氯化氢，意味着这颗红色星球可能仍存在休眠状态的火山活动。
此前，轨道探测图像已经显示，火星上的部分火山可能在过去数百万年内仍然活跃；地震仪也探测到了火星地震活动。这些迹象都表明，火星可能仍具有火山活动能力。不过，迄今为止，科学家尚未发现明确的火山喷发或熔岩流动证据。
该研究联合负责人、波兰科学院空间研究中心科学家丹尼尔 · 梅热（Daniel Mège）在发给 Space.com 的声明中表示：“我们的研究结果表明，火星内部保留了足够的热量，能够支持其在不久前发生火山活动，甚至现在可能仍然如此。TGO 找到了关键证据，整个过程就像大海捞针一样。”
火星火山处于休眠状态的证据不断增加
梅热及其同事最初注意到火星上的异常现象，是因为他们发现，火星北半球在夏季会出现氯化氢浓度突然升高的情况。无论从时间还是地点来看，这种气体都不应该在此时出现。
通常情况下，火星北半球的氯化氢浓度会在冬季达到峰值，到了夏季则逐渐消失。这种变化与火星上的水循环和尘埃循环有关。不过，在阿尔巴山火山侧翼的裂隙区域，早夏时节会出现一种例外情况。
随后，TGO 对这一现象展开进一步观测，在阿尔巴山区域发现了一些新形成的狭窄裂隙，部分裂隙长度达数百英尺。这是火山活动存在的明显迹象。
梅热表示：“令人惊叹的是，探测器在持续沿轨道运行、监测整个火星大气层的过程中，竟然能够捕捉到来自某个可能间歇性活动源的少量气体分子。”
研究团队认为，这些气体在火星冬季从地下深处向上逸出，随后被冰层封存。到了夏季，冰层发生升华，也就是从固态直接转变为气态，原本被困住的气体随之释放，从而导致 TGO 观测到氯化氢浓度突然升高。
梅热表示：“观察这些气体渗出的空间分布后，我立即意识到，这背后可能存在某种火山活动，但我们必须拿出证据加以证明。研究中的很大一部分工作，就是排查火星大气中可能发生的所有化学过程。”
他还表示：“我们必须以严谨、审慎且富有创造性的方式，解释氯化氢为何会出现在那里。这些数据十分复杂，但也为研究提供了大量值得深入思考的线索。”
对火星生命探索意味着什么？
梅热及其同事推测，这些气体可能与火星地下的“火山管道系统”有关，其下方或许存在一个处于休眠状态的岩浆房。
这类区域可能成为未来寻找火星生命的重要目标。原因在于，过去火星上的氯化氢等岩浆气体可能更加丰富，进而形成更为浓厚的大气层和更温暖的气候环境。
这不仅可能使液态水覆盖火星表面的大片区域，还可能创造适宜微生物生存的温暖环境。当熔岩穿过火星地壳并与地下水接触时，便有可能形成适合微生物生存的温暖区域。
梅热最后表示：“在阿尔巴山区域那些气体渗出的裂隙中寻找火星生命，是非常合理的选择。如果当地的热液系统仍在活动，就可能具备微生物生存和繁衍所需的物质与能量，同时还能保护微生物免受地表恶劣且多变环境的影响。”
研究团队的这项成果已于当地时间 11 月 4 日（周三）发表在《科学进展》（Science Advances）期刊上。

title: 目标 2028 年登月：美国宇航局公布阿尔忒弥斯 Artemis 计划加速方案
content:
11 月 5 日消息，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）昨日（11 月 4 日）公布阿尔忒弥斯（Artemis）计划加速方案，明确将在 2027 年开展阿尔忒弥斯 3 号试飞，
并力争 2028 年通过阿尔忒弥斯 4 号任务将宇航员重新送上月球表面。
根据方案，阿尔忒弥斯 3 号将把 4 名宇航员送入近地轨道，执行约 14 天的飞行任务。任务期间，宇航员将乘坐“猎户座”飞船，分别与蓝色起源公司的“蓝月”着陆器测试件、SpaceX 的“星舰”3 型着陆器测试件进行交会与对接，验证未来登月所需的关键操作能力。IT之家附上相关图片如下：
美国宇航局表示，阿尔忒弥斯 3 号的硬件研制进展顺利，相关处理周期已缩短约一半。该机构还在 5 个月内自主完成了一项关键燃料管路组件的重新设计、制造和测试，成本约为此前外包方案估价的十分之一。
面向 2028 年的阿尔忒弥斯 4 号登月任务，美国宇航局将采用“猎户座”飞船与 SLS 重型火箭，并继续与 SpaceX 和蓝色起源合作开发月球着陆器。
阿尔忒弥斯 4 号登月任务中 SpaceX 任务规划
阿尔忒弥斯 4 号登月任务中蓝色起源任务规划
SpaceX 方案计划让“星舰”在地球轨道加注燃料后与“猎户座”会合，再飞往月球；蓝色起源则计划通过地球轨道转移级，将“蓝月 2 号”着陆器送至较近的月球轨道，与飞船会合后着陆。
为支持早期月面活动，美国宇航局还与 Axiom Space 合作开发更轻便的“登月服”。该服装重量约为主力宇航服的一半，将用于首次月球行走，而原有主力宇航服仍将服务未来更长、更复杂的月面任务。

title: 科学家在巴西恐龙化石中发现红细胞证据，但未发现 DNA
content:
IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，科学家在一块恐龙化石中发现了迄今为止最有力的血细胞存在证据。这块化石来自一只中等体型的肉食性恐龙，其右腿骨骼在约 1.15 亿年前的白垩纪时期形成。当时，这种恐龙曾在今天的巴西境内活动。
研究人员在阿拉塔龙（Aratasaurus museunacionali）的骨骼中发现了大量微观结构，这些结构看起来像是已经形成化石的红细胞。此外，他们还检测到了与红细胞关键组成成分有关的化学证据：一种含铁生物分子 —— 血红素。血红素与血红蛋白有关，后者正是赋予血液红色的蛋白质。
这些血细胞和血红素的相关证据，来自一只阿拉塔龙骨骼内部的血管通道。研究人员认为，这只恐龙死亡时可能处于幼年或青年阶段，年龄约为 4 岁。作为一种双足行走的恐龙，它的体长约为 3.1 米。
该研究负责人、澳大利亚珀斯科廷大学有机地球化学与同位素地球化学家克利蒂 · 格赖斯（Kliti Grice）表示：“我们并没有找到一管恐龙血液。我们看到的是古代生物留下的矿物质和分子层面的回响，而这在科学上更有研究价值。”
格赖斯说：“对我而言，最令人惊讶的是，经历了如此漫长的地质年代，我们仍然能够同时观察到这些结构，以及能够证明其生物学来源的化学证据。”
据IT之家了解，红细胞由骨髓持续生成，负责将氧气从肺部输送到身体各处的组织，再帮助组织将产生的二氧化碳运回肺部，最终通过呼吸排出体外。
与坚硬的骨骼和牙齿不同，肌肉、羽毛等软组织很少能够在化石中保存下来。而血液等体液中的细胞，在化石中更是极为罕见。
格赖斯表示：“骨骼和牙齿能够为我们提供大量有关生物解剖结构、生长过程和进化的信息。分子和细胞层面的证据，则有望进一步丰富我们对古代生物的了解。”
不过，格赖斯强调，这项研究并未发现恐龙 DNA，并提醒外界不要将此次发现解读为完整恐龙遗传物质得以保存的证据。
她表示：“DNA 等大型、包含丰富遗传信息的生物分子，其保存特性与小分子及经过化学转化的分子残留物截然不同。细胞状结构和血红素相关化学信号得以保存，并不意味着细胞中原本存在的 DNA 也留存了下来。”
持续探索分子保存的极限
研究人员还在阿拉塔龙骨骼中检测到了与胶原蛋白有关的氨基酸。不过，格赖斯指出，这并不意味着科学家已经成功提取出完整的古代蛋白质或遗传信息。胶原蛋白是一种含量丰富的结构蛋白，可以理解为支撑和连接人体组织的“骨架”。
格赖斯表示：“这项研究促使我们继续探索分子保存能力的极限，而不是简单地认定，所有生物学信息都会在经过某个时间跨度后彻底消失。”
此前，科学家报告发现的最古老 DNA，来自格陵兰岛沉积物中的动物、植物和微生物，其年代约为 200 万年前。
据该研究共同作者、巴西国家博物馆古生物学家亚历山大 · 凯尔纳（Alexander Kellner）介绍，这块阿拉塔龙化石是在巴西东北部塞阿拉州的一座石膏矿中出土的，包含部分右侧股骨、胫骨和足部骨骼。
格赖斯最后表示：“我们认为，这项研究的独特之处在于多项证据相互印证，且证据链十分有力：恐龙骨骼内部原位保存着大量类似红细胞的结构，这些结构已经矿化，位于骨骼的血管系统中，同时还存在与血红素有关的原位化学证据。据我们所知，此前还没有人在恐龙化石中以这种方式展示过如此完整的一组证据。”
这项研究于周一发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》（Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences，PNAS）上。

title: 运行近 22 年后谢幕：NASA“雨燕”天文台已坠入地球大气层，大部分部件预计烧毁
content:
11 月 5 日消息，当地时间 11 月 4 日，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）确认尼尔 · 格雷尔斯 · 斯威夫特天文台（Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory，又称“雨燕”天文台）已于当天再入地球大气层，结束近 22 年的太空观测任务。
美国太空军确认，“雨燕”天文台于美国东部时间 11 月 4 日 7 时 39 分（北京时间 11 月 4 日 20 时 39 分）在印度尼西亚北苏门答腊地区上空再入大气层，再入位置约为北纬 3.4 度、东经 98.6 度。
NASA 表示，预计“雨燕”天文台的大部分部件会在穿越大气层的过程中烧毁，但仍不能排除部分部件残骸存留并落至地面的可能性。
IT之家注：“雨燕”天文台于 2004 年 11 月发射升空，主要任务是探测和观测宇宙中的伽马射线暴。其最初设计的主要任务期限仅为两年，实际运行时间接近 22 年，远超最初的任务规划。
NASA 介绍称，“雨燕”天文台能够观测多个波段的宇宙辐射，并快速调整观测方向，捕捉持续时间较短的宇宙爆发事件。当探测到伽马射线暴等瞬态天文现象时，它还能够向其他地面及空间观测设施发送警报，协助开展后续观测。
在近 22 年的运行期间，“雨燕”天文台积累了大量观测数据，帮助科学家研究伽马射线暴及其他宇宙天体和高能天文现象，拓展了人类对宇宙中剧烈爆发现象的认识。
随着运行时间不断增加，“雨燕”天文台的轨道高度持续下降。NASA 此前曾尝试通过提升轨道高度的方式延长其运行寿命，但相关努力未能成功。最终，这座运行近 22 年的天文台再入大气层，结束了太空观测任务。
