Hanwha Power Receives ABS Approval in Principle for 1,700 TEU Battery Powered Containership Design
Fully electric propulsion design featuring approximately 151 MWh of energy storage strengthens capabilities in zero-carbon maritime transport
Integrated solution combines electric propulsion, and containerized battery energy storage systems
Expanded eco-friendly marine propulsion portfolio lays the groundwork for
entry into the next-generation zero-carbon vessel market
SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Hanwha Power announced that it had received Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for its design of a 1,700 TEU battery-powered containership.
The certificate presentation ceremony took place on October 22, local time, at the MHE (Maritime Hybrid, Electric & Hydrogen Fuel Cells) Conference & Exhibition 2026 in Bergen, Norway. Jong-kyu Hwang, Vice President, Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power, attended the ceremony alongside senior representatives from ABS. The event runs from October 21 to 23 at the Scandic Hotel Bergen City.
The newly approved design concept features a fully electric container vessel powered by a large-scale 151 MWh Energy Storage System (ESS). Electrical energy stored in containerized battery units serves as the vessel’s primary propulsion source, enabling operation without direct carbon emissions through the use of port charging infrastructure.
The use of containerized batteries, which can be handled and stowed like standard cargo containers, enhances space efficiency, maximizes cargo capacity, and optimizes overall vessel performance. This approach also supports flexible battery replacement and scalable operation, offering a practical pathway for the decarbonization of short-sea and regional container transport.
The AiP strengthens Hanwha Power’s capabilities in fully electric vessel design using large-scale battery energy storage and expands its portfolio of marine propulsion solutions. The company plans to build on this achievement to pursue opportunities in the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market.
Alongside the approval, Hanwha Power has also completed the basic design of a 1,000 TEU battery-powered container vessel. Building on its expertise in vessel design across multiple ship classes, the company aims to develop a comprehensive lineup of electric-propulsion vessels tailored to a wide range of operating conditions and customer needs.
Jong-kyu Hwang,
Vice President, Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power, said:
This AiP from ABS marks an important step in extending Hanwha Power’s marine technology capabilities to fully electric vessels powered by large-scale battery systems,
“We will address the needs of the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market with integrated solutions that combine electric propulsion and containerized battery system technologies.”

LG Energy Solution – AI Data Center Power Solutions: From BBUs and UPS Batteries to Grid-Scale BESS
LG Energy Solution showcased a battery portfolio for AI data centers at Data Centre World Asia 2026, spanning server-level BBUs, facility-level UPS batteries and grid-scale BESS.
Through the One LG AI Factory, LG Energy Solution, LG Electronics and LG CNS are combining power, cooling, construction and operational capabilities to address next-generation AI infrastructure needs.
Under the theme “End-to-End AI Factory Infrastructure Partner,” the joint booth addressed infrastructure requirements across the AIDC lifecycle. Within this ecosystem, LG Energy Solution showcased battery solutions for key power infrastructure needs, including Battery Backup Units (BBUs), Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) batteries, and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
Growing AI Workloads Increase Demand for Data Center Power Infrastructure
As AIDCs become larger and computing workloads become more intensive, reliable power infrastructure is increasingly important. Higher compute density requires systems that can support continuous operation and protect servers and critical equipment from even brief interruptions.
Battery-based solutions help meet these needs by providing immediate backup power at the server-rack level and supporting energy management across the facility and grid.
Battery Solutions for Different Power Needs: From Server Racks to the Grid
At the server level, LG Energy Solution showcased its
2170 cylindrical
battery for BBUs. Installed on power racks, BBUs can provide immediate Direct Current (DC) power to IT racks during unexpected power interruptions and help maintain stability. Customer examples and video content illustrated how these capabilities can support power stability and operational efficiency in AIDCs.
For facility-level backup power, LG Energy Solution exhibited the JP5 designed to provide high energy density within a compact footprint. The system delivers 1MW-class power in a 1m² footprint, helping address space constraints for backup power infrastructure.
The JP5 also incorporates a Self-Powered Switched-Mode Power Supply (SMPS), allowing its Battery Management System (BMS) and Battery Protection Unit (BPU) to operate independently without an external power source. Together with
UL9540A certification
, these features are designed to support the safety and reliability of backup power systems in data center environments.
At the grid level, the company presented the JF2 DC Link, an
LFP-based
, long-cell BESS designed to provide large-scale energy storage for power infrastructure supporting AIDCs. The system offers 5.0MWh-class energy capacity in a single 22.1-foot
container, with liquid-cooling thermal management and UL9540A safety certification.
The JF2 DC Link also features LG Energy Solution’s proprietary State-of-Charge (SOC) Calibration Free technology. By maintaining SOC accuracy without separate calibration, the technology supports more efficient management of large-scale energy storage systems.
In addition, LG Energy Solution promoted its JF2 AC Link through a dedicated pop-up banner. The product, targeted primarily at North American utility customers, was highlighted as meeting NVIDIA DSX Ready requirements.
Connecting Power, Cooling, and Construction Through the One LG AI Factory
LG Energy Solution’s presence at
DCWA 2026
extended beyond individual battery products. The joint booth also demonstrated the One LG AI Factory concept, which brings together LG Energy Solution’s battery and power infrastructure technologies, LG Electronics’ cooling solutions, and LG CNS’s expertise in AIDC construction and operations.
Visitors explored how gigawatt-scale AIDCs are constructed and operated through interactive dioramas, video content, and prefabricated modular AI Factory solutions that can shorten construction timelines.
Meeting AI Power Demands
As AI power demands continue to increase, AI infrastructure requires solutions across multiple layers, from server-level backup to facility-level power continuity and grid-scale energy management. The One LG AI Factory offers an integrated approach to meet power, cooling, construction and operations needs as AIDCs become larger and more complex. LG Energy Solution is committed to meeting these requirements through BBUs, UPS batteries and BESS, providing solutions across different levels of AIDC power infrastructure.

title: Switzerland - Japanese GreenTech company GSA opens a battery recycling lab in Biel/Bienne - Batteries News

Switzerland – Japanese GreenTech company GSA opens a battery recycling lab in Biel/Bienne
Japanese GreenTech company Green Science Alliance (GSA) has opened a laboratory at Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne, in the canton of Bern. The lab will develop a technology that regenerates valuable materials from used lithium-ion batteries.
Green Science Alliance (GSA)
, a Japanese chemical and GreenTech company, has opened a laboratory dedicated to next-generation battery recycling at Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne (SIPBB). Inaugurated on 19 October 2026, the lab operates in partnership with the Swiss Battery Technology Center (SBTC). GSA develops advanced materials for a more sustainable society, from biomass-based alternatives to petroleum-derived products to rechargeable batteries, fuel cells and solar cells.
Regenerating cathode materials directly
Mechanically processing used lithium-ion batteries produces a dark powder called black mass, which contains valuable electrode materials. Conventional recycling dissolves it with acids or bases to recover individual metals, which then need several more processing steps before reuse. GSA’s approach is to directly regenerate the cathode active materials so that they can go back into new batteries, without fully breaking them down into elements. This could cut recycling steps and resource use.
Early results show that batteries made with regenerated cathode materials reached over 90% of the initial capacity of comparable batteries using commercial materials. The technology is being developed for both NMC (nickel-manganese-cobalt) and LFP (lithium iron phosphate) batteries.
A partnership with SBTC
SBTC is one of the four applied research centers of SIPBB. It provides scientific expertise, infrastructure and lab space, and the joint work covers assessing regenerated materials, making electrodes and cells, testing performance, and evaluating industrial potential and scalability. The partnership is supported by an
Innosuisse
Innovation Cheque, described as a first step toward joint research.
A base for European expansion
GSA chose Biel/Bienne as its base for expanding in Europe, and plans further collaborative R&D. It aims to commercialize the technology in Europe with the help of the SIPBB network of industrial partners, start-ups and research institutions across the battery value chain. If scaled up, the method could reduce the resources needed for recycling, lessen reliance on newly mined raw materials and support more resilient European battery supply chains.

content:
Volkswagen to recall over 70,000 EVs worldwide due to faulty batteries
Volkswagen has issued a recall for nearly 72,700 electric vehicles due to faulty batteries, according to data from the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) published on Tuesday.
Some 10,000 vehicles, largely from Volkswagen’s ID line, are affected in Germany alone.
It became known last week that Volkswagen was preparing a recall, after internal quality checks found that individual high-voltage battery cells in certain ID family vehicles do not meet quality requirements. The cause is production defects at suppliers, affecting a limited production period, according to Volkswagen.
The company
said last week,
In rare cases, this can lead to increased thermal stress on these batteries; in extreme cases, a fire could break out
Models affected include the ID.3, ID.4, ID.7 and ID.Buzz from certain production periods between 2022 and 2025, as well as the Cupra Born built by Spanish subsidiary Cupra between 2022 and 2024.
Affected customers will receive a letter, the company said.
As an immediate measure, Volkswagen is limiting charging of the affected vehicles to a maximum of 80% for safety reasons, until the car is checked by a workshop. The affected battery modules might not necessarily have to be replaced, as a software update might be enough, according to Volkswagen.
This is not the company’s first recall this year over battery problems: In March, Volkswagen and Cupra had already called in more than 90,000 cars worldwide for the same reason – 28,000 of them in Germany.
At the end of September, the carmaker also called in just over 5 million cars worldwide to workshops over a corrosion-prone screw on the steering system.

title: Avicenne Energy, Li-Bridge Standardize Battery Readiness
content:
Battery Manufacturing
Battery News
Avicenne Energy and Li-Bridge teamed up with industry stakeholders to standardize how battery programs measure technical and manufacturing maturity.
November 6, 2026
5 Min Read
EV battery manufacturing
PhonlamaiPhoto/iStock / Getty Images Plus
At a Glance
Avicenne Energy and Li-Bridge created a framework to standardize TRL and MRL definitions across the battery industry.
The biggest gap: TRL 4-6, where companies struggle to scale from prototypes to automated, repeatable production.
Stellantis already uses the framework to spot gaps between technical readiness and manufacturing maturity.
Battery manufacturers love to talk about Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Levels (MRL). The problem is, they rarely mean the same thing when they do.
One company's "pilot production" is another's "pre-production," and a program that looks mature on paper might be nowhere near scalable. That gap between what a battery technology can do and what a factory can actually produce has quietly become one of the industry's biggest blind spots.
To close it, Avicenne Energy teamed up with Li-Bridge — the public-private alliance working to build a stronger domestic lithium-battery supply chain — along with a group of leading industry stakeholders. Together, they built a standardized
Readiness Assessment Framework
designed to bring order to the messy, inconsistent world of TRL and MRL definitions.
Why readiness got so confusing
TRL and MRL sound similar, but they measure very different things.
tracks how mature the technology itself is — does the chemistry work, does the cell perform, is the concept validated? It typically runs from 0 to 9.
tracks something else entirely: can that technology actually be manufactured, consistently and at scale? It usually runs from 1 to 10.
Related:
Battery Show North America 2026: Technology Highlights From the Show Floor
Here's the simplest way to think about it: TRL asks "does it work?" MRL asks "can we make it, reliably, in the volumes we need?"
A battery program can score well on TRL while its MRL lags far behind. The chemistry might be excellent in the lab, but the manufacturing process hasn't been automated, standardized, or proven at scale yet. That disconnect is exactly where many programs run into trouble — and exactly what makes a shared readiness language so important.
Battery cells for automotive industry on production line. Credit: SweetBunFactory / iStock / Getty Images Plus
The industry pressure behind the problem
A few forces are converging to make this issue harder to ignore. EV and energy storage demand keeps pushing automakers to industrialize new battery technologies faster than ever, while federal agencies are increasingly weaving MRL terminology into grants and partnerships. At the same time, startups, OEMs, and suppliers all define "readiness" differently, making cross-industry benchmarking nearly impossible — and "pilot production" has become a catch-all term that can mean wildly different things depending on who's using it.
Without a common framework, companies risk overestimating how close a program really is to commercial scale — a costly mistake when capital, timelines, and partnerships are on the line.
What the framework actually found
The project zeroed in on the critical TRL 4-6 / MRL 3-5 window — the stage where a battery program moves from early technical validation toward manufacturable, repeatable, increasingly automated production. This is where most of the industry's confusion (and risk) lives.
Related:
QuantumScape Plans 100-MWh Line to Chase AI Data-Center & Defense Markets
Working with Li-Bridge and industry input, the team built volume criteria tied to each TRL and MRL stage, mapping out exactly what "readiness" should look like at each point. A few key findings stood out:
TRL 1-3 — R&D pilot lines are everywhere.
The U.S. has plenty of facilities supporting early-stage material and cell development. They could use tighter SOPs and more standardization, but capacity isn't the issue here.
TRL 4-6 — This is the real gap.
Producing thousands of cells using standard, automated techniques is where the U.S. market falls short. This is the bridge between "it works in the lab" and "we can actually scale it" — and right now, there's a serious shortage of capacity at this stage.
TRL 7-9 — Thin, but growing.
Higher-volume pre-production capability is still limited, though private companies are increasingly stepping in to meet customer demand.
For OEMs and large manufacturers, levels beyond TRL 6 are often managed through internal systems like Stage-Gate, PSDP, or MPRQ — meaning the framework's biggest value shows up earlier in the journey, right when programs are deciding whether they're truly ready to scale.
Related:
Inside the 2026 Battery Awards, Where Innovation Took Center Stage
Framework-driven diagnostic analysis. Credit: Avicenne Energy
Choosing a path forward
Using the standardized framework creates a consistent, disciplined way to evaluate readiness across technologies, projects, and organizations. It enables clearer benchmarking, improves alignment around what “ready” actually means, and helps identify gaps earlier in the development process, when they are typically less costly and easier to address. The result is better-informed decision-making and a more structured path toward commercialization and scale.
Avicenne Energy's full case study breaks down the complete comparison between these approaches, along with the five-phase implementation roadmap used to roll the framework out.
Read the full case study here
The results so far
Stellantis is among the companies already putting the framework to work after making some adjustments to the structure to better fit its industrialization processes. The impact has been tangible: greater discipline and rigor in battery program reviews, a clearer read on where programs truly stand, and — perhaps most valuable — early visibility into the gap between what the technology can do and what the factory can actually produce.
That visibility has helped teams avoid overstating readiness and make more informed calls about when to scale.
The bigger lesson
Inconsistent definitions aren't just a semantics problem — they're a business risk. When teams, partners, and investors don't share the same readiness language, collaboration breaks down and scale-up decisions get riskier.
A common framework fixes that. It's not just useful for automakers — cell manufacturers, materials suppliers, pack and component makers, energy storage system builders, pilot line operators, equipment suppliers, and investors all face the same readiness ambiguity. Anyone trying to move a promising battery technology from the lab to the production line stands to benefit from a framework that finally draws a clear line between "it works" and "we can build it."

title: Sodium-Ion Batteries Gain Ground in Australia’s Energy Market
content:
Materials
Battery Applications
Industry Outlook
Interviews
Sodium-ion batteries are challenging LFP in Australia, with growing momentum in household storage, grid systems, safety, commercialization and future scale.
November 6, 2026
4 Min Read
Sodium-ion (Na-ion) batteries are an alternative to lithium-ion batteries.
2265191331/iStock / Getty Images Plus
Neeraj Sharma,
Director at the Australian Battery Society & Professor of Chemistry at
UNSW Sydney
, recently gave a free public talk on sodium-ion batteries at
ScienceKind
as part of its new Tuesday series, “From Atoms to Grids”. Sharma brought a true lab-bench perspective to a topic attracting growing attention across the energy industry. Following the talk,
Battery Technology
interviewed him, extending the discussion beyond the presentation to explore why sodium-ion batteries matter now and what may come next.
How does sodium-ion compare with LFP today, and where do you see its strongest advantage?
Neeraj Sharma, Director at the Australian Battery Society & Professor of Chemistry at UNSW Sydney:
Generally speaking,
sodium-ion batteries
with the current generation of components (cathodes and anodes) are comparable to LFP. They are comparable in terms of energy density and, depending on the cathode/anode choice, can be cheaper, but this does depend on the price of lithium.
Related:
ExxonMobil on Building a Competitive & Resilient North American Graphite Supply Chain
They can be discharged to 0 V and so can be safer to transport than the LFP counterparts. In my opinion, one of the key aspects for sodium-ion battery technology is to validate the lifetime of the cells and to validate this under different load conditions and under different external conditions (e.g., temperatures, etc.).
What developments are you seeing in Australia that suggest sodium-ion is gaining real momentum?
As I said in the interview with ScienceKind, sodium-ion batteries have an opportunity to displace LFP systems in household storage and grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS). That is where the opportunity lies, and we are seeing companies trying to bring these systems to market. The smaller household units are easier to commercialize, as the larger BESS tend to go for safer, tried and tested technology. We did have situations earlier in the year where guidelines and such were for lithium-ion battery systems, e.g., rebate and certification schemes, which required modification to include sodium-ion battery systems.
Battery energy storage system with solar and turbine farms. Courtesy of PhonlamaiPhoto/ iStock / Getty Images Plus.
How is Australia contributing to the progress of sodium-ion batteries right now?
We have commercial entities that are bringing sodium-ion battery systems to Australia for household-scale storage and specialised applications. There is interest in local firms adapting to this technology as well and potentially producing modules based on sodium-ion cells in-country. We have other firms investigating the viability of producing cells in Australia for specialised applications. This opens up new opportunities for growth and development.
Related:
SPE Names Three Finalists for EV Innovation Award
In terms of research and development, there are number of active research groups working electrode, electrolyte and separator materials. Research ranges from materials discovery to electrode formulations to completely new concepts in device construction. Researchers are looking at a variety of electrolytes, including traditional carbonates to ionic liquids and solid-state. Research is also engaging in understanding recycling and the impact sodium-ion batteries will have on recycling streams and value. A number of research projects are being licensed and spun out of research institutes.
Which applications do you see as the best near-term fit for sodium-ion batteries, grid storage, EVs or something else, and why?
As mentioned above, household and grid-scale storage is probably the best utilization for sodium-ion batteries. Essentially, here mass/weight and size/shape is not as much of an issue as say portable and mobility applications. Research and development is working on factors such as depth of cycling, cycling rates, cycling conditions and lifetime to understand how batteries behave under different conditions. As these discoveries and know-how become more established, uptake may increase.
Looking ahead over the next five years, what should the industry be watching most closely to judge whether sodium-ion will truly scale?
Firstly, not all lithium-ion batteries are the same; there are NMC, NCA, LFP, and LTO-based lithium-ion batteries. A similar case is true for sodium-ion systems. The lithium-ion and sodium-ion systems are evolving as well; we are seeing Si-graphite in the anode for lithium-ion batteries and different chemistries appearing for electrode components in sodium-ion systems. There will be a mix of battery chemistries for different applications, much like NMC, NCA, and LiCoO2 cathodes in lithium-ion batteries dominate the portable electronics market and LFP tends to dominate the lithium-ion battery household/grid-scale storage markets. We are likely to see a similar range of chemistries in the sodium-ion battery space for different applications.

title: Can Optical AI Cut Data Center Inference Power Use?
content:
Power is always a limiting factor for data centers, and AI inference is increasing that strain more than ever.
Lumai, an optical compute company spun out of the University of Oxford in 2021, says it can ease that pressure by using light rather than transistors to perform the core math of inference.
The company is now putting that claim to a real-world test. Lumai is deploying its Iris Nova servers in the Scaling Inference Lab, a UK facility that evaluates new AI hardware on real workloads in a live commercial setting. Iris Nova is Lumai’s first server, an optical AI accelerator built for
data center inference
, and it will be the first optical inference platform deployed in the lab.
The UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA), a government-backed R&D funding agency, supports the lab, while CommonAI CIC, a non-profit focused on collaborative AI development, operates it. Researchers will use the deployment to evaluate how optical compute performs in a commercial data center environment.
Related:
Nvidia Unveils DSX POD Amid Greenpeace Protest
The problem the hardware is designed to address is power.
“Power is the biggest challenge,” Phillip Burr, director of product at Lumai, told
Data Center Knowledge
. “Data centers have a fixed power budget, and inference demand is growing faster than the available power.”
How Optical Inference Could Ease Data Center Power Constraints
Matrix multiplication, the process of multiplying large grids of numbers together, sits at the center of AI inference. According to Burr, that is an area where optical compute can operate very efficiently.
To understand why optical hardware may have an advantage, it helps to look at how GPUs and optical systems perform that arithmetic differently.
“GPUs are silicon chips that use transistors to perform the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inference,” Burr explained. “Optical compute uses the properties of light to perform the same matrix multiplications, completing millions of operations in a single optical cycle.”
Lumai said Iris encodes numbers as light intensity and uses passive optical components, such as lenses, to perform the math. The company said the computation itself uses negligible amounts of energy, with power use rising only minimally as performance scales.
That does not mean the system abandons traditional electronic components altogether. Burr said Lumai’s architecture is hybrid: optics handle matrix multiplication, while memory, control, and nonlinear functions are performed electronically.
There are two main phases of inference, and optical compute targets one of them. Burr said the prefill phase is where the prompt and context are processed. The second phase, decode, is where the output tokens are generated.
Related:
Nvidia Unveils DSX Pod for Faster AI Data Center Builds
“Prefill is compute-bound; each model weight is reused across every token in the prompt, so arithmetic dominates,” Burr said. “This is where optical compute boosts performance.”
In practical terms, compute-bound means the speed of the arithmetic determines overall performance. A token is a small unit of text, such as a word or part of a word.
Decode works differently because tokens are generated one at a time. Burr said decode is limited by
memory bandwidth
, so faster arithmetic does not provide the same benefit. He added that model training is also not a strong fit for optical compute today, as it requires higher precision and continuous weight updates.
“GPUs remain a good fit for training and decode,” Burr said.
The Lumai Iris Nova server is designed to handle the prefill phase and leave decode to other hardware.
“Iris is designed for the prefill stage, while GPUs or other decode-optimized hardware are used for decode,” Burr said. “Moving prefill off GPUs also frees that GPU capacity for decode.”
How Iris Nova Fits into Existing Data Center Infrastructure
For operators that split inference by running prefill on Iris Nova and decode on GPUs, software is needed to route those tasks to separate hardware. That approach is known as disaggregated serving, and Burr said Iris Nova is designed to work with the frameworks that support it.
Related:
Optical PCIe Extends the Reach of AI Rack Design
“For integration, Iris works with standard software frameworks such as PyTorch, standard networking interfaces, and disaggregated inference serving frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang,” Burr said.
Whether that split pays off depends on the work a data center is handling.
“The deciding factor for an operator is how much of their compute goes to prefill,” Burr said. “Prefill dominates with long prompts and agentic workloads, where models repeatedly process large contexts. This is where optical compute delivers the most.”
Another practical consideration is facility requirements, and Burr said the hardware is built from familiar components.
“Lumai Iris servers are built from components already manufactured at high volume for data center communications, rather than novel materials or bespoke fabrication,” Burr said.
cooling requirements
are similarly conventional. The Scaling Inference Lab, where Iris Nova is being deployed, tests hardware in a live commercial setting with standard power, cooling, and rack integration, giving Lumai a trial under typical data center conditions.
“Iris Nova operates in standard air-cooled racks and does not need liquid cooling,” Burr said.
Lumai said the goal of the ARIA-backed deployment is to validate the system further and generate data to help shape its next product for production deployment.
“The ARIA deployment will put a cluster of Iris Nova servers into an independently run lab, ARIA’s Scaling Inference Lab,” Burr said. “It will show that optical compute can run real AI workloads outside a research setting, and it will provide system-level data on performance.”

title: Honda just showed off its first high-end electric mountain bike
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 7 2026 - 3:51 am PT
Honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike.
Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many
automotive-branded e-bikes
that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.
The RN0 was
jointly developed
with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.
There’s actually some real history behind that connection. Honda experimented with mountain bike development in the early 2000s, culminating in its wild RN01 downhill racing bike. In 2005, that project won the overall series championship in the UCI Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Honda never turned the RN01 into a consumer bicycle, but more than two decades later, the RN0 is effectively picking up where the company previously left off.
The roughly 24 kg (53 lb) RN0 is set up as a multi-role electric mountain bike, featuring 160 mm FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima front suspension paired with a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima rear shock. DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE wheels use a mullet setup with a 29-inch wheel up front and 27.5-inch wheel in the rear, while Shimano DEORE XT four-piston brakes handle stopping duties.
Those are some quality components, but the drivetrain may be even more interesting.
Honda is using Shimano’s new 2.3 kg drive unit, rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, paired with a sizeable 720 Wh battery.
Shimano’s AUTO ASSIST can automatically vary motor assistance based on terrain and rider input, while AUTO SHIFT handles gear changes to maintain an appropriate cadence.
There’s even an Assist Carryover function that briefly continues providing power after pedaling stops, potentially making it easier to clear rocks, roots, and other technical obstacles that normally would see the assist grind to a halt right when it is needed most.
A 2.2-inch color display is integrated directly into the top tube, and there’s USB-C charging plus Shimano app connectivity for adjusting motor settings and electronically locking the bike.
hasn’t yet announced
pricing in its release, but with a carbon chassis, Factory-level FOX suspension, XT brakes, and premium Shimano electronics, don’t expect this to be the everyman’s electric bike.
If anything, the RN0 looks much more like Honda is finally bringing its motorcycle engineering mentality back to mountain bikes – this time with a battery and motor along for the ride.

title: Yamaha’s new electric scooter takes aim at Europe’s 125cc commuters
content:
Electric Motorcycles
electric scooter
Micah Toll
| Nov 7 2026 - 4:30 am PT
Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter lineup with the new XENTER E, a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter designed specifically with European city riding in mind.
Unveiled around EICMA 2026 in Milan
alongside the new NMAX E
, the XENTER E is a high-wheel scooter riding on 16-inch wheels front and rear.
That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.
The XENTER E uses Yamaha’s new eAxle powertrain, combining the motor, controller, and reduction gearbox into a compact frame-mounted unit. The motor produces 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power and 33.3 Nm of torque, putting the scooter into Europe’s A1 license category.
Mounting the motor to the frame also means Yamaha can use a more conventional motorcycle-style swingarm rather than hanging the motor on the rear suspension like many scooters. That reduces unsprung weight and should help improve handling and ride quality.
Power is supplied from an integrated 3.5 kWh battery mounted low in the chassis. Yamaha claims 108 km (67 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, though real-world range is expected to be somewhat lower.
An 800W onboard charger can refill the battery in around 5.5 hours from a public charging station. Yamaha will also offer a cable for charging from a household outlet.
Other niceties include three riding modes, traction control, regenerative braking, a reverse mode for maneuvering at low speeds, smart-key operation, and a 5-inch TFT display. Smartphone connectivity adds navigation, battery information, maintenance reminders, and parking-location tracking.
There’s also enough underseat storage for a full-face helmet, depending on its size, plus USB-C charging and provisions for accessories such as a windscreen and 34-liter top case.
The XENTER E shares its powertrain and battery with
Yamaha’s new NMAX E
, but the high-wheel layout gives it a distinctly more European commuter flavor.
Yamaha hasn’t officially announced pricing for each market, though
early reports
It’s certainly not cheap, but the XENTER E looks like Yamaha is finally getting serious about building electric scooters that can replace its bread-and-butter 125cc urban machines, rather than simply supplement them.

title: EV Buyers Could Foot The Bill For Saving Europe’s Carmakers
content:
A new report warns that Europe’s push for homegrown batteries could add €2,100 to an EV’s cost.
Photo by:
General Motors
8:09am ET
Requiring EU-made battery cells could add €2,100 to the cost of an EV with a 60-kWh battery.
Buyers could pay more if carmakers pass on those costs.
Bruegel says protection should be temporary and give European carmakers time to build cheaper EVs.
Buying a European EV can come with a potentially expensive catch. Policymakers want more of the batteries powering Europe’s electric cars to be made locally, helping secure jobs and reduce dependence on China. But those batteries cost more to produce, and someone has to cover the difference. It will likely be the buyer.
That’s the warning in a September 22 policy brief from Brussels think tank
, which was picked up by
Euronews
. The report argues that protecting established manufacturers risks leaving consumers (and taxpayers) with the bill.
Its battery calculation is pretty straightforward. Requiring EU-made cells could raise costs from €50 to €85 per kilowatt-hour. Multiply that by 60 kWh, and it works out to €2,100. A proposed low-carbon steel requirement could add another €200. Simplifying vehicle approval, meanwhile, would save manufacturers an estimated €61 per car, according to the report.
Volkswagen Group PowerCo Battery plant in Salzgitter, Germany.
Photo by: Volkswagen
None of this is set in stone, though, and what buyers would actually end up paying depends on the final form of the rules, government subsidies, and how much of the extra cost carmakers pass on to consumers. Regardless of the details, those looking to buy at the most affordable end of the market would be hit hardest.
The pressure to protect Europe’s industry is real. EU car production has fallen 19% since 2019, while buyers purchased 2.2 million fewer new cars in 2025 than in 2019. The wider automotive sector employs around 14 million people. However, Bruegel also points to continued exports and roughly €3 billion in quarterly investment in battery and EV factories. It raises concerns that Europe is gradually losing technology, suppliers, and overseas customers.
We saw this at the Paris motor show this year
, where Chinese brands brought compelling software, luxurious gadget-filled interiors, and advanced charging technology, while European manufacturers leaned heavily on their history and design. The
Mercedes’ electric GLC
showed that Europe can fight back, but a familiar badge doesn’t sell cars as easily as it used to.
Local battery production is a hugely important component, but it’s proving difficult to set up in Europe. Northvolt’s failure, Porsche’s retreat from manufacturing at Cellforce, and shelved ACC factories show how hard it is to match China’s costs. Even batteries made in Europe often rely on equipment and know-how from Asia.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Europe’s additional duties on Chinese EVs, which can be as high as 35.3%, targeted fully electric cars while excluding
plug-in hybrids
. Bruegel points to flattening BEV imports from China while hybrid imports surge. It also cites French research that found EVs excluded from purchase subsidies suffered a 60% sales decline relative to eligible models, potentially slowing overall adoption and strongly suggesting that subsidies matter.
Bruegel says agreeing with China to temporarily limit the number of electric cars and plug-in hybrids sent to Europe could help. That would give European carmakers more time to develop cheaper EVs. The deal would have a clear end date, and restrictions could tighten if China broke it.
But with fewer Chinese cars available, they could end up costing more. Europe previously limited Japanese car imports, and Canada now limits Chinese EV imports. Both show the trade-off: protecting local carmakers can make cars more expensive for buyers.
Foreign investment can help Europe catch up, the report's authors argue. South Korean firms already own 65% of its battery cell manufacturing capacity, and Chinese companies own 55% of the capacity currently under construction. European factories need that outside expertise to function.

title: Toyota Quietly Gave The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV A Big Upgrade
content:
Toyota Quietly Gave The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV A Big Upgrade
With Tesla-style NACS ports and fast-charging capability on all trims, you can use your RAV4 PHEV like an EV.
- You may not need the gas engine on the 2027 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid all that much.
- It gets a native NACS port now located near the driver's side door.
- The RAV4 is among a handful of plug-in hybrids with fast-charging capability.
Toyota has quietly upgraded the sixth-generation RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid. All trims of the model year 2027 RAV4 PHEV now get a Tesla-style North American Charging Standard (NACS) port straight from the factory—plus fast-charging capability.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV Fast-Charging Upgrades
That’s a pretty big deal for a few key reasons. When the RAV4 PHEV launched last year, it arrived with a CCS charging port at a time when all new EVs had started transitioning to native NACS ports. At the time, only the PHEV XSE and Woodland trims could fast charge, meaning you had to pay at least a $4,000 premium for the capability.
Now that fast-charging capability expands to the full PHEV lineup, all the way down to the entry SE model, which costs $42,100. The same goes for the top-trim GR Sport. Owners can now simply drive the 2027 RAV4 PHEV to Tesla Superchargers or any of the new stations equipped with NACS cables. It will charge at maximum rate of 50 kilowatts, enough to go from 10-80% in just 30 minutes.
Moreover, not many PHEVs get fast-charging capability, let alone native NACS ports. The RAV4 PHEV is now the first and only major PHEV in the U.S. to transition to the NACS port, joining the wave of new fully electric models doing the same.
Some other notable PHEVs that have fast-charging capability include the Mercedes GLC 350e which gets a CCS port and the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV which gets the outdated CHAdeMO connector.
Gallery: 2026 Toyota RAV4 PHEV
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV Home Charging Capability
If owners are used to plugging-in at home, they can continue to do so. The RAV4 PHEV gets an onboard AC charger for Level 1 and Level 2 charging. And home charging can now be faster as well, with GR Sport and SE trims getting 11 kW AC charging, up from 7 kW before. The XSE and Woodland were already rated for 11 kW since last year.
And the one final notable upgrade is that the charging port is now located near the driver’s side door—it was previously at the passenger’s side. This could be useful depending on how you park at home and where you live, since there’s no industry standard for the charging port location.
The newer V4 Tesla Superchargers, as well as Ionna, Walmart, and pretty much every major new station have long cables with well-engineered retraction systems, so the location of the port shouldn’t be a problem. The older V3 Tesla Superchargers will be a challenge since they were designed for rear left ports.
The RAV4 PHEV gets up to 52 miles of EPA range from its 22.7 kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery. If you regularly plug it in, you can cover your everyday driving needs using battery power alone and use the gas engine for longer trips. And now, it looks like that charging experience just got a little better.

content:

Anthropic 宣传称，月费 100 美元

分别是 Pro 套餐的 5 倍和 20 倍
。但今年 6 月提起诉讼的消费者指控，如果按整周计算，实际额度
远远达不到宣传中的倍数
两名原告卡尔 · 卡恩和所罗门 · 史密斯计算发现，以 Claude 的一款模型为例，200 美元
（现汇率约合 1,337 元人民币）
只有 Pro 套餐的 6 倍

则为 3.5 倍

title: GitHub 推出新 Git 存储架构：内部测试单个代码仓库支持 5000 个智能体同时协作，每秒处理 7200 次推送
content:
感谢IT之家网友
11 月 7 日消息，当地时间 11 月 5 日，GitHub 发布博文，称上周在 GitHub Universe 大会上，正式公布了全新的 Git 存储架构，代号“Rubicon”。
官方表示，该架构不仅具备每秒处理数千次写入的能力，还能实现读取按需水平扩展。经内部压力测试验证，新架构能够在保持极低读取延迟的同时，
支持单个代码仓库容纳 5000 个智能体（Agent）并发协作，并承受每秒高达 7200 次的代码推送
IT之家获悉，该架构目前已经开启
小范围定向内测（limited private preview）
明年初逐步扩大开放范围
据介绍，如今 GitHub 上最繁忙的代码仓库，其单秒写入峰值最多也不过数十次，且往往呈现短暂脉冲式的突发状态。然而，随着越来越多的研发工作交由全天候高并发运行的 AI 智能体处理，预计在未来一年内，这种瞬时突发将演变为常态化的持续高吞吐负载。
每一次代码推送（Push）都会级联触发更多的读取请求：CI 流水线即刻启动、部署系统拉取最新提交，其他协同智能体也会同步获取代码作为上下文。这种读操作的扇出扩散（Read Fan-out），随着写入频率的攀升，对平台整体流量产生了极为显著的放大效应。
在流量分布曲线最顶端的头部仓库中，这一趋势已然显现。下方图表展示了 GitHub 上某个典型代码仓库在 3 月至 5 月期间的日请求量变化 —— 短短两个月内，其流量便激增了约 4 倍；此后至今，其访问增长更始终维持着陡峭的指数级上升轨迹。

title: 体检辐射会伤身吗？央视科普：常规项目剂量均在安全范围内、空腹不等于禁水
content:
IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，每年体检季，有很多跟体检相关的谣言，比如，有人说体检影像检查存在辐射，会危害身体健康。对此，央视新闻今日针对两类常见误区给出医学科普。
首都医科大学附属北京世纪坛医院健康管理中心副主任杨磊解释称，年度体检中的普通 X 光、胸部低剂量 CT 等常规影像项目辐射剂量均较低，符合国家安全标准，无需过度焦虑。
影像检查按辐射性质可分为两类 —— 核磁共振与 B 超，但它们均不会产生电离辐射，适用人群广泛，老人、儿童、孕妇均可安全检查。
其中，核磁共振用于排查脑梗、脑肿瘤、关节软骨与软组织损伤；B 超主要覆盖肝胆胰脾、甲状腺、乳腺、泌尿系统及孕期常规检查。
产生电离辐射的检查中，剂量差异显著。骨密度检测单次约 0.001 至 0.01 毫希沃特，胸部 X 光单次 0.02 至 0.1 毫希沃特。
作为参照，人体每年接受的天然本底辐射全球平均约 2.4 毫希沃特（IT之家注：天然本底辐射来自宇宙射线、土壤与建筑材料中的放射性核素等，是日常生活中无法避免的辐射来源）。低剂量肺 CT 单次约 1 至 2 毫希沃特，是肺结节早筛与肺癌早期诊断的核心手段；增强 CT 单次约 10 至 15 毫希沃特，主要用于血管病变、肿瘤分期与疑难病变确诊，不作为常规体检项目。PET-CT 剂量更高，一般仅用于肿瘤患者的全身分期、转移灶排查与疗效评估，需专科医生评估后开展。
另外，民众对于体检检查前空腹要求的误区同样常见。医学上的空腹指禁食 8 至 12 小时，饮水并非完全禁止，体检前可饮用 100 毫升以内的少量白开水，不会稀释血液或影响化验结果。
经过一夜睡眠，人体血液相对黏稠，完全禁水反而加重血液浓缩，对老年人及高血压、高血脂人群可能增加心脑血管风险。茶水、咖啡、饮料、豆浆与糖水则不在允许之列。
用药方面，高血压、冠心病、哮喘等慢性病患者体检当天无需停药，可在体检前一小时用少量白开水送服常规药物，以保持指标平稳。糖尿病患者应暂时停用降糖药，待采血、B 超等空腹项目结束后、准备进食时恢复常规用药。
首都医科大学宣武医院健康管理科主任褚熙表示，体检前少量白开水一般不影响常规体检，体检的目的是反映身体的真实状态，从容、科学体检才能实现有效健康筛查。
医务人员同时建议错峰体检，每年 12 月至次年 3 月通常为淡季，流程更从容；目前体检机构普遍实行分时段预约，按预约时间到场即可，无需刻意赶早。

title: 全新里程碑：全国首个非侵入式脑机接口项目完成 818 号令备案
content:
感谢IT之家网友
11 月 7 日消息，11 月 4 日，由天津大学脑机交互与人机共融海河实验室（以下简称“实验室”）团队研发，依托天津市环湖医院开展临床工作，燧世（天津）智能科技有限公司、北京品驰医疗设备股份有限公司协同制备的《SCS 联合无创脑控混动外骨骼训练治疗慢性卒中下肢运动障碍的安全性与可行性探索研究》项目，
正式完成国家生物医学新技术临床研究 818 号令备案
IT之家注：国务院第 818 号令《生物医学新技术临床研究和临床转化应用管理条例》（以下简称《条例》），
是我国第一部专门规范生物医学前沿技术临床研究与转化应用的国家行政法规
官方表示，该项目是自 2026 年 5 月《条例》施行后，
全国首个完成备案的非侵入式脑机接口生物医学新技术临床研究项目
，标志着中国非侵入式脑机接口前沿技术正式迈入规范化研究新阶段，
项目所使用的核心设备，为脑机海河实验室团队牵头研发国际首个脑-机-脊-体高性能复合神经调控康复系统“神工-神驰”，
主要用于慢性卒中下肢运动障碍平台期患者的神经康复干预治疗
据介绍，脑机接口技术凭借解码大脑运动意图实现主动康复的独特优势，是神经康复领域的前沿热点；同时，脊髓电刺激（SCS）具有非破坏性、可逆、可调节、作用直接等特色。
团队跳出传统单一脑控外骨骼的技术路径，融合
无创脑机接口、脊髓电刺激、混合驱动外骨骼
三大技术，通过解码患者大脑运动想象意念，结合脊髓电刺激对脊髓环路进行的兴奋性调控，混动外骨骼配合胫骨前肌功能性电刺激完成下肢步态执行，完整搭建起“
大脑驱动-脊髓传导-外周执行
”全链条复合调控环路，定向诱导人体自身神经可塑性重建，真正实现从“机器带动人被动走路”，向“
意念驱动自身神经通路重建
的主动康复模式转变

title: 刷新算力巅峰：IBM 在美国芝加哥揭幕其最强量子计算机
content:
感谢IT之家网友
11 月 7 日消息，IBM 昨日（11 月 6 日）发布联合公告，宣布携手芝加哥大学、美国伊利诺伊州政府、以及伊利诺伊量子与微电子园（IQMP），
已在芝加哥海德公园实验室投运 IBM Quantum System Two 量子计算机。
这是 IBM 在伊利诺伊州部署的首台量子计算机，也是该公司当前最先进的量子计算系统，其核心为 IBM Quantum Nighthawk 芯片，被 IBM 称为迄今打造的最强大量子芯片。
Nighthawk 是 IBM 于 2025 年发布的超导量子处理器系列，芝加哥部署的是其第二代版本 Nighthawk r2。IBM 将其称为“迄今最强大的量子芯片”，综合了最高的电路复杂度、连接性和运行速度，并引入独立高速量子比特复位架构。
每个量子比特可独立、快速复位，使系统能以每秒超过 10 万次的速率执行电路，从而显著提升科研和工业用户在相同时间内可完成的实验与计算量。
该系统由芝加哥大学托管，未来将迁入正在建设的伊利诺伊量子与微电子园，并成为国家量子算法中心（NQAC）的核心计算平台。该中心由伊利诺伊州政府于 2024 年设立，IBM 为主要合作方，旨在联合高校、国家实验室、初创企业和产业界，开发下一代量子算法及实际应用。
新系统将面向药物研发、电网优化、材料模拟、高能物理等计算密集型领域开放合作。IBM 称，伊利诺伊州的科研机构与企业已开始围绕量子计算如何扩展至复杂现实问题展开研究。
其中，芝加哥大学与 IBM 的联合团队此前曾利用 70 个逻辑量子比特，在约 15 分钟内完成一项结构化计算任务，展示了超越传统经典模拟方法的潜力。
IBM 董事长兼首席执行官阿尔温德 · 克里希纳表示，新系统已能为伊利诺伊州及更广泛地区的机构提供具有科学价值的研究成果，其落地标志着该州量子社区的重要里程碑。IT之家附上相关截图如下：
伊利诺伊州州长 JB· 普利兹克则称，这一部署将为研究人员和企业提供把构想转化为现实解决方案的工具，并带动本地高质量就业。

title: 千公里信号单程传输仅 3.43 毫秒！我国新一代通信网技术取得新突破
content:
11 月 7 日消息，据央视新闻报道，近日，我国完成全球首个千公里空芯光纤双向实时传输验证。这意味着我国在新一代通信网关键技术领域取得新的突破。
技术人员透露，此次试验在 1007.48 公里的光纤线路上，首次实现了双向各 64Tb 每秒的信号同步传输，相当于
支持每秒 160 部 4K 电影的上传和下载（每部按 50GB 计算）
，千公里信号单程传输只需 3.43 毫秒，创造了空芯光纤实时传输距离的新纪录。
这种技术比当前性能最好的实芯光纤
传输容量提升一倍，传输距离提升 60%
。和同类空芯光纤传输试验相比，这次验证的传输距离提升了 50 倍。
在气体中传送信号
的特性，空芯光纤相比传统实芯光纤时延能够降低 30%。此次实验的成功，证实了空芯光纤可以复用现有的传输设备的情况下，能够形成长距离大容量低时延的传输能力，为算力网的建设储备下关键的技术。
据IT之家此前报道，不久前，《信息通信行业发展“十五五”规划》发布，提出到 2030 年，全面建成覆盖完善、性能领先的新一代通信网，
5G 用户普及率达到 95%、千兆以上宽带用户数达到 3.2 亿户
、智能算力规模达到每秒 9800 百亿亿次浮点运算，为到 2035 年基本实现信息通信行业现代化奠定坚实基础。“十五五”时期，我国将把握新一代通信网络建设的战略机遇，
适度超前、系统推进新一代通信网建设
未来 6G 基站不光能通信还能当雷达，新闻联播报道详解新一代通信网加快建设

title: 又一项重要成果，我国牵头制定脑机接口参考架构国际标准正式发布
content:
感谢IT之家网友
11 月 7 日消息，据央视新闻报道，记者 6 日从国家标准委了解到，一项由我国牵头制定的脑机接口参考架构国际标准近日正式发布，这是我国在脑机接口国际标准化领域取得的又一项重要成果。
报道称，该标准围绕“
脑机接口是什么、怎么用、有什么功能、如何实现
”四个核心问题，系统梳理了典型实现模式，形成包括概念、应用、功能和实现的完整技术框架。
脑机接口参考架构国际标准起草人潘纲介绍，现在大家对脑机接口的定义，也在逐步地发展过程当中，早期脑机接口概念最主要就是意念的读出，现在经过二三十年的发展，它不单是读出，简单地说，其实是一个信号的读出来，去解读它，进而去调控、干预、影响它，这样形成信号的读出和写入的闭环。
IT之家注意到，标准把脑机接口“怎么用”归纳为五类，包括
实时感知人的注意力、疲劳、认知负荷
等脑状态，可用于工业作业等安全预警场景。
对于身体严重损伤或者没有办法交流的患者，通过脑机接口来跟外部机器人包括外控的轮椅实现打字、喝水这些日常的功能。脑机接口还可以与康复机器人等结合开展神经康复训练，促进脊髓损伤、卒中等患者运动功能恢复；通过神经反馈等方式帮助健康人开展注意力调节、认知训练等，提升或拓展原有能力；另外，将脑机接口与眼动、语音、手势、肌电等交互方式结合，还能形成更加准确、灵活的多模态人机交互。
潘纲表示，现在脑机接口技术也到了从技术的突破逐步往产业转换的关键阶段。一个厂家是做不了所有的内容的，不同的部件，包括数据的格式都特别不一样，通过这个标准，让大家尽量能够在这个框架下去形成未来的整个产业体系。
报道提到，我国已牵头发布三项脑机接口领域基础的国际标准，
分别是术语、用例和参考架构
。目前，我国正在牵头制定多项脑机接口国际标准。
据 ISO 官网信息，此次发布的脑机接口参考架构国际标准编号为 ISO / IEC 27572:2026，全称为《信息技术脑机接口参考架构》，于 2026 年 9 月正式出版，共 18 页，由国际标准化组织（ISO）与国际电工委员会（IEC）下设的 ISO / IEC JTC 1/SC 43（脑机接口分委会）负责制定。
ISO / IEC JTC 1/SC 43 于 2022 年 3 月成立，其前身是 JTC 1 第 16 咨询组（AG16），工作范围覆盖信息技术领域的脑机接口标准化，但明确将人体植入物及医疗应用标准排除在外。目前中国是该分委会 13 个参与成员（P 成员）之一。
我国牵头发布的三项脑机接口领域基础国际标准中，术语标准为 ISO / IEC 8663:2025《信息技术脑机接口术语》，由中国医学科学院生物医学工程研究所专家蒲江波担任项目牵头人，我国于 2021 年 3 月提出提案、同年 9 月通过投票立项，先后有美、日、澳等 8 个国家参与，标准共梳理出基本概念、分类、信号、实验、应用等 8 大类 126 个词条；用例标准为 ISO / IEC TR 27599:2025，于 2025 年 5 月发布，共 108 页，收录了医疗健康、工业控制、智能环境等领域的代表性用例。
文章中提到的标准起草人潘纲，是浙江大学教授，任职于浙江大学脑机智能全国重点实验室、计算机学院及良渚实验室，长期从事脑机接口、类脑计算等方向的研究。
在国内层面，与之对应的国家标准为 GB/T 47023-2026《信息技术脑机接口参考架构》，由全国信息技术标准化技术委员会（SAC / TC 28）归口，起草单位包括浙江大学、中国电子技术标准化研究院、南湖脑机交叉研究院、天津大学、华为技术有限公司、电子科技大学、中兴通讯等，该标准于 2026 年 1 月 28 日发布、2026 年 8 月 1 日实施。

title: 我国核技术应用年直接经济产值预计将达 4000 亿元，未来有望形成万亿级市场规模
content:
IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，据新闻联播报道，今年以来，在保障电力供应基础上，我国积极拓展核能供热供汽等多元场景，加快推进核能综合利用。
在江苏连云港，全球首个三代加四代核电技术的徐圩核能综合利用项目正在加快建设。这座核电站不只生产电力，还能大规模制造工业蒸汽，直供连云港石化产业基地。
参考IT之家此前报道，江苏徐圩核能供热发电厂的高温气冷堆“炽龙一号”核岛建设已于 11 月 6 日全面启动，这标志着我国自主四代核电技术迈入规模化商业化落地阶段。它采用球形燃料元件，能耐受 1620 摄氏度高温，即使核电站丧失冷却功能，反应堆也能靠自然散热保持安全。
如今，核能的应用场景正在不断拓展。在大连红沿河核电站，已经开始向周边两万多居民提供清洁供暖。在秦山核电基地，商用反应堆实现镥‑177、钇‑90 等医用同位素规模化生产，这些同位素经过加工制成靶向药物，补齐了我国高端核药自主供给短板。
报道还提到，今年以来，我国核能综合利用效率显著提升，核技术应用年直接经济产值预计将达到 4000 亿元，未来有望形成万亿级市场规模。

title: 我国自主研制新型模块化“移动暖屋”将登陆南极：单个建筑面积 18m²，适应零下 40℃ 低温
content:
11 月 7 日消息，据新华社报道，由中国建筑第八工程局和绿色建筑全国重点实验室共同研发的南极应急宿舍舱，7 日随“雪龙 2”号出征南极。我国南极考察队员今后在野外进行科学考察时，
有望住上这种新型模块化“移动暖屋”
据介绍，“移动暖屋”采用钢结构模块体系，
实现了结构、围护、机电、内装、能源系统全工厂预制
，出厂即成品，运抵南极后即可投入使用；底座采用标准集装箱角件接口，既能装船远洋运输，也能接上雪橇，在冰面雪地上拖行，
科考队员走到哪，“移动暖屋”就能跟到哪
“移动暖屋”还能像搭积木一样，串联、并联拼在一起
，通过内部切换，快速“变身”以适应不同用途。此外，为抵抗南极的极端严寒，“移动暖屋”以方钢为建筑主体，能适应零下 40 摄氏度的低温，配合高保温围护体系与发热地板，可将室内温度稳定维持在 18 至 24 摄氏度的舒适区间。
IT之家注意到，其自主研制的断桥可调节通气阀技术，能在防风雪倒灌、杜绝冷凝水侵入舱内的同时，最大限度降低热传导，
满足极地建筑无动力持续换气与保温的需要
根据规划，在中国第 43 次南极考察中，有 3 个新型模块化“移动暖屋”随“雪龙 2”号登陆南极，
每个模块建筑面积 18 平方米
。温暖、明亮、舒适的居住环境，将使我国南极野外科考保障能力进一步提升。

title: 星眼太空感知星座开启组网验证，重点观测“太空碎片”
content:
感谢IT之家网友
11 月 7 日消息，北京时间今天 7 时 37 分，谷神星二号遥三运载火箭在酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空，将搭载的观澜试验星、云遥一号 28 星、中北大学一号卫星、钧天一号 06A 卫星共 4 颗卫星顺利送入预定轨道，飞行试验任务取得圆满成功。
据央视新闻报道，今天成功入轨的卫星当中，有一颗承担特殊使命的卫星，它和以往对地观测的卫星不同，它的任务是观测太空中运行的航天器，重点是太空碎片，为在轨航天器提供太空交通管理服务。这颗卫星就是星眼太空感知卫星，它拍摄的目标就是在太空中运行的卫星，尤其是太空碎片。
当前低轨 1 厘米到 10 厘米的太空碎片数量已高达百万级
，这类“看不见的威胁”是航天器安全的最大隐患之一。目前，全球近地轨道活跃卫星已超万颗，空间目标数量持续攀升。而地面观测太空目标的方式会受地理、气候约束，存在时空覆盖短板，所以才要发射星眼卫星把摄像机放到天上，实现“在天看天”。
▲ 图源“星图测控”
据悉，该卫星搭载对空天感知的相机，它运行在晨昏轨道上，相机始终顺着太阳光去观测，它通过观测太阳光打在空间碎片上的反光，
来捕捉空间碎片的轨迹
，通过轨迹把空间碎片进行定轨、进行关联，然后进行编目。编目就是把太空中所有的物体编成一个数据库。
IT之家查询获悉，
星眼星座总规划 156 颗卫星
，走试验先行、分步建设路线。先通过星眼 01 星等多颗试验星，在轨考核相机成像、星上算力、智能算法以及整套天地感知系统的可靠性。

title: 最高爬升 1.45 万米高空：ApusNeo 太阳能无人机已翱翔 80 小时，正冲刺 100 小时续航
content:
IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，科技媒体 New Atlas 昨日（11 月 6 日）发布博文，报道称 UAVOS 公司的 ApusNeo 太阳能无人机正在西班牙富埃特文图拉岛开展长航时测试，本轮连续飞行已超过 80 小时，正向 100 小时目标推进。
UAVOS 公司表示，其 ApusNeo 是首架在欧洲空域飞行高度达到 14,500 米（47,600 英尺）的太阳能飞机，该公司希望利用它来监测野火。
IT之家援引博文介绍，ApusNeo 翼展 18 米，起飞重量最高 47 公斤，加强型可搭载约 3.4 公斤任务载荷。其机翼上的太阳能电池板白天为电机供电，同时给电池充电；入夜后，飞机依靠储存的电能继续飞行，形成昼夜能源循环。
此次长航时测试之前，ApusNeo 已验证高空飞行能力。该机于 10 月 16 日从西班牙富埃特文图拉岛的高空平台与无人机技术中心起飞，持续飞行 29 小时，最高升至约 1.45 万米。今年 9 月，该机还曾分别完成 29 小时和 52 小时的不间断飞行，逐步拓展续航能力。
在用途方面，报道介绍，该机搭载由高分辨率相机和红外传感器组成的观测吊舱，可实时向地面传回图像。其中，红外传感器能够探测热源，为早期发现野火、跟踪火势提供支持。UAVOS 希望将其用于森林火情监测，但正式投入任务的时间尚未明确。

title: 调节精度超 99.5％：我国单体最大功率飞轮储能项目正式投运
content:
11 月 7 日消息，据科技日报今日报道，
我国单体最大功率飞轮储能项目昨日在华能兰州热电公司并网运行
，标志着我国在火电基地飞轮储能快速调频技术领域取得重要突破。
据介绍，飞轮储能依靠高速运转的转子实现电能存储。电力充裕时，电能驱动转子高速旋转，将电能转化为转动动能加以储存；电网需要供电时，高速运转的转子再将动能重新转换为电能向外输送。它可快速完成充电、放电，保障电网平稳运行，具备转换效率高、适应性强、设备使用寿命长等优势。
此次并网运行的飞轮储能项目
创新采用“5 兆瓦大功率飞轮 +0.5 兆瓦惯量飞轮”协同模式
。区别于传统单飞轮模式，双飞轮协同运行可实现优势互补、分级响应。
5 兆瓦大飞轮可有效应对电网大频差波动，0.5 兆瓦小飞轮负责稳定日常小幅度的电网频率波动。搭载双飞轮储能的火电机组响应电网调频的时间可小于 100 毫秒，
调节精度超 99.5％
，可在更为复杂情况下有效提升机组调频性能，快速支撑电网频率稳定。
IT之家查询获悉，此次投运的 5 兆瓦飞轮为目前国内单体最大功率飞轮，调节速率可达到 5 兆瓦 / 秒，储电量可达 1250 千瓦时，
充放电效率达 85% 以上
，循环寿命可达千万次。该项目由华能甘肃公司牵头组织，西安热工院负责技术研发。投运后将为西北地区电网安全稳定运行提供技术支撑。

title: GXO’s Strategic Logistics Hub: Growth Across Asia Pacific
content:
GXO’s Strategic Logistics Hub: Growth Across Asia Pacific
Prioritise Us
on Google
GXO is expanding operations with a new APAC hub. Credit: GXO
Scott Copeland, Managing Director, Asia Pacific at GXO explains how the new hub will aid with operational growth and meeting demand
GXO is growing its footprint, gaining a new strategic hub in Malaysia. The APAC region is undergoing rapid transformation in the logistics sector, driven by the adoption of automation, growing consumption and changing supply chains.
Global disruption has demonstrated that logistics needs to change, which has driven organisations across APAC to rethink how networks operate.
Alongside this, organisations are growing their global footprint, understanding that a network needs to be global in order to withstand volatility.
Supply chain resilience
GXO Logistics, the largest pure-play contract logistics provider, has announced the opening of a new logistics hub in Medini, Malaysia. Demonstrative of its commitment to the fast-growing region, GXO is working strategically to grow its standing in the area.
In 2024, APAC led the global logistics market, driven by stronger trade activity and the accelerated adoption of advanced logistics technologies.
This has continued to shift in recent years, driven by various geopolitical disruptions and a growing understanding of the need for diversification. Companies around the world are turning away from a single production area, as well as working hard to break into new markets.
To avoid supply chain risks that are limited to one area, organisations are diversifying production around the world. Alongside this, they are recognising the importance of storing goods closer to the customer.
Businesses are reducing risk by diversifying across Southeast Asia and India, alongside maintaining operational continuity
amid volatility and controlling costs
more effectively.
Asia Pacific continues to be one of the most dynamic growth markets for GXO.
Michael Jacobs, Chief Executive Officer of the Americas and Asia Pacific at GXO
Strategic positioning
Alongside the risk-reduction behind diversification in logistics, it is also a crucial step in ensuring customer satisfaction. The rise of social commerce is increasing the need for
cross-border trade
, with consumers finding more products through social media.
Due to the global reach of these platforms, trade is becoming more global. As a result, there is a core need for a strong, global logistics network.
GXO’s new hub is located in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (SEZ), which has all the benefits of a Free Trade Zone (FTZ), as well as access to one of the region;s most strategically positioned logistics corridors.
It has close connectivity to major manufacturing centres, airports and ports, meaning that companies can optimise their inventory positioning. This results in more resilient supply chains and reduced operating costs.
“Asia Pacific continues to be one of the most dynamic growth markets for GXO,” explains Michael Jacobs, Chief Executive Officer of the Americas and Asia Pacific at GXO.
Michael Jacobs, Chief Executive Officer of the Americas and Asia Pacific at GXO
“The opening of our Medini facility reflects our commitment to bringing world-class logistics solutions to high-growth markets. From its strategic location within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, the site will offer customers greater flexibility, resilience and speed while connecting them with some of the region’s most important manufacturing, technology and trade hubs.”
At a glance
GXO has more than 1,000 warehouse locations
The company has operations in 27 countries
More than 200 million square feet of warehouse space makes up GXO’s operations
30% of Fortune 100 companies are in its customer base
GXO has more than 150K team members
Improving customer service
The new facility is specifically designed to support customers across advanced industrial sectors and technology. It is currently the regional hub for major global supplier or semiconductor manufacturing equipment, meaning the facility is well-designed for critical technology.
GXO is also exploring growth within the site, including capabilities for emerging warehouse technologies. An aim for this is to drive collaboration between GXO and its customers, as well as increased visibility across the supply chain.
“As technology and advanced manufacturing continue to expand in Asia Pacific, companies are increasingly looking for ways to position inventory closer to regional demand,” said Scott Copeland, Managing Director, Asia Pacific at GXO.
Scott Copeland, Managing Director, Asia Pacific at GXO
“With access to Singapore and southern Malaysia’s key ports and manufacturing hubs, our new Medini site gives customers a strategic base to scale efficiently and serve both regional and global markets.”
Key partners
GXO Logistics is the world's largest pure-play contract logistics provider, spun off from XPO Logistics in 2021. title: 'Message to the West': Bomb threats target European flights, newsrooms
content: European newsrooms received chilling bomb threats warning that “the clock is ticking” on Friday, prompting evacuations and broadcast suspensions across the continent. The messages threatened imminent explosions and claimed responsibility for a wider campaign targeting passenger aircraft across Europe.Ireland’s public broadcaster RTÉ evacuated its offices after receiving an email warning that an explosive device would detonate within 45 minutes. Bulgaria’s Nova TV received a similar message, while Britain’s Sky also reported a security threat.No explosives have been discovered at any affected location. Investigators have not established whether the newsroom threats share a source with the growing wave of aviation disruptions.Emails Threaten Imminent ExplosionsThe emails sent to RTÉ and Nova TV carried the subject line “Message to the West.” They were signed by someone identifying himself as Mikhail Andropov, who claimed to lead a group behind the recent aviation threats.One message warned that an operative had planted an explosive device inside a broadcaster’s building. It gave authorities just 45 minutes before the alleged detonation.“But this is only the beginning. What happened this week is just a small part of what awaits Europe in the near future,” the sender wrote.RTÉ suspended programming and evacuated its offices while security teams investigated. Some broadcasts disappeared for as long as three hours, replaced by music and prerecorded announcements.Police inspected Nova TV’s newsroom in Sofia and declared the building safe. Employees subsequently returned to their desks, and the broadcaster maintained its programming.Sky also confirmed receiving a security threat. However, authorities have not disclosed whether its warning contained similar language or originated from the same sender.Aviation Threats Disrupt FlightsThe newsroom warnings followed several days of bomb threats targeting European aviation. The first major wave emerged Tuesday, affecting at least seven flights and a cruise ship.Threats prompted emergency landings, flight diversions and fighter jet escorts across Poland, Bulgaria, Italy and Spain. Another wave struck Thursday, affecting at least 27 flights.Friday brought further disruption across the continent. Prague’s Vaclav Havel Airport reported nine threatened flights, including services connecting Denmark, Spain and Britain.France also reported threats against at least four flights. A Ryanair service scheduled to travel from Lisbon to Rome encountered another alert.At least three aircraft received escorts from Hungarian fighter jets during Friday’s incidents. Every affected aircraft landed safely, and authorities have found no explosives aboard the threatened planes.Investigators probe threat campaignAuthorities have yet to identify the person behind the newsroom emails or establish whether all the threats share a common source. Investigators are examining the messages alongside the wider wave of aviation disruptions.The incidents have exposed how anonymous bomb threats can disrupt critical infrastructure without any confirmed explosives. Each alert forces security teams to investigate potential dangers before normal operations can resume.Aviation security specialist Eric Schouten told Reuters that airline security departments initially assess incoming threats through established procedures. They then alert authorities, who can order flight diversions or deploy fighter aircraft when necessary.Recent cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems have also heightened security concerns across Europe. Investigators have not established any connection between those incidents and the bomb threats.No explosives have been discovered at the affected aircraft or broadcasting facilities. However, the sender’s warning that this is only the beginning has left European authorities facing the possibility of further disruptions.

title: 18-year-old quantum computing conjecture solved in just three days
content: An 18-year-old mathematical problem concerning the limits of quantum computing may finally have been solved in just three days. Physics research company PSI claims to have cracked the long-standing Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, potentially shedding new light on when quantum computers can outperform conventional machines.The company said its system completed the proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture in three days. The problem, first proposed in 2008, concerns the conditions under which quantum computers can achieve an exponential speed advantage over conventional computers.PSI said its research system used a non-public model from Anthropic, running on the company’s own infrastructure. The system produced a mathematical proof that was accepted by Lean, a proof-assistant software used to check the logical correctness of formal mathematical arguments.The company said the system subsequently improved the proof twice, with Lean accepting the final version as well.However, the result has not yet undergone full independent academic review. While researchers at Stanford University have examined aspects of the work and provided feedback, wider scrutiny will be important in establishing whether the proof resolves the original conjecture.A long-standing quantum questionThe Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture addresses how much information a classical computer needs to simulate certain quantum algorithms.More specifically, it concerns whether quantum algorithms with a particular mathematical structure can be efficiently approximated by classical computers. If the conjecture holds, classical computers could simulate a broad class of quantum algorithms on randomly selected inputs with only polynomial overhead. The distinction matters because polynomial and exponential growth can produce vastly different computing demands as the size of a problem increases.That would help explain why some quantum algorithms may not deliver an exponential advantage over classical computing, even if quantum hardware can process information in fundamentally different ways.The result does not mean quantum computers have no advantage over classical machines. Algorithms designed for particular problems, including Shor’s algorithm for factoring large numbers, are not ruled out by the conjecture.Instead, the conjecture addresses a specific class of quantum computations and the conditions under which their apparent advantage can be reproduced classically.Independent scrutiny remainsPSI said David Turturean led the work, developing the research system, defining the problem and running the process. He also reviewed the resulting draft and was responsible for the paper’s correctness.The company said Jim Halverson audited the proof, while Phiala Shanahan provided comments on its Lean formalisation.Researchers at Stanford, including Guy Blanc, Jordan Docter, Carmen Strassle and Li-Yang Tan, have also been examining the result. The group previously proved a special case of the conjecture in August 2026 and is preparing a shorter exposition of PSI’s full proof for other experts.Their involvement is significant because formal verification and independent mathematical review serve different purposes. Lean can check whether a formal proof follows logically from its stated assumptions, but researchers must also assess whether the formalized statement accurately captures the original conjecture.PSI, which launched publicly in September 2026, describes itself as a physics research company building automated systems for scientific discovery. Its announcement marks a potentially important milestone, but the claim will need to withstand broader expert review before it can be treated as a settled result.

title: 3632°F heat turns old wind turbine blades to silicon carbide, graphene
content: Researchers at Tsinghua University have developed an “upcycling” method using flash Joule heating to turn retired wind turbine blades into silicon carbide and graphene. These two are high-value materials used in manufacturing.Giant wind turbine blades are designed to survive the unthinkable. They slice through freezing gales, endure relentless UV radiation, and withstand lightning strikes for over two decades. But that extreme durability turns into an environmental issue when their service life ends. Decommissioned blades mostly end up buried in landfills.China-based team has now unlocked a solution to this long-standing dilemma. The chemical and environmental engineers found a way to transform tough composite waste into high-value manufacturing materials using a brief burst of extreme heat.Researchers prepared resin samples reinforced with silicon carbide and graphene recovered from discarded wind turbine blades for a tensile performance test. Credit: Hao Bi.A thermal miracle in secondsThe wind power surge of the early 2000s has created an urgent disposal crisis today as the first major generation of 20-year turbine blades reaches retirement. Annual decommissioned blade waste across China, Europe, and the U.S. now reaches thousands of tons. Outright landfill bans on composite waste in nations like Germany and Austria make finding scalable alternative processing methods an imperative for the renewable energy sector.“As aging turbines are decommissioned, especially in China, where wind power has expanded rapidly, much of the waste has ended up in landfills. It’s a waste of resources,” said Bing Deng, senior author and chemical and environmental engineer at Tsinghua University, China. The key was found in the raw ingredients already inside every blade. Turbine blades are built from silica-rich fiberglass bound together by carbon-dense resin.In this new work, researchers used flash Joule heating to zap broken blade material to roughly 2,000°C (3,632°F) in a matter of seconds.The intense heat triggers a rapid reaction in which carbon bonds with silica to form silicon carbide, a ultra-hard, heat-tolerant compound. At the same time, the remaining carbon atoms restructure into graphene, one of the strongest and most conductive nanomaterials known to science.Integrating tiny amounts of the recovered silicon carbide and graphene mixture directly into fresh resin boosted performance. A 0.3 percent weight addition strengthens the resin, increasing tensile deformation resistance by 27 percent and flexural strength by 9 percent. Adding a mere 0.1 percent concentration boosts thermal diffusivity by 41 percent, allowing heat to disperse far more efficiently.This upgraded material can be used to construct next-generation wind turbine blades, creating a closed-loop system where old turbines help build stronger new ones.Upcycling with a profit marginExisting recycling methods like pyrolysis and solvent dissolution carry heavy price tags and high carbon footprints. Flash Joule heating could also change the economic model. “With conventional recycling methods, you have to spend money to process the waste. But our method could actually turn a profit of about $80 per ton because the recovered silicon carbide and graphene are valuable,” said lead author and environmental engineer Hao Bi of Tsinghua University. “By comparison, pyrolysis costs about $460 per ton, while chemical dissolution costs about $1,800 per ton.” The team is currently scaling up the process for industrial deployment. Broadening the technology could also help upcycle composite materials from aerospace, automotive, and electronics industries.The team published the findings in the journal Chem Circularity.

title: AQUILA interceptor uses 3-stage design for hypersonic aerial threats
content: At the Euronaval 2026 defense exhibition, European missile consortium MBDA reportedly provided design details for AQUILA. It is an endo-atmospheric interceptor built to dismantle both hypersonic weapons and medium-range ballistic missiles in one fell swoop.The AQUILA interceptor will use a 3-stage architecture comprising a booster accelerator, cruiser, and kill-vehicle to perform long-range, high-altitude engagements against high-velocity maneuvering threats.AQUILA forms the technological core of the European Hypersonic Defense Interceptor Study (HYDIS). The program is locked in a high-stakes competition against the rival HYDEF project to secure the continent’s next-generation shield against emerging aerial threats. “AQUILA is MBDA’s first interceptor concept specifically designed to counter hypersonic threats. It embodies a new generation of endo-atmospheric defense, reinforcing MBDA’s air-defense portfolio and ensuring more durable and effective protection of high-value assets and deployed forces in an increasingly contested environment,” the company noted.AQUILA. CREDIT: MBDAAmbitious AQUILA hypersonic interceptorThe rapid evolution of hypersonic systems over the past decade has created a major strategic challenge. Extreme speeds and unpredictable flight trajectories make maneuvering ballistic missiles, hypersonic cruise missiles, and hypersonic glide vehicles exceptionally difficult to counter. MBDA addressed this gap by investing heavily in research and development to create AQUILA, an advanced endo-atmospheric interceptor for modern atmospheric defense. An endo-atmospheric interceptor is a defense missile built to detect, track, and eliminate airborne threats within Earth’s atmosphere.MBDA officially unveiled the AQUILA concept to the public at the Paris Air Show (Le Bourget) in 2023.What makes AQUILA a standout? It attempts what no current Western defense platform can.Prompted by the combat emergence of maneuvering threats like Russia’s Kinzhal and Zircon missiles, European military planners realized traditional air defenses were falling behind. The Pentagon currently splits this massive operational burden across multiple dedicated platforms. It relies on the SM-3 and THAAD for ballistic missile defense and is developing the Glide Phase Interceptor (GPI) for maneuvering hypersonic glide vehicles.Europe wants a single effector to handle the entire spectrum. To pull off this feat, MBDA finalized a 3-stage, all-rocket configuration.The interceptor features four all-rocket-propelled stages, a design choice settled upon to deliver extreme acceleration. Speed matters. The missile will execute direct “hit-to-kill” engagements across vastly different altitudes. At the edge of the atmosphere, AQUILA will target Intermediate-Range Ballistic Missiles (IRBMs) with ranges up to 3,000 kilometers (1,864 miles). Lower down, it will hunt elusive Hypersonic Glide Vehicles (HGVs) and hypersonic cruise missiles.Stronger air defense for EuropeSize constraints are equally critical.AQUILA is designed for easy naval integration, built to fit standard Mk-41 Vertical Launch Systems (VLS) and upgraded SYLVER naval launchers. Operationally, a battery can protect a 100-kilometer zone using only its organic radar system. Even so, network feeds from space sensors and radar grids will dramatically boost its target acquisition.Engineered for both land and ship platforms, the system complements the proven ASTER missile family, reinforcing integrated air and missile defense architectures to neutralize emerging hypersonic threats.If successful, MBDA’s four-stage bet will streamline Europe’s air defenses.

title: Can Claude dream now? Anthropic explores human-like machine memory
content: Science fiction has long imagined machines that think, learn, and perhaps even dream. Anthropic is now exploring an idea that sounds straight out of that world. Its latest research examines how Claude can revisit past experiences during periods of inactivity, correct faulty memories, and organize what it has learned for future conversations. Anthropic calls this process “dreaming,” although it has little to do with the dreams humans experience.The approach allows Claude to review previous interactions when it has idle time. It can identify incorrect information, refine existing notes, and build structured knowledge that future sessions can access. The process draws inspiration from how human brains consolidate memories during sleep.Anthropic’s research examines several components of this system. Its experiments suggest that selective memory and regular maintenance can improve performance on complex, long-running tasks.Teaching ClaudeClaude can save useful information in memory files while completing tasks. However, deciding what deserves storage presents a challenge. Recording every interaction creates clutter, while overlooking important details can leave future sessions without useful context.Anthropic tested this problem using Pokémon Red, where Claude had to navigate the game’s world and earn badges. The researchers compared two models after approximately 10,000 gameplay steps.Memory is what allows Claude to learn from experience. In a new Engineering Blog post, we share how “dreaming” helps Claude organize what it’s learned, correct its mistakes, and find what it needs more easily the next time. https://t.co/uUEN4bNkr9— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) November 6, 2026Sonnet 3.7 recorded almost everything it encountered. Its memory directory contained 413 files across 225 folders, totaling nearly 978,000 characters. Despite maintaining this enormous record, the model earned just one badge.Claude Fable 5 took a considerably different approach. It maintained only 10 files across three locations, using approximately 43,400 characters. The model earned four badges during its run.The smaller memory system prioritized navigation strategies and lessons learned through gameplay. It also maintained a central file containing its current objectives and planned actions.This approach helped Claude avoid repeatedly processing information that it could already retrieve from the game’s interface. It also preserved useful discoveries that would otherwise disappear between sessions.Dreaming helps correct mistakesMemory files can contain incorrect information, creating problems when future sessions treat those details as established facts. Anthropic demonstrated how dreaming could address this issue through another Pokémon experiment.Claude incorrectly recorded the location of a Pokémon Center near Mt. Moon. The mistake caused it to misunderstand its position after leaving the building. It repeatedly walked over a one-way ledge and returned to an earlier route.An offline review changed the outcome. Claude compared its stored notes against the original session transcript and identified the incorrect location. It then updated the memory file with the correct information.With that correction, Claude re-entered Mt. Moon and eventually reached Cerulean City. The version using incorrect memory repeatedly encountered the same obstacle and never completed the journey.Building knowledge beyond conversationsAnthropic also explored whether dreaming could turn large document collections into interconnected knowledge bases. These systems resemble wikis, with individual pages linking related information.One experiment involved approximately 350,000 internal documents from software company Stainless. The collection contained roughly 420 million tokens.Across 128 sessions, Claude gradually developed and refined a wiki using information from those documents. Its performance on 25 evaluation questions improved from 13 percent to 48 percent.A separate merger-document experiment produced another notable result. Claude answered questions requiring information from multiple documents with 87 percent accuracy using its wiki. Direct document search alone achieved 73 percent.Dreaming can also reorganize information for future sessions. Claude can move frequently needed details into readily available context while keeping less relevant information in searchable files.Anthropic acknowledges that the approach still requires careful management. Memory maintenance consumes computing resources, and excessive information can overwhelm future sessions.The researchers believe agents must learn when to preserve information and when to revisit it. Their experiments suggest that better memory management could help Claude handle increasingly complicated tasks across multiple sessions.

title: Counter-drone air defense system fires 3,000 rounds per minute in trial
content:
Designed to protect military convoys

defensive
positions. The ASGARD program also reflects Slovenia’s broader efforts to strengthen its domestic defense industrial
capabilities
